title: Mazloum Abdi: SDF enters a new phase in the integration of military and administrative institutions
content:
The 100th anniversary of the founding of the city of Qamishlo was celebrated at Azadi Park with the participation of thousands of people, as well as SDF and Autonomous Administration officials and a delegation from the Syrian Transitional Government.


Speaking at the celebrations, Qamishlo Municipality co-mayor Berivan Omer greeted the participants and highlighted the city’s historical importance, its multicultural character and its role in a culture of coexistence.


Qamishlo represents the history and diversity of the region


Speaking afterward, SDF General Commander Mazloum Abdi said that the peoples of the region, with all their different components, had lived together for more than a century. Abdi said the construction of Qamishlo reflected the continuity and diversity of the cultures of the region’s peoples and their coexistence, adding that the city represents the history and all the components of Syrian Jazira.


Abdi said that during the Baath regime, chauvinist policies had been implemented aimed at altering the region’s demographic structure and Arabizing it. He stated that the Autonomous Administration had been struggling against these policies for 15 years and seeking to restore the region’s identity.


The SDF was established through people resistance


Recalling that the region had witnessed a devastating war in recent years, Abdi said the people had defended themselves against attacks and that the SDF had been established during this period of resistance.


Emphasizing that the SDF emerged as a result of the people’s resistance, Abdi commemorated the Kurdish forces and their fighters who fought against attacks on the region. He respectfully commemorated all the fighters who lost their lives while defending the people and saluted the region’s population for its 15 years of resistance.


A new phase has begun


Abdi said that with the fall of the Baath regime, a new phase had begun for the construction of a new Syria, adding that the decision to join the New Syria had been taken on the basis of the 29 January Agreement.


Abdi said that the integration of the military, security and administrative institutions established in recent years into state institutions was being carried out in a way that would preserve their identities and gains. He said: “The phase of integrating the military, security and administrative institutions into the state institutions has come to an end, and a new phase has begun as of today.”


Abdi called on the people of the region to protect and support the institutions built through the sacrifices of the martyrs.


The struggle to ensure constitutional guarantees for rights will continue


Abdi said the struggle to guarantee the rights of the Kurdish people and all components of Syria would continue, adding that political efforts would be intensified at the current stage.


Abdi stressed that the political struggle would continue to ensure that the legitimate rights of the Kurds and all other components are guaranteed in Syria’s new constitution. Saying that Qamishlo could in the future become a center of culture, politics and diversity, Abdi concluded by calling on all the components of the region to work together to build a peaceful future.

author: A.N.A.
title: [Itália] Antiespecismo, veganismo e crise climática
content:
O verão que estamos vivendo está nos mostrando de forma tremendamente tangível o quanto nossas atividades destrutivas estão impactando o clima terrestre. Não há parte do mundo que não esteja sofrendo com desconfortos, ou mesmo verdadeiros desastres, climáticos. Em nosso país, ondas de calor tropical se sucedem, causando cada vez mais incêndios (quando não são criminosos), eventos climáticos extremos e fazendo diminuir assustadoramente o nível da água dos rios e lagos.


Nossa casa comum, a Terra, está doente e o vírus que a infectou somos nós.

 Um conceito mais que banal e totalmente evidente. Apesar de tudo isso, no âmbito antiespecista e vegano, este assunto tão dramaticamente urgente quase nunca é abordado. No entanto, toda vez que uma floresta pega fogo, morrem milhões de Animais, assim como também ocorre com deslizamentos, enxurradas, alagamentos, transbordamentos, longos períodos de seca e tempestades. As zonas climáticas estão mudando rapidamente e isso também significa o desaparecimento de muitas espécies animais que não conseguirão mais se adaptar ao novo clima. Como é que não paramos para refletir sobre tudo isso?


A 

Questão Animal

 diz respeito a todas as áreas da ação humana, a todas as suas implicações e consequências, portanto, também e principalmente, aos desastres climáticos que estamos causando com a poluição, o enorme desperdício de energia, as atividades extrativistas, a poluição, a exploração dos ecossistemas e a antropização e destruição dos habitats naturais. Não considerar tudo isso sob uma ótica antiespecista e vegana, para tentar combater este fenômeno gravíssimo e complexo que produzimos diretamente, é simplesmente uma loucura.


Se a nossa função, enquanto pessoas humanas antiespecistas, é retirar os Animais da exploração humana e, por fim, chegar à tão almejada libertação, não podemos nos eximir de compreender o quanto a crise climática está impactando de forma devastadora a vida dos seres vivos terrestres.


Cada vez mais, a mídia nos mostra imagens de rios secos; toda vez que um rio desaparece, deixando apenas um leito vazio e seco, desaparecem também milhões de Animais, plantas, muitos outros organismos vivos que o habitavam e outros que dependiam de sua presença: quando um rio morre, com ele morre um mundo inteiro, é um grande e vital amigo que se foi. Não podemos ser tão estúpidos e insensíveis a ponto de não compreender isso.


Temos o dever e a urgência de incluir no leque de reflexões e intervenções do nosso ativismo conceitos básicos de ecologia: certamente não aquela especista, antropocêntrica e superficial que nos é empurrada diariamente, mas a 

ecologia profunda

 não antropocêntrica, útil para nos ajudar finalmente a entender o quão frágil e ameaçada está a rede da vida na Terra.


Adriano Fragano

title: 1,500 mink escape from Oregon farm after fence is cut open reportedly by extremist animal rights group
content:
Roughly 1,500 mink escaped an Oregon farm after a hole was cut in a fence — with an extremist animal rights group linking themselves to the plot to free the creatures, according to authorities and reports.

The scores of mink were intentionally let loose from Cascade Farm in Turner late last Wednesday night as the farm’s manager, his wife, children, and other employees were sleeping, KOIN reported.

The suspected intruders cut a hole in a chain-link fence enclosure, allowing the mink to roam free, the local outlet said.

The Animal Liberation Front — a decentralized group of international animal rights advocates labeled as extremists by the FBI — appears to have taken responsibility for the break-in, the outlet reported.

In a press release, the radical group said they have yet to receive an “anonymous communique” officially taking credit for the action.

But Jerry Vlasak, a spokesperson for the North American Animal Liberation Front, told the outlet that the mink escape plot was consistent with their group’s actions and that communiques from activists claiming responsibility are not always sent.

The farm owners have since recovered about 90% of the cute, semiaquatic mammals, the Marion County Sheriff’s Office told the outlet.

“This wasn’t activism. It was a criminal act against a legally operated, certified farm,” Challis Hobbs, Executive Director of Fur Commission USA, an organization that represents mink farmers including Cascade Farm, told the outlet.

“The farm manager and his wife and children live on this property, along with other employees and their families,” he said. “It’s deeply unsettling to have people cut through a fence in the middle of the night with children sleeping just steps away.”

Cascade Farm raises mink legally for pelts and is Humane Care Certified. Any of the mink that aren’t recovered within 24 to 48 hours also face risk of starvation and death, Fur Commission USA added.

The animal activists, however, claimed the mink would be subjected to “egregiously cruel and violent” treatment in captivity.

“The animals liberated last night have a fighting chance at life; they faced a 100 percent death rate if they stayed on the farm,” the Animal Liberation Front wrote in a statement.

The group previously claimed responsibility for cutting open a fence at Olsen Fur Farm in Wisconsin in 2023, allowing about 3,000 mink to escape, CBS reported.

title: Hunting: It’s No Child’s Play
content:
In 2023, the UN released General Comment No. 26. This document updates the famous UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. It explicitly states children must be kept safe from witnessing violence, including physical or psychological harm inflicted on animals. Yet every week across the UK children are taken out to participate in hunting, where they will be exposed to horrific levels of animal cruelty.


A small child is witness to a fox being dug out and thrown to waiting hounds.


On Boxing Day 2020 the Avon Vale Hunt were filmed digging out a fox and throwing her to waiting hounds. Tom Ledbury, the terrierman for this hunt, was sentenced to a 12-month community order for his role in this sickening act. Something equally horrifying is how a small child was present throughout the dig out.


Recent HSA articles have exposed the extent of indoctrination of children into the world of hunting. One of the most recent exposes is the

Stowe Beagles

 recent conviction for killing a hare. Kennel huntsman Philip Kennedy was convicted for the offence but drone footage shows students from Stowe School gloating and celebrating while the hare is mauled by hounds.


Is it part of Stowe Schools curriculum to encourage students to participate in the tearing apart of wildlife?


In November 2025 Lake District Hunt Sabs caught the horrifying moment the

Coniston Foxhounds

 dug out a fox with the use of a terrier, and carried her to waiting hounds. What is apparent from the footage is how co-ordinated the dig out was, a clear indication that this is a regular occurrence. What is also evident are the ages of some of the participants. While older members of the group are participating in the dig out, younger members are watching closely, enthusiastically waiting to get involved, with one of them being handed the terrified fox who he then carries and throws to hounds.


This youth gleefully grabbed the fox by the scruff of her neck and threw her to hounds.


As we know, animal cruelty is just one part of a hunt, there is much more anti-social behaviour and illegal activity that comes with it and this doesn’t stop just because a hunt is professing to have a children’s meet.


In February this year West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs reported of road chaos and violence at a Warwickshire Hunt children’s meet. While hunting in Little Kineton gamekeeper Michael Collins physically assaulted a saboteur. This was followed by hunt master Olivia Forsyth purposely blocking the busy B4455 while she ranted and raved, before eventually being moved on by police.


What a great example to set for children.


It’s not just fox and hare hunting that indoctrinates children; they are exposed to animal cruelty at all blood sports. Just this weekend, at the Dove Valley Mink Hounds, children as young as 11 were present, with one as young as 14 carrying a T-bar and a shovel, ready and waiting to participate in the tormenting of mink and otters.


What a wonderful way to spend the summer holidays, learning how to terrorise and abuse the local wildlife.


As the UN states, children should be kept safe from witnessing all forms of violence, including that inflicted upon animals. What the above examples show are that children are not only witnessing this violence, they are active participants from a very young age, being taught that this is acceptable and being encouraged to be complicit in breaking the law.


The problem is the adults teaching them were subject to the same indoctrination and so a cycle has been formed. A cycle of barbaric violence and law breaking which is dressed up as ‘tradition.’ There are some things that should not be passed onto children and blood sports is one of them.

title: Der Bauernverband gibt der Ernährungsinitiative recht
content:
Am 27. September 2026 können die Stimmberechtigten der Schweiz über die Ernährungsinitiative abstimmen.


Hier meine persönliche Meinung zu dieser Initiative: diese Initiative möchte, dass der Anteil in der Schweiz produzierter und konsumierter pflanzlicher Lebensmittel steigt und schlägt vor, über die Förderung des Anbaus und des Konsums solcher Lebensmittel einen Selbstversorgungsgrad von 70% anzustreben.


Das ist ein sinnvolles Anliegen, das sich für eine ressourceneffizientere und somit nachhaltigere Landwirtschaft einsetzt: aktuell wird in der Schweiz auf Ackerland viel Tierfutter angebaut in Form von Futtermais, Futtergetreide und Futterrüben. Es wäre viel sinnvoller und effizienter auf diesen Flächen stattdessen Lebensmittel für die menschliche Ernährung anzubauen. Erst recht da wir in der Schweiz eine Unterversorgung haben an Getreide und Leguminosen für die menschliche Ernährung und diese im grossen Stil importieren, während bei tierischen Produkten teilweise gar grosse Mengen exportiert werden müssen, weil in der Schweiz die Nachfrage nicht genügt.


Obwohl das Anliegen der Initiative vernünftig und nachhaltig ist, macht die Gegnerschaft schon seit geraumer Zeit mit absurden Parolen wie «Nein zum Veganzwang!» Stimmung gegen diese Initiative. Und sie macht das so erfolgreich, dass inzwischen sogar der Umweltverband Pro Natura, welcher die Initiative anfangs unterstützte, wohl aus Angst vor einem Imageschaden die Nein-Parole beschlossen hat. Ein sehr bemerkenswerter Vorgang bei einem ökologischen Anliegen.


Trotz der reisserischen Parolen lohnt es sich, die Argumente der Gegnerschaft genauer anzuschauen: Unter dem Titel vom «Veganzwang» argumentiert der Bauernverband, dass ein Selbstversorgungsgrad von 70% nur durch eine vegane oder nahezu vegane Ernährung möglich wäre. Ja, richtig gelesen: der Bauernverband sagt, dass durch vegane Ernährung ein höherer Selbstversorgungsgrad möglich wäre. Das ist eine wilde 180°-Wende zu pflanzenbasierter Ernährung: von Verteidiger:innen der Nutztierhaltung hiess es bis anhin fast durchs Band, dass vegane Ernährung in der Schweiz keinen Sinn mache, da aufgrund des Grünlandes in der Schweiz bei einem höheren Anteil pflanzlicher Ernährung der Selbstversorgungsgrad sinken würde. Nun bestätigt also der Bauernverband, dass mit einem höheren Anteil pflanzlicher Lebensmittel ein höherer Selbstversorgungsgrad möglich wäre. Er bestätigt damit auch, dass die aktuelle Schweizer Landwirtschaft in hohem Mass Ressourcenverschwendung betreibt. Und er gibt damit inhaltlich auch der Initiative Recht: mit mehr pflanzlichen Lebensmitteln wäre ein höherer Selbstversorgungsgrad und eine ressourceneffizientere Landwirtschaft möglich.


Das einzige, was der Bauernverband gegen die Initiative sagt, ist also, dass er das nicht möchte. Er möchte lieber die aktuellen verschwenderischen landwirtschaftlichen Förderstrukturen beibehalten, anstatt den Anbau von pflanzlichen Lebensmitteln zu fördern, die nachhaltiger wären und für die es in der Schweiz tatsächlich einen Bedarf und eine Nachfrage gäbe.


Dass der Bauernverband trotz dem offenen Eingestehen, dass ihre Landwirtschaft nicht nachhaltig ist, die Stimmung so prägen kann, dass selbst Pro Natura einknickt, sollte zu denken geben. Und zeigt meiner Meinung nach zwei Dinge: erstens welche Diskursmacht der eng mit den Wirtschaftsverbänden verbundene Bauernverband bei Landwirtschaftsthemen bis weit in linke und ökologische Kreise hinein hat. Und zweitens welch überhöhte, romantisierte und unantastbare Stellung die Tierhaltung und insbesondere die Rinderhaltung in der Schweizer Öffentlichkeit hat.


Darum umso dringender: JA am 27.9.26 zur Ernährungsinitiative!

title: Découverte macabre : 300 cochons morts dans un élevage Eureden
content:
L214 publie des images d'un élevage porcin situé à Hénon et à Saint-Carreuc, dans les Côtes-d'Armor. L'exploitation, liée à la coopérative Eureden et récemment présentée comme un modèle d'avenir pour l'élevage porcin, révèle une situation catastrophique : plus de 300 cadavres de cochons et de porcelets (en décomposition avancée, corps momifiés ou déjà à l’état de squelettes). Un enfer où des cochons vivants se trouvent encore au milieu des morts. Pour L214, il s'agit de l'un des pires cas d'abandon d'animaux documentés par l'association. L'association porte plainte pour mauvais traitements et abandon d'animaux auprès du procureur de la République du tribunal judiciaire de Saint-Brieuc, signale les faits aux services de la préfecture des Côtes-d'Armor et demande au préfet la fermeture immédiate de l'exploitation.

Cette enquête montre 300 cadavres de cochons abandonnés dans les bâtiments d'un élevage situés dans les Côtes-d'Armor (Bretagne). Certains corps sont momifiés, d'autres sont réduits à l'état de squelettes. Des animaux sont morts depuis plusieurs semaines, certains depuis plusieurs mois. Il s'agit de l'un des pires cas d'abandon d'animaux documentés par l'association.

Quelques semaines avant la découverte de ces cadavres, cet élevage faisait l'objet d'une importante communication de la coopérative agro-industrielle Eureden. Le 19 juin 2026, une journée portes ouvertes y a réuni 550 personnes autour d'un des bâtiments, neuf et sans animaux, présenté comme l'avenir de l'élevage porcin, à la pointe de l'innovation et du « bien-être animal ». Derrière ces éléments de langage, les animaux sont pris au piège dans des bâtiment fermés privés de leurs besoins les plus fondamentaux, et laissés sans soin.

Nous demandons à Monsieur le préfet :

la fermeture immédiate de cet élevage ;

la mise à l'abri des animaux encore vivants ;

l'interdiction pour l'exploitant de détenir ou d'exercer une activité auprès d'animaux.

title: ‘They’re still there’: Activists warn of more mink raids after break-in at Oregon farm
content:
PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) — After a late-night break-in last week led to the escape of 1,500 mink from an Oregon farm, some animal rights activists say more intrusions could be on the way.

The Animal Liberation Front, a decentralized group of extremist animal rights advocates known for sabotage, vandalism and even arson, has claimed responsibility in a press release shared on its website for the Aug. 13 break-in at Cascade Farms of Oregon mink farm in Turner, Oregon.

That claim has been unconfirmed by officials. The Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Portland office declined to comment on whether it is investigating the break-in.

The Marion County Sheriff’s Office said there have been no arrests related to the case, and they have no information indicating the ALF’s involvement.

The owner of Cascade Farms of Oregon, Randy Lucas, did not respond to multiple phone calls seeking comment about the break-in. Cascade Farms was established by Lucas’ father, John Lucas, as a meat business and ranch in 1980. The meat business has since closed, and John Lucas passed away, but the ranch remains in business.

But Joseph Buddenberg, a former member of the Animal Liberation Front, said the break-in at Cascade Farm in Turner is consistent with an ALF action. Jerry Vlasak from the North American Animal Liberation press office, which represents the ALF in North America, also said it was consistent with an ALF action but has not received an anonymous communique taking credit for the action. Vlasak also said communiques are often submitted by activists days or even weeks after an event but sometimes aren’t sent at all.

“There have been over 100 fur farm raids in the United States dating back to the 1990s,” Buddenberg said. “Cutting the fences, opening cages, and destroying breeding records have been tactics historically utilized by the ALF.”

Buddenberg pleaded guilty in 2016 to conspiracy to violate the Animal Enterprise Terrorism Act after he and a partner were accused of terrorizing the fur industry during cross-country road trips. He has since completed his sentence and said he hopes speaking out can help people understand why activists go to such extreme lengths.

“Every summer we see activists break in to free mink from farms,” he said. “Every November, they’re pelted.”

Farmed mink are typically bred and raised early in the year until around November, when they’re harvested for their pelts, which are sold for luxury fur apparel and other items. The industry generated $28.1 million in pelts in 2024, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Mink Survey.

Humanely certified operations use carbon monoxide gas, which immediately renders them unconscious and ensures they die quickly and without pain, according to the trade organization Fur Commission USA. The group estimates there are approximately 275 mink farms in 23 states across the U.S., and has said mink that are released often don’t survive.

“If they stayed on the farm, they’d have a 100% death rate,” he said. “Release at least gives them a chance at survival. Fur farmers should definitely expect to see more of this before November.”

Despite his previous felony conviction and time served, Buddenberg remains steadfast in his views.

“Opening cages and freeing these animals is the most compassionate thing you can do,” he said. “My mind hasn’t changed on that at all.”

Oregon’s mink farming industry is a shadow of what it once was. Data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture show Oregon had 37 mink farms in 1978. A decade later, in 1998, that number dropped to 30. By 2006, there were only 18 mink farms in Oregon. Since then, the USDA has stopped including the number of ranches in its reports. Some estimates say Oregon currently has around 11 mink farms. Others, including Buddenberg, estimate there are only about five left in the state, including Cascade.

“Actions like this have a history of closing fur farms,” Buddenberg said. “My hope is that this farm will close. Actions like this are very effective.”

The ALF claimed responsibility for multiple mink farm break-ins in Oregon in 2008, according to several reports published in the Oregonian and the Daily Astorian. They included a break-in at Jefferson Mink Farm in Jefferson, a break-in at S&N Fur Farm in Scio, and a break-in at Ylipelto’s Fur Farm in Astoria. In all three cases, fencing around the farm was cut, and the mink were released into the wild.

author: PETA-Team
title: Hayden Panettiere: Letzte PETA-Kampagne gegen Delfinarien
content:
Nur wenige Wochen vor ihrem Tod setzte sich Schauspielerin Hayden Panettiere gemeinsam mit PETA USA im Rahmen einer eindringlichen Kampagne gegen 

Delfinarien

 und 

Meeresparks

 wie SeaWorld ein. Für das Motiv legte sie sich in eine Badewanne, um auf Platzmangel aufmerksam zu machen, unter dem Delfine in Gefangenschaft leiden. 


PETA USA veröffentlicht die Kampagne im August 2026 in Erinnerung an Panettiere und ihren langjährigen Einsatz für Meeressäuger. Ihre zentrale Botschaft: Menschen sollten keine Tickets für Einrichtungen kaufen, die 

Delfine

 in kleinen Becken gefangen halten und zu touristischen Attraktionen degradieren. 


Hayden Panettiere zeigt, wie wenig Platz Delfine in Gefangenschaft haben 


In dem Kampagnenvideo verdeutlicht Panettiere, was Delfinen in Gefangenschaft genommen wird:  


In ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum können sie mit ihren Familien zusammenleben, große Distanzen zurücklegen, tief tauchen und sich frei im Meer bewegen. 


In Delfinarien dagegen sind die Tiere auf kleine Becken oder flache Lagunen beschränkt. 


Nicht nur in den USA werden Hunderte Delfine in solchen Anlagen gehalten. Dort werden sie beispielsweise gezwungen, 

„Kunststücke“ vorzuführen

 oder werden für 

touristische Begegnungen

 missbraucht, bei denen fremde Menschen sie immer wieder anfassen. Die Delfine haben dabei keine Möglichkeit, sich zurückzuziehen. 


Viele der heute in Gefangenschaft lebenden Delfine wurden vor Jahrzehnten aus dem Meer entrissen und von ihren Familien getrennt. Andere wurden bereits in Gefangenschaft geboren und konnten nie frei im offenen Ozean schwimmen. 


Panettiere macht in dem Video deutlich, welche Folgen diese Gefangenschaft für die Tiere haben kann, und fordert die Öffentlichkeit dazu auf, keine Meeresparks mit Delfinhaltung zu besuchen. 


Vow today to never go to a marine park that keeps dolphins in extreme captivity. Together, we can end this cruelty.

Hayden Panettiere


Sie ruft dazu auf, keine Meeresparks zu besuchen, die Delfine unter solch grausamen Bedingungen gefangen halten, und diese Tierquälerei gemeinsam zu beenden. 


Hayden Panettieres langjähriger Einsatz für Delfine 


Die Kampagne war nicht Panettieres erster Einsatz für Delfine und andere Meeressäuger. Bereits 2007 paddelte die damals 18-Jährige vor 

Taiji in Japan

 ins Wasser und stellte sich Delfinjäger:innen entgegen. Die Ereignisse rund um die dortige Delfinjagd wurden später auch im Oscar-prämierten Dokumentarfilm 

The Cove

 thematisiert. 


2015 unterstützte Panettiere zudem eine juristische Stellungnahme gegen die geplante Einfuhr von 18 wild gefangenen Belugas aus Russland durch das Georgia Aquarium. 


2019 appellierte sie an den russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin, fast 100 Belugas und 

Orcas

 freizulassen, die für die Haltung in Meeresparks vorgesehen waren. Die Tiere wurden anschließend ins Meer zurückgebracht; Russland untersagte im selben Jahr ihre entsprechende Gefangennahme. 


Auch für andere Tiere setzte sich Panettiere ein 


Panettieres Engagement beschränkte sich nicht auf Meeressäuger. Während der Dreharbeiten zur Serie 

Heroes

 ließ sie beispielsweise die Arbeiten unterbrechen, um Vögel zu schützen, die von einem Crewmitglied mit einem Laubbläser vertrieben wurden. 


Gemeinsam mit unseren internationalen Partnerorganisationen erinnern wir von PETA Deutschland durch die Veröffentlichung ihrer letzten Kampagne an Panettieres langjährigen Einsatz für Tiere. Hayden Panettiere starb wenige Wochen

 

nach den Aufnahmen für die Kampagne. Sie richtete sich dabei an alle Menschen, die Delfine schützen möchten: Unterstützen Sie keine Einrichtungen, die die Tiere zu 

Unterhaltungszwecken

 gefangen halten.

title: COVERDALE SHOOT STOPPED BY SABS ON THE INGLORIOUS TWELFTH
content:
The HSA has continually

shared footage and information

 exposing the destruction and cruelty caused by the shooting industry. The extent of the persecution knows no bounds with badgers, foxes, corvids and all manner of wildlife being killed as the land is stripped of any natural balance just to appease those in tweed.


Snare found on the Walshaw Estate, West Yorkshire, January 2024.


So, as is customary, on the 12th of August, coined the ‘glorious twelfth’ by shooters, sabs joined forces to stop them and save lives.


Upon entering the Yorkshire Dales, it quickly became apparent that North Yorkshire police were ready and waiting to try and delay and prevent sabs from achieving their mission. Sab vehicles were pulled over, and dispersal orders were quickly scribbled out, but sabs are not easily deterred and great teamwork and communication meant that some groups made it onto the moors where they prevented the Coverdale shoot from a day’s killing.


North Yorkshire police enabling the slaughtering of Grouse.


In frustration their main transport vehicle drove at sabs while the police were present, drawing attention to the fact that their vehicle had no tax, leaving the tweed clad sour faces to walk to a nearby farm to await collection.


Sabs congregated on the moors to prevent the Coverdale shoot from a day’s killing.

© Newcastle Hunt Sabs


As well as witnessing the sheer lengths the police will go to to protect this blood sport it was also glaringly apparent the extent of damage being done to the moors for this high money business.


The entire ecology of the moors has been altered to accommodate this industry with desolate and barren views stretching far and wide and with the UK reaching record high temperatures over the past few years, wildfires are becoming more common as the intensive management of grouse moors creates the perfect conditions for it to spread.


Shoots burn heather on the moors resulting in a reduction in biodiversity and the release of stored carbon dioxide.


Without a doubt shooting isn’t just a blood sport, it is extremely detrimental to the environment, and the HSA will continue to expose it.

title: 1500 Captive Mink Liberated Last Night From Oregon Fur Farm (USA)
content:
Although an anonymous communique has yet to be received by the North American Animal Liberation Press Office, activists appear to have liberated 1500 captive mink from Cascade Fur Farm at 7582 Hunsaker Road SE in Turner, Oregon early this morning, according to local news media. The perimeter fence was cut allowing the genetically wild animals access to freedom, whereas they would have all been killed by the owners, John, Donna and Randy Lucas, sometime in November or December.

Reading from their usual playbook, industry spokesman Challis Hobbs recited the dis-proven propaganda about the animals being unable to survive in the wild, dying from thirst, starvation or being run over by cars, and that most of the animals returned to the farm voluntarily to await execution. In reality, its has been shown in scientific studies that farmed mink remain genetically wild and routinely survive long-term after release. They are also indigenous to the area, and while there may be environmental impacts, their chance of survival is quite good.

Mink are genetically wild animals that roam up to 5 miles a day but are kept in 10-inch cages on fur farms; their treatment is egregiously cruel and violent. The mink are born in February or March and are killed by gassing, clubbing or anal electrocution in November, before being skinned, sometimes while still alive, for their fur. The animals liberated last night have a fighting chance at life; they faced a 100 percent death rate if they stayed on the farm.

The number of fur farms in America has dwindled from more than 300 in the 1990s to less than 50 today, as the fur industry continues its steady decline into oblivion. A listing of all known fur farms in North America, is available here: https://finalnail.com/

author: PETA-Team
title: Naturwildpark Granat: Luchs entflohen und erschossen | Update
content:
Update vom 10. August 2026 


Luchs entflieht aus dem Naturwildpark und wird von Jäger erschossen  


Nachdem Luchs Mikaesch Ende Juli 2026 aus seinem Gehege im Naturwildpark Granat entkommen war, wurde er am 8. August, rund zwei Wochen später, von einem Jäger getötet. Berichten zufolge soll der Luchs den Hund eines Spaziergängers bedroht haben. Luchse gelten jedoch als sehr scheu und meiden Menschen in der Regel. Wie Mikaesch aus seinem Gehege fliehen konnte, bleibt bislang unklar.  


Der Vorfall wirft erneut Fragen zur Haltung von Tieren im Naturwildpark Granat auf. Erst im März 2026 haben wir von PETA Deutschland Strafanzeige gegen den Betreiber wegen des Verdachts auf Vernachlässigung einiger Tiere erstattet. Die Haltung von Luchsen und anderen Tieren in Zoos und Wildparks muss endlich beendet werden.  


„Erst eingesperrt, dann ausgebrochen und schließlich erschossen: Mikaesch hat die Sehnsucht nach Freiheit mit dem Leben bezahlt. Immer wieder kommt es in Zoos zu Unfällen und Ausbrüchen, die für die Tiere tödlich enden können und auch Menschen und andere Tiere in Gefahr bringen. Kein noch so großes Gehege kann den natürlichen Bedürfnissen von Wildtieren gerecht werden. Wer verhindern will, dass die Gefangenschaft für weitere Tiere tödlich endet, muss aufhören, fühlende Lebewesen für die Schaulust von Menschen auszustellen.“ 

Dr. Yvonne Würz, Biologin und Fachreferentin bei PETA Deutschland  


Update vom 20. März 2026

 


Aktuelle Fotos deuten erneut auf Vernachlässigung hin 


Ende Februar 2026 erreichte uns bei PETA Deutschland eine Whistleblower-Meldung mit aktuellen Fotos, die ein Mufflon im Naturwildpark Granat mit überlang gewachsenen, sogenannten Schnabelhufen zeigen. Aufgrund von Fehlstellungen kann dies mit erheblichen Schmerzen für das Tier verbunden sein. Wir haben das Kreisveterinäramt Recklinghausen darüber verständigt und aufgefordert, die Tierhaltung umfassend zu überprüfen.  


Bereits im Herbst 2025 wurde uns und der Veterinärbehörde durch einen Augenzeugen von einer ähnlichen Beobachtung berichtet. Wenn Tiere möglicherweise über Monate hinweg mit schmerzhaft überlangen Hufen leben müssen, ist das ein klares Zeichen für Vernachlässigung. Daher werden wir nun erneut Strafanzeige gegen die Wildpark-Verantwortlichen erstatten.  


PETA hatte ähnliche Missstände bereits 2022 nach mehreren Meldungen von Augenzeug:innen beim zuständigen Veterinäramt im Kreis Recklinghausen angezeigt und Strafanzeige erstattet. Damals stellte die Staatsanwaltschaft Essen das Verfahren ein, nachdem die Behörde keine Verstöße festgestellt hatte.  


Update vom März 2023:

 

Trotz Augenzeugenberichten: Staatsanwaltschaft Essen stellt Verfahren gegen Betreiber des Parks ein 

 


Im Jahr 2022 hatten wir nach einer Augenzeugenmeldung Strafanzeige gegen den Betreiber des Naturwildparks Granat erstattet. Damals berichteten Besucher:innen von verschiedenen Missständen in der Haltung der Tiere, darunter ein humpelndes Schwein im 

Streichelzoobereich

. Fotos dokumentierten ein Mufflon mit stark deformierten Hufen. Das Bildmaterial legte unserer Einschätzung nach nahe, dass die Erkrankung des Tieres bereits mehrere Monate unbehandelt blieb. Laut Augenzeug:innen konnte das Mufflon kaum noch laufen.  


Nach der medialen Berichterstattung über die von uns erstattete Strafanzeige wandten sich drei weitere Augenzeug:innen an uns und berichteten ebenfalls von verschiedenen tierquälerischen Missständen. Dennoch stellte die Staatsanwaltschaft Essen das Verfahren im März 2023 ein. Der Betreiber des Wildparks gab an, dass ein regelmäßiger Hufschnitt in Freigehegen normalerweise nicht erforderlich sei, da sich die Hufe durch natürliche Bewegung abnutzen würden. Das betroffene Tier habe erst mit zeitlicher Verzögerung eingefangen werden können, um einen Hufschnitt durchzuführen.  


Wir kürten das Kreisveterinäramt Recklinghausen im Jahr 2022 als 

eine der fünf schlechtesten Veterinärbehörden Deutschlands

, weil dieses nach Ansicht von PETA nicht konsequent gegen die Missstände vorging. 


Schnabelhufe und deren körperlichen Folgen 


Bei der sogenannten Hufrehe, einer schmerzhaften Entzündung der Huflederhaut, können im chronischen Stadium sogenannte Schnabelhufe auftreten. Damit es nicht zu dieser krankhaften Veränderung kommt, müssen Tierhaltende regelmäßig die Klauen kontrollieren, kürzen und pflegen. Tiere, die lahmen, müssen tiermedizinisch versorgt werden. Bleibt diese Versorgung aus, ist das tierschutzwidrig.

title: Boldaş: Nature is being plundered in the name of investment
content:
Mining, hydropower and geothermal energy projects are increasingly encroaching on ecosystems and the livelihoods of the people in the Kurdish province of Bingöl. Water resources, forests, pastures and agricultural land are being opened up for industrial projects, while traditional forms of farming and livestock breeding that have developed over generations are coming under increasing pressure, particularly in rural villages.


Canfidal Boldaş, an environmental engineer and secretary of the Provincial Coordination Council of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) in Bingöl, does not view these developments as a series of unrelated individual projects. According to Boldaş, mining operations as well as hydroelectric, solar, wind and geothermal power plants are all part of a policy that subordinates nature and living environments to economic interests.


“A policy of ecocide”


“All of these activities are part of a policy of ecocide,” Boldaş told ANF. He said that the impact on nature and the local population is largely disregarded during the planning process. The projects, he said, primarily serve to generate profits for domestic and foreign companies, as well as joint ventures with close ties to the ruling system.


According to Boldaş, these projects are accompanied by developments such as deforestation and depopulation. Particularly in a region rich in both surface and underground resources, he said, these processes cannot be viewed separately from one another.


Traditional livelihoods are disappearing


Bingöl has historically been shaped by agriculture and livestock farming. According to Boldaş, this economic system and way of life are becoming increasingly restricted by the expansion of industrial projects.


“Pastures, forests, meadows, fields, agricultural land and ecologically valuable areas within the population’s living environment are being destroyed.”


As a result, the conditions necessary to sustain traditional forms of production are gradually disappearing. In many areas, agriculture and livestock farming are coming to a halt, Boldaş said. According to him, the ecological issue is therefore directly linked to the social future of the region.


When pastures, water resources, soil and forests are destroyed, he argued, the issue goes beyond the loss of natural areas. “At the same time, people are being deprived of the material basis that enables them to continue living in their villages.”


Corporate profits prioritized over livelihoods


Boldaş criticized current policies for prioritizing the economic interests of companies over the living conditions of the population. “When people’s living environments are sacrificed to industrialism and their means of subsistence are destroyed, the entire ecosystem of life also collapses.”


According to Boldaş, the depopulation of the region is itself part of what he describes as a policy of ecocide. Given the region’s wealth of natural resources, the displacement of the population facilitates both their economic exploitation and security-related interventions.


He argued that attempts to justify these interventions through supposedly ecological concepts within the existing economic system cannot obscure this connection.


“They call it investment, we see destruction”


Boldaş was particularly critical of the language used to legitimize mining and energy projects: “They call it investment; we see destruction. They call it production; we see plunder. They call it development; we see devastation.”


“When villages and entire districts are handed over to corporate interests in this way, people’s livelihoods are increasingly eroded. Living environments become uninhabitable, and in the end, many people are left with no option but to migrate.”


For those affected, this often means being forced to leave the places where they were born and raised. They are pushed toward cities or regions with which they often have no connection and where their economic future remains uncertain.


Resistance against the destruction of living environments


At the same time, Boldaş sees growing resistance to these interventions. Wherever living environments are under threat, people are making their opposition visible, often together with environmental organizations and other civil society groups. However, these protests have received little meaningful response from state institutions.


“I cannot say that there is a public administration that responds positively …

author: Jian Zharese Joies Sanz
title: Pangasinan green group opposes Marcos Jr.’s pro-nuclear stance
content:
MANILA — Will nuclear energy production help in energy security?

For region-based environmental organization Pangasinan People’s Strike for the Environment (PPSE), it will not.

Last July 27, in his fifth state of the nation address, Ferdinand Marcos Jr pushed for nuclear energy production “to reinforce the country’s energy security and to reduce rising cost of energy.”

“For our environmental defenders in Pangasinan, this is a fake and destructive energy project because its purpose is not to provide an electricity supply to the households and communities in our province,” PPSE stressed in a statement.

Proposed by Pangasinan 2nd District Representative Mark Cojuangco, the planned P225 billion ($3.88 billion) Labrador Nuclear Power Plant is an initial 1,000-megawatt facility to be built on a 120-hectare site.

While Cojuangco claimed that nuclear development could make Labrador the richest municipality in Pangasinan, PPSE stressed that these promises are detached from ground reality as communities are already hit hard by rising fuel prices, declining fish stocks, and high power bills—proving that mega-power projects is not a grounded solution.

“Development is not measured by how many buildings you can erect, but by whether the people have food to eat,” said Pax Guinto (real name withheld for security reasons) of PPSE.

The PPSE member noted that nuclear waste buried underground threatens severe soil degradation and will put communities at risk.

Pangasinan, long known as a coastal stronghold in Northern Luzon, derives its very name and identity from the sea. From the sprawling salt beds along its coasts to the world-renowned bangus (milkfish), the province’s rich marine ecosystems serve as a vital lifeline for millions.

In an interview with Bulatlat, Guinto of PPSE shared the importance of the “Atin ang Lingayen Gulf” (Lingayen Gulf is ours) campaign, which includes their strong opposition to the planned Labrador Nuclear Plant in Pangasinan.

According to Guinto, over 550,000 fisherfolk and more than a million residents depend directly and indirectly on the municipalities within Lingayen Gulf like Anda, Bolinao, Alaminos, Labrador, Lingayen, Binmaley, and Dagupan, for their survival. This includes small-scale fishers who find themselves increasingly squeezed out by skyrocketing fuel prices, ecological degradation, and repressive policies.

“We are launching the campaign, firstly to fight for the ocean, which is the source of livelihood of locals, and the ecological integrity of the sea.”

Lingayen Gulf is considered an Environmentally Critical Area under proclamation no. 156, meaning that the Gulf and its surrounding coastal zones are recognized as ecologically sensitive areas subject to strict environmental regulations.

Under the campaign, PPSE firmly opposes the proposed Labrador Nuclear Power Plant and planned Waste-to-Energy (WTE) incineration projects, while advocating for the livelihood of fisherfolk communities and protection of the environment. The group also demands an immediate halt to offshore black sand and magnetite mining operations such as those linked to Iron Ore Gold Vanadium Resources Inc. covering over 9,000 hectares across 26 coastal barangays in the municipal waters.

In a press release, PPSE also expounded the geopolitical reality behind the push for the power plant despite Pangasinan being a highly susceptible location. “The presence of a nuclear power plant transforms Pangasinan into a highly strategic vulnerability. In the context of modern military strategy, critical energy infrastructure serves a direct geopolitical purpose.”

The green group linked it to Pax Silica, stressing that as the U.S. seeks to secure absolute control over critical earth minerals for foreign profit, the proposed Labrador Nuclear Power Plant (LNPP) functions as a strategic asset to secure and power these foreign-dominated industrial supply chains.

The group further emphasized that the projects under the U.S.–Philippines 123 Agreement Framework and Nuclear Energy Road Map won’t truly benefit communities and are destructive to the environment.

The government’s Nuclear Energy Roadmap sets the national target of integrating nuclear power into the country’s energy grid by 2032. It is based on the U.S.–Philippines 123 Agreement, which provides the legal framework for foreign corporations to sell nuclear hardware, technical expertise, and Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) into the Philippines. author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: 3 anti-mining Nueva Vizcaya residents released on bail, groups decry harassment
content:
Police at the community barricade in Kasibu. Photo courtesy of Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano para sa Kalikasan (ANVIK).

MANILA – Environmental groups condemned the harassment against the people of Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya who continue to defend their land against mining exploitation of the North Luzon Mineral Resources Center (NLMRC).

This is after the recent arrest of three anti-mining advocates in Barangay Pacquet, Nueva Vizcaya. According to Save Cagayan Valley, the three advocates were later released on the same day after posting bail for grave coercion and violation of the Article 151 of the Revised Penal Code.

The three are members of the local organization, Kasibu Inter-Tribal Response for Ecological Development or KIRED.

Earlier, the Center for Environmental Concerns (CEC)’s posted an alert that around 33 to 40 members of Philippine National Police (PNP) arrived early morning today, August 19, to escort seven drums of oil for a supposed government road project of Barangay Pao which would use NLMRC’s backhoe for the project.

But the members of the community are skeptical due to the project’s link to NLRMC. Those who were at the barricade checked the delivery and found out that only five out of seven barrels are officially approved.

The community insisted on blocking the two unofficial drums of crude oil which led to the tension between the members of the community and the PNP. Three community members were arrested namely Lei Jin Dugay, Don Dugay, and June Fiataccag.

Lei Jin Dugay is also facing charges of cyber libel filed by NLMRC due to her post on her social media account expressing her opposition to their mining activities. The residents’ lawyers have also been slapped with cyber libel.

Read: Environment groups alarmed over cyberlibel raps vs anti-mining advocates

Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment (KPNE) stated that the community barricade has been maintained to limit the entry of resources of NLMRC’s equipment to conduct their mining activities within the area.

“The arrest of barricaders is a blatant act of harassment and intimidation against communities defending their land, environment, and livelihoods. Instead of addressing the community’s legitimate concerns, state forces have once again been deployed against environmental defenders,” KPNE stated.

After the arrest around 4:20 pm, PNP continued to escort the entry of crude oil into the area.

KATRIBU Kalipunan ng Katutubong Mamamayan ng Pilipinas said in a statement that this action only proved that the government prioritizes profit over the rights and safety of its constituents. The group asserted that the community has the right to peaceful assembly and expression, especially when they are protecting their livelihood and the environment, especially when there are decisions they are not well informed about.

“The arrest of community and environmental defenders cannot be the government’s response to legitimate concerns over destructive mining and the protection of Indigenous lands and livelihood,” Katribu said in a statement.

The police began staying at the community barricade on August 5 and ordered residents to remove the barricade. However, the community insisted that the land where the barricade was built is privately owned.

The Alyansa ng Novo Vizcayano para sa Kalikasan (ANVIK) has earlier stated that the harassment, threat and intimidation they are facing are due to their opposition to the large-scale mining.

The community strongly opposes NLMRC’s mining activities due to lack of genuine consultation as well as threats of losing their livelihood.

The Mines and Geoscience Bureau granted 4,456 hectares of mining exploration permit to NLMRC in June 2025 yet the community came to know about it in October 2025.

The barricade was set up by the community members in Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya to protect their land from threats of large-scale mining. The areas to be affected by the mining exploration are their ancestral land which is covered by Certificate on Ancestral Domain Title of National Commission of Indigenous People.

Read: Indigenous community rising up against mining in Nueva Vizcaya

The groups reiterated their call to stop judicial harassment against anti-mining leaders and their lawyers, saying it is a “longstanding pattern of deliberate attempts from the collusion of state and private actors to stamp out local dissent.” (AMU, RVO)

author: anred
title: Jujuy: revocaron el sobreseimiento de integrantes de la Comunidad Indígena Las Capillas
content:
Imagen: Infoterritorial


Lo hizo la Sala Penal de la Suprema Corte de Justicia provincial en relación a comuneros y comuneras de Las Capillas, que pertenece al Pueblo Ocloya, y dispuso además retrotraer la causa iniciada a partir de una denuncia por presunta usurpación, realizada por la empresa minera Piuquenes. El conflicto comenzó en 2016 cuando la minera pretendía utilizar el territorio que habita la Comunidad de Las Capillas. En este marco, Piuquenes los denunció por usurpación en 2019 por una protesta que realizaron ante el cierre del camino ancestral con un candado.

Por Red Eco Alternativo.


En 2022 nuevamente se cerró el paso a la comunidad y ante la protesta pacífica de la Comunidad se llevó adelante un operativo policial de desalojo, con más de 100 agentes y sin orden judicial. Incluso detuvieron a varios integrantes de la comunidad acusándolos de “entorpecimiento de libre circulación” y “turbación de la posesión”.


En 2025, el juez Martín de Athayde Moncorvo dictó el sobreseimiento de la comunidad al considerar que se había extinguido la acción penal de la prescripción, un fallo que luego fue ratificado por el Tribunal de Revisión.


Sin embargo, ahora los jueces Martín Francisco Llamas, Emma María Mercedes Arias y Federico Francisco Otaola, integrantes de la Corte Suprema de Jujuy, revocaron ese sobreseimiento.


Compartimos el comunicado de la Asamblea Permanente por los Derechos Humanos (APDH) en rechazo a esta decisión judicial:


La APDH expresa su profunda preocupación ante la decisión de la Sala Penal de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de Jujuy que revocó el sobreseimiento de integrantes de la Comunidad Indígena Las Capillas, perteneciente al Pueblo Ocloya, y dispuso retrotraer la causa iniciada a partir de una denuncia por presunta usurpación.


La APDH advierte según los testimonios y la información pública de los hechos, que la decisión judicial se produce en el marco de un conflicto territorial que involucra a la comunidad preexistente de “Las Capillas” con sectores empresariales mineros y problemáticas ambientales. Teniendo dicha comunidad personería jurídica y documentación estatal que reconoce su posesión y ocupación tradicional, actual y pública del territorio comunitario.


La APDH advierte también que cualquier decisión que pueda afectar el desplazamiento de integrantes de la comunidad debe ser analizada en el contexto de las garantías constitucionales e internacionales asumidas por el Estado Argentino (art. 75 inc. 17 de la Constitución Nacional, el Convenio 169 de la OIT, la Declaración de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de los Pueblos Indígenas y la Declaración Americana sobre los Derechos de los Pueblos Indígenas).


La APDH observa con preocupación que una disputa judicial vinculada con la posesión ancestral de un territorio indígena pueda ser abordada exclusivamente desde la perspectiva penal, sin garantizar una adecuada consideración de los derechos territoriales colectivos y de las obligaciones estatales de protección de las comunidades indígenas.


Por ello, la APDH exhorta a las autoridades judiciales y provinciales de Jujuy a garantizar el debido proceso, la tutela judicial efectiva y los derechos territoriales de la Comunidad Las Capillas, evitando cualquier medida que pueda traducirse en un despojo o desplazamiento de sus integrantes violando la normativa constitucional protectoria de las comunidades indígenas.


La APDH exige el cumplimiento del Estado argentino de tutelar y proteger los territorios de los pueblos indígenas y garantizar que ningún conflicto territorial derive en la criminalización de quienes ejercen derechos reconocidos por la Constitución y los tratados internacionales de derechos humanos.


La APDH exhorta al cumplimiento de el Acuerdo de Escazú y las leyes ambientales vigentes para la evaluación de presuntos impactos ambientales en territorio comunitario y el cumplimiento de los derechos de participación y consulta de la comunidad.


La APDH expresa su solidaridad y acompaña a la Comunidad Indígena Las Capillas en su defensa del territorio comunitario y reclama que toda actuación estatal respete plenamente sus derechos colectivos, su identidad cultural y su posesión ancestral.

title: US Army Corps Pushes Michigan Pipeline Project Ahead Over Indigenous Opposition
content:
The project, which tribes say violates treaty rights, has been the subject of heated controversy and legal battles.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers issued a key permit for a plan to update an aging segment of the Line 5 pipeline crossing the Straits of Mackinac in Michigan, the waterways that tribal nations say are central to their ways of life.

It’s a procedural win for Line 5 owner Enbridge Energy, but comes amid ongoing legal and regulatory hurdles at the state level that prevent the start of construction. The pipeline carries oil and natural gas liquids 645 miles from Superior, Wisconsin, through Michigan to Sarnia, Ontario, and Enbridge wants to replace a 4-mile segment that lays on the bottom of the ecologically sensitive straits with a new one, buried in a tunnel under the lakebed.

In a statement issued with the decision, the Army Corps said the project wasn’t contrary to the public interest, complied with Clean Water Act guidelines, and “would not abrogate or impermissibly impair tribal treaty rights.” Review of the permit was fast-tracked under President Donald Trump’s executive order last year declaring a “national energy emergency.”

For Michigan tribes that have fought for years to shut down the pipeline, the federal permit approval was “disrespectful and ludicrous,” said Austin Lowes, chairman of the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians.

“They’re acutely aware of the impact that this project will have on Indian Country, and they just flat-out ignored it,” Lowes said. “It’s one of the most disgusting things that I’ve ever been confronted with as a tribal leader.”

According to the Army Corps itself, tunnel construction would have permanent adverse impacts on wetlands, vegetation, land use, and cultural resources. The straits are sacred to Anishaabe peoples — the waters feature prominently in their creation story and serve as burial grounds for ancestors. Five tribal nations also hold treaty rights to fish and hunt in these waters, rights that predate Michigan’s statehood and are protected by federal law under the 1836 Treaty of Washington.

“Us surrendering and ceding that land came with certain expectations and rights,” Lowes said. “And one of those expectations was that we would be consulted any time decisions were going to be made on the federal level that would impact our way of life, and the tunnel project certainly does that.”

The agency determined that despite any negative impacts on surrounding lands and property, the proposed tunnel would reduce the environmental risks associated with the pipeline, such as leaks caused by a direct hit from a boat’s anchor. “The benefits of the project outweigh its detriments,” the Army Corps stated. Its scope of analysis was focused on the construction impacts, and not the risk of an oil spill or greenhouse gas emissions beyond the tunnel site, which the agency said is the responsibility of the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration.

Last year, seven Michigan tribal nations withdrew from discussion with the Army Corps over the permit, saying that regulators ignored tribal expertise, input, and concerns, and undermined treaty rights. The withdrawal also came after the Army Corps suggested that the review process would likely be fast-tracked under President Trump’s emergency executive order.

“A project that’s going to take somewhere between six and 10 years to build is certainly not a response to a national energy emergency, and it won’t change the amount of fossil fuels transported,” said Debbie Chizewar, managing attorney at Earthjustice, a legal nonprofit supporting Michigan tribes in litigation against Enbridge.

The Army Corps’ “flawed” review likely has wider impacts for all tribal nations, said David Gover, who is Pawnee and Choctaw and a managing attorney at the Native American Rights Fund, which is supporting Earthjustice.

“This notion that, ‘Yeah, we understand that this will permanently destroy your resting relatives, but we don’t care, and we got to move ahead. We got to have these fossil fuels’ — that challenges tribal sovereignty,” Gover said.

Enbridge spokesperson Ryan Duffy said in a statement that the permit approval is “a significant step forward” for the project, and reflects years of “rigorous review” from the federal agency. The company “is committed to …

Sur l'enfermement psychiatrique en France

fermés

La brochure trouve d'autant plus son sens dans le contexte actuel de fascisation et d'eugénisme grandissant. Qu'on pense à la gestion de la pandémie de Covid-19 mais aussi plus récemment aux épisodes caniculaires répétés (durant lesquels les personnes psychiatrisées ou médicamentées sont plus particulièrement victimes) ou encore plus idirectement à la loi «

 

fin de vie

 

» qui introduit dans le droit français le suicide assisté et l'euthanasie, la hiérarchie des vies sur laquelle il se fonde et la menace directe qu'il représente pour les personnes malades ou handicapées, les exemples sont légion.


La psychiatrie est aussi utilisée comme outil de surveillance et de répression depuis maintenant une bonne dizaine d'année, avec une accélération impressionante depuis les mandats Macron. Dès 2018, un nouveau fichier, Hopsyweb, est créé afin de recenser les données relatives aux personnes faisant l'objet de soins psychiatriques sans consentement (internements sur demande d'un tiers, d'un juge, du préfet...)

FSPRT

 (fichier de traitement des signalements pour la prévention de la radicalisation à caractère terroriste). Le tout, sous-entendant évidemment que les forces répressives prennent en compte la psychiatrie et le "trouble mental" soit comme un facteur aggravant de la soi-disant "radicalisation" voire comme menace en soi à prévenir. Ces listes de personnes psychiatrisées rappellent évidemment les mouvements fascistes historiques et l'implication des corporations médicales dans ces derniers, notamment à travers le mouvement eugéniste, qu'on retrouve des Etats-Unis à l'Europe dès les années 1920, soutenu par de nombreuses fondations capitalistes

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Jeffries Says He Opposes Medicare for All — Which Would Save 114k Lives Yearly
content:
This is a reversal of his prior stance on the legislation, which he once cosponsored.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) has said that he now opposes Medicare for All, flipping on his previous stance just as Democrats are on the cusp of potentially winning back control of the House.

Medicare for All is “not legislation that I am currently cosponsoring or that I support,” Jeffries said in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday. Jeffries declined to say whether or not he would bring the legislation to a vote, though suggested that he wouldn’t, in the case that Democrats retake the House — which some pollsters say is a likely outcome.

This is a reversal of his stance from just a few years ago. Jeffries first announced that he was backing the legislation in 2019, and was listed as a cosponsor as recently as 2021. But he dropped off of the cosponsor list in 2023, after he succeeded Rep. Nancy Pelosi (California) to take the helm of House Democratic leader.

In the interview, Jeffries did not offer a different policy solution, but rather the vague promise that Democrats are “going to fight to make health care affordable for every single American,” he said.

Jeffries has often offered platitudes in the face of the health care crisis; last year, as Republicans were gutting the Affordable Care Act and kicking millions of Americans off of their health insurance, Jeffries simply said that, to push back, Democrats must “decisively address the Republican health care crisis because it is serious,” and that they must do so in a “bipartisan” way.

His latest statements came just days after Yale University and University of Maryland researchers released preprinted research finding that the universal single-payer health care system proposed under Medicare for All would prevent a whopping 114,000 deaths a year. At the same time, it would also save the U.S. over $1 trillion in health care costs annually, the study found — undercutting one of the biggest criticisms of the proposal.

Jeffries did not say why he has backed off his support for the legislation. But the tack to the right comes as he faces a new ascendant class of left-wing politicians taking over the Democratic Party, who are running on policy positions like abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), opposing the construction of data centers, and backing Medicare for All.

Unlike Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer (D-New York), Jeffries does not currently appear to be in danger of losing his position as head House Democrat. Still, he made several comments hostile to the left and left-wing priorities that could isolate incoming members of his own party.

In the interview, Jeffries said that he doesn’t support the Democratic Socialists of America’s policy agenda, and declined to say whether he believes that democratic socialists belong in the Democratic Party. He also declined to say if he would bring legislation on abolishing ICE to a vote if Democrats retake the House.

He instead said that he is “committed to dramatically reforming ICE” with proposals like unmasking ICE agents and ensuring they wear body cameras — though some places have already barred ICE agents from wearing masks, and the agency is already mandating the wearing of body cameras.

Jeffries has a history of hostility toward the left, and has continued to emphasize his opposition to more left-wing candidates for office. In June, after a slate of Zohran Mamdani-backed democratic socialist candidates swept House primary races in New York, Jeffries said that Mamdani has “work to do” in order to placate the more conservative wings of the Democratic Party.

author: Unknown
title: Temmuz zammının ardından hastaneden izlenimler
content:
Aylardır tüm memurlar gibi biz sağlık emekçilerinin de beklediği temmuz ayı zammı belirlendi. Ancak sonuç hepimiz için büyük bir hayal kırıklığı oldu. Çalışanlar arasında yüzde 13.5’lik zammın adeta bizimle dalga geçmek olduğu konuşuluyor. Zamla maaşlarımızda 9-13 bin lira arasında bir artış oldu. Oysa gıdadan elektriğe, sudan temizlik malzemelerine, giysiden daha birçok temel ihtiyaca kadar her şeye kat kat zam geldi.

Biz sağlık emekçileri 12 ay boyunca zor çalışma koşullarında, eksik personelle çalışıyoruz. Çoğu zaman dört kişinin yapması gereken işi bir sağlık emekçisi yapmak zorunda kalıyor. Kış aylarından indirimli ve taksitli olarak ayarladığımız tatillere bile artık gidemiyoruz. “Bırakın tatili, aç karnımızı bile zor doyuruyoruz” diyen arkadaşlarımız var. Bu şartlarda birçok sağlık emekçisi ek iş yapmak zorunda kalıyor. Kimi küçük bahçesinde yetiştirdiği, belki kendisine bile ancak yetecek sebzeleri satıyor. Kimi el emeğiyle yaptığı ürünleri satarak gelir elde etmeye çalışıyor. Kimi e-ticaret işleri yapıyor. Mesai sonrasında kafede çalışan da var, araba yıkayan da… Bu liste uzayıp gidiyor. Çünkü herkes gibi sağlık emekçisi de artık zar zor geçiniyor.

Çocuklarımız söz konusu olduğunda da durum farklı değil. Üç aylık okul tatilini ekonomik açıdan bir fırsat olarak görmek zorunda kalanlarımız var. Çocuğunu memleketine, anneannesinin ya da babaannesinin yanına gönderen, “Hiç değilse üç ay kurs ücreti vermiyoruz” diyenlerimiz var. Oysa kim ister üç ay boyunca çocuğundan ayrı kalmayı? Bir de okullar kapalıyken kendisi çalışmaya devam ettiği için çocuğuna bakacak kimseyi bulamayan ve mecburen kurslara astronomik ücretler ödeyen sağlık emekçileri var.

Tatil anlayışımız da ekonomik koşullara göre değişti. Bazı sağlık çalışanları daha ekonomik olsun diye ortak bir yazlık tutup iki-üç aile birlikte tatil yapıyor. Bazılarımız ise memlekette ailesinin yanına gidiyor hem birkaç gün orada kalıyor hem de kışlık hazırlıklarını yapıp dönüyor. Tatilini bu şekilde değerlendiren sağlık emekçilerinin sayısı da az değil.

Hastanede çalışırken çevreme baktığımda artık bunların tek tek insanların yaşadığı istisnai durumlar olmadığını görüyorum. Aynı koridorlarda çalışan, aynı nöbetleri tutan, aynı yoğunluğu yaşayan sağlık emekçilerinin ortak gündemi geçinebilmek. Aylarca beklediğimiz zamdan sonra bile konuştuğumuz şey dinlenmek ya da tatil yapmak değil; hangi masraftan kısacağımız, çocukların yaz aylarını nasıl geçireceği ve mesai sonrasında hangi ek işi yapabileceğimiz. Oysa biz, en temel ihtiyaçlarımızı bile tam olarak karşılayamadığımız bu koşulları değil; insanca yaşayabileceğimiz bir ücreti, dinlenebileceğimiz bir tatili, çocuklarımızla kaygı duymadan zaman geçirebilmeyi, mesai sonrasında başka bir işte çalışmak zorunda kalmadan hayatımızı sürdürebilmeyi istiyoruz.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Jaharra Anglin Stubbs
title: Massachusetts Expands Later Term Abortion Access
content:
Early Monday morning on August 10, 2026, Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey signed the Prioritizing Patient Access to Care Act into law, expanding access to abortion later in pregnancy and removing the state’s previous 24-week gestational limit. Under the new law, healthcare providers can determine whether abortion care is medically appropriate based on their professional judgment.

Previously, Massachusetts law generally limited abortion access to the first 24 weeks of pregnancy, creating a significant barrier for those seeking later-stage care. After that point, physicians could provide abortion care only under limited circumstances, including when necessary to preserve a patient’s life or physical or mental health, in cases of a lethal fetal diagnosis, or when the fetus was unlikely to survive outside the uterus.

Even within these exceptions, patients were sometimes denied care. State Representative Christine Barber shared that hospitals were still denying patients access to abortions, even when a fetus was determined unlikely to survive outside the uterus. As a result, Massachusetts patients were forced to leave the state, sometimes as far as the Southwest, to access the care they needed.

The new law changes that. As ACLU of Massachusetts Executive Director Carl Rose affirmed, Massachusetts residents facing dire medical complications can now receive essential healthcare without these rigid in-state limitations.

Massachusetts is now the 10th state, including Washington, D.C., to no longer have gestational limits on abortion access. That change could also make Massachusetts a “destination” for patients from states where abortion remains heavily restricted, particularly for those seeking care later in pregnancy.

Unfortunately, 13 states still enforce strict abortion bans at any stage of pregnancy, even though they claim there are exceptions to these rules. Across the country, vague or restrictive abortion laws have created uncertainty about when providers can legally provide care, leaving patients to bear the consequences.

Massachusetts’ new law represents an important recognition that abortion is health care and that decisions about pregnancy should be made by patients in consultation with their healthcare providers, not dictated by arbitrary legal restrictions.

​​But state-level protections alone cannot guarantee equitable access to abortion.

Although Massachusetts has taken a much-appreciated step to assert what we know to be true, that abortion is healthcare, there is still more work to be done. It is not enough to have examples of abortion protections at the state level; it is critical to have abortion protections across every border within the United States.

title: Antifa-Ost-Prozess: trotz Unterbringung in der Psychiatrie verhandlungsfähig?
content:
Ein weiterer zäher Prozesstag im Dresdner Antifa-Ost-Komplex fand diesen Mittwoch statt. Es ist schon fast 10:30 Uhr, als die wenigen Zuschauer:innen die sich eingefunden hatten, in den Saal dürfen, denn seit gestern war die Öffentlichkeit ausgeschlossen.


Was war passiert?


Einer der Angeklagten befindet sich in einer psychisch sehr belasteten Phase und verliert Lebenskraft sowie Lebensmut. Das zuständige Amtsgericht hat ihn zu seinem Schutz vorläufig in die Psychiatrie eingewiesen, dort darf er nichts besitzen, womit er sich das Leben nehmen könnte, keinen Gürtel, keinee Schnürsenkel, keine Ladekabel.


Dies war vermutlich schon am Tag zuvor in nicht-öffentlicher Sitzung erörtert, die Öffentlichkeit jedoch zum Schutz der persönlichen Belange des Betroffenen ausgeschlossen worden. Jetzt ist es aber sein Anwalt der in der heutigen Sitzung genau diese Details vorträgt, als er ein Obergutachten fordert.


Der eine Arzt der Klinik spricht davon, dass der Betroffene, wenn überhaupt, nur dann reisefähig ist, wenn medizinisches Personal diesen begleitet, ein anderer Arzt wiederum sieht keinerlei Bedenken was Verhandlungs- und Reisefähigkeit angeht.


Auch die Verhandlungsfähigkeit ist strittig, zum einen wegen der akuten Belastungsreaktion und krisenhaften Zuspitzung im Leben des Angeklagten, zum anderen wegen dessen Medikation, denn das verordnete Psychopharmakon wirkt stark dämpfend.


Das Oberlandesgericht lässt den Angeklagten jedoch aus der Psychiatrie nach Dresden bringen, ohne allerdings, dass das polizeiliche Begleitpersonal über die konkrete Situation umfassend informiert ist, ohne dass Notfallmedikamente zur Hand sind, ohne, dass die Polizei weiß was bei welchem Notfall konkret zu tun wäre. Der Anwalt ist ersichtlich empört, auch weil im Gerichtsgebäude sich dieses Unwissen bei den Wachtmeister:innen nahtlos fortsetzt.


Der Antrag wird entgegen genommen, aber eine Antwort einstweilen vom Vorsitzenden zurück gestellt.


Die einzige Zeugin des Tages


Geladen ist Kriminalhauptkommissarin Golze, die knapp eine viertel Stunde über ihre Vernehmung des angeblich geschädigten Neonazi Karl Jonas Kaden befragt wird. Dieser soll in Wurzen 2020 nach seiner Rückreise von einer Demonstration in Dresden, am Bahnhof in Wurzen attackiert worden sein.


Kaden selbst wollte am 19. März 2026 vor dem Oberlandesgericht

nicht aussagen

, er selbst befindet sich gerade in Haft, da er im „Sächsische-Separatisten-Prozess“ als Angeklagter vor Gericht steht.


Und so hangelt sich die Polizistin durch ihre Erinnerungen daran, was der Zeuge Kaden im Rahmen ihrer Vernehmung gesagt haben soll. Sie hätte ihn, nach Rücksprache mit seinen Eltern in dessen Kinderzimmer vernommen, er habe klar auf alle Fragen geantwortet und sich der AfD zugerechnet und als „geschichtsinteressiert“ bezeichnet. Mit ein paar anderen sei er nach Dresden Gefahren, wo jedes Jahr Nazis aufmarschieren um an die Bombardierung Dresdens zu erinnern.


Er sei von 15-20 Vermummten attackiert worden, eine Kopfwunde musste getackert werden. Da ihn jemand einen „Scheiß Nazi“ genannt habe, vermute er „Linke“ hinter dem Angriff. Wenig später wir die Zeugin im allgemeinen Einverständnis entlassen und darf gehen.


Langes Betrachten von Bildern auf dem Monitor


Der Rest des Prozesstages, der erneut von diversen Pausen geprägt war, vergeht damit, dass sich die Prozessbeteiligten und die zu Anfang noch 11, dann sieben und am Ende sechs Zuschauer:innen Fotos ansehen. Um den Prozess zu beschleunigen werden zahlreiche Akten im „Selbstleseverfahren“ eingebracht, sprich alle Beteiligten bekommen Zeit und Gelegenheit Aktenteile selbst zu lesen. Die Bilder jedoch, die müssen „in Augenschein“ genommen werden, in der Verhandlung.


So geht es dann mal in die Wohnung von Lina E. aus dem ersten Antifa-Ost-Prozess, man sieht einen Beutel an einer Türklinke hängen. Oder es werden Observationsphotos gezeigt, wobei hier eine der Verteidigerinnen der Verwertung widerspricht, da die rechtlichen Voraussetzungen für die Observation nicht vorgelegen hätten. Aufgabe der Ermittlungsrichter:innen sei es, Anträge auf Observation eigenständig, und unter Zuhilfenahme der Akten zu prüfen und nicht bloß abzunicken. Dazu Fotos von Handys oder deren Displays, wann wer wen angerufen hat.


Zustimmendes Gemurmel im Publikum kommt auf, als auf einem der präsentierten Bilder „Free Lina“ zu sehen ist.

author: Luis Barrueto
title: Vita Activa & the Digital Security Helpline join forces to support mental health and digital safety for activists
content:
A digital attack is never just a technical incident. It often comes with psychological distress, leads to burnout, and opens up new threats to physical safety that require expert support. At the same time, individuals coping with harassment or online violence often need more than mental health support; they need immediate technical assistance to secure their digital presence and stay safe.


Activists, nonprofit organizations, human rights defenders, independent journalists, and other at-risk communities may lack sufficient access to the resources and expertise they need to address these intertwined problems. By joining forces, Access Now’s

Digital Security Helpline

 and the nonprofit organization

Vita Activa

 aim to meet that need, ensuring that civil society members receive holistic, rapid, and tailored support. 


Vita Activa, an

Access Now grantee

, operates a helpline for journalists, activists, human rights defenders, women, and LGBTQ+ people who face stress, trauma, burnout, digital violence, or crises arising from their work and activism. Our Digital Security Helpline offers 24/7, free-of-charge technical assistance on digital security for members of civil society, with a specific

mandate

 to assist activists, researchers, media organizations, journalists, bloggers, and human rights defenders. 


Our new framework for collaboration will allow the two organizations to offer:


Holistic case referrals:

 With explicit consent from individuals seeking help, our organizations will streamline referrals to provide complementary support. A tech query at Vita Activa will seamlessly connect with the technical expertise of the Digital Security Helpline, while individuals contacting Access Now who need mental health assistance, peer support, or psychological first aid will be connected directly to Vita Activa.


Mutual collaboration to sustain the ecosystem of support for civil society:

 Our organizations already collaborate, offering one another mutual support through information sharing, documentation, joint efforts to develop sustainable solutions for our respective communities, and more. Our new framework formalizes this work and allows both teams to explore further avenues for collaboration.


How to reach out for support


If you or your organization are facing digital attacks, we encourage you to learn more about our respective services and reach out to either of our organizations depending on the type of support you need:


Experiencing online violence or burnout? Need psychological first aid?

If you meet the criteria for support,

contact

Vita Activa

 for free and confidential assistance in  in Spanish, Portuguese, English, and Arabic, at support @ vita-activa.org (Spanish) and support @ vita-activa.org (English)  or +56 9 3291 9018  (WhatsApp, Signal).


Facing a digital attack or incident that threatens your digital security? Need advice to prevent attacks or secure your online presence?

If your request fits within our

mandate

,

contact the Digital Security Helpline

, which provides direct technical assistance and support in nine languages.


As civil society continues to face mounting challenges to basic rights and freedoms worldwide, it is crucial to ensure that those most at risk have continuous holistic support and protection, especially given the drastic fund reductions that have

further exposed civil society to security vulnerabilities

. We are proud to work with Vita Activia on creative, collaborative, and flexible approaches to defending those who defend our rights.


The post

Vita Activa & the Digital Security Helpline join forces to support mental health and digital safety for activists

 appeared first on

Access Now

content:
Victorian allied health workers strike for better pay, conditions


Isaac Nellist

Thousands of allied health professionals working in Victoria’s public hospitals took part in a 24-hour strike on August 11 demanding better pay and working conditions.


Striking healthcare workers gathered outside the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre in Parkville where they heard from delegates and union officials.


Workers at the protest told Green Left that one of the main reasons for the strike was because allied health workers “need better working conditions and a genuine pay offer that keeps up with inflation”.

Victorian education workers continue to demand better pay, conditions


Historic council workers’ strike demands fair pay, conditions


Julia, a delegate at Bendigo Health, spoke about the challenges of working in rural healthcare where it’s hard to retain staff and asserted that “everyone deserves to have access to high quality care”.


She pointed out that the Victorian State government refusal to value healthcare professionals will have disproportionate impacts on healthcare in rural areas.


Andrew Hewat , executive officer for Victorian Allied Health Professionals Associations (VAHPA) said “the state government has boxed us into a corner” and that “healthcare workers are being disrespected by the state government not giving a genuine offer”.


VAHPA is campaigning for a 38.16% pay increase over three years. While Victorian Labor’s latest offer is reportedly only about 19-21% over four years.
