title: Attack on Kurdish workers in Zonguldak
content:
It was reported that more than 70 workers and their families from the Cizre (Cizîr) and Silopi (Silopiya) districts of Şirnak (Şirnex), who had traveled to Bektaşlı village in Zonguldak’s Alaplı district as seasonal hazelnut workers, had been attacked over the past two days.


DEM Party Şirnak lawmakers issued a statement following footage circulated on social media and raised concerns among the public. The lawmakers said they had been informed that the workers were attacked yesterday. After the workers contacted the party this morning, meetings were held with the Zonguldak Governor’s Office and the Alaplı District Governor’s Office.


They were attacked twice


During the meetings, it was reported that the gendarmerie had intervened in the attack and that the workers’ safety had been secured. However, it was stated that the workers were attacked again in the evening while returning from the fields. The statement noted that, despite the gendarmerie being present at the scene, footage circulated publicly showed that it had been unable to prevent the attack. The statement said that the Alaplı District Governor was subsequently contacted again, emphasizing that the safety of the more than 70 workers and their families must be ensured immediately and effectively. It was reported that the district governor’s office was working either to move the families to a safe location nearby or to take the necessary security measures where they were staying.


“Legal proceedings have been initiated”


The statement also said that the Alaplı Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office had initiated legal proceedings regarding the attack.


The statement noted that seasonal agricultural workers had traveled hundreds of kilometers to Zonguldak in order to earn a living, and said, “Ensuring the safety of our people is the responsibility of the public authorities.” The lawmakers said they would continue to follow the process to ensure the safety of the workers and their families, investigate the attack in all its aspects, and prevent similar attacks from occurring again.

author: Unknown
title: Kural: More democratic laws will strengthen support for the process
content:
Actress Jülide Kural said the Framework Law has shortcomings, adding: “Rather than rejecting it, I see this process as a beginning, the first line in rebuilding a space for democracy, peace and freedom. We have to join hands and achieve this together.” Kural emphasized that art would also feel much freer in a society where everything is not associated with “terrorism,” and said the government needs to take more concrete and comprehensive steps to address concerns about the process.


Actress Jülide Kural answered ANF’s questions about the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the relationship between art and peace.


Kural emphasized that art can play a major role in breaking down prejudices and said: “Art undoubtedly provides something in this respect. Looking at the long history of humanity, we are confronted with this reality: Through art, people can grasp the emotion beyond words, empathy and the truth behind what is visible. Through a painting, a piece of music, a play or a movie, art can create spaces that enable people to move away from many entrenched and categorized ideas they have accumulated in their minds over thousands of years and to think freely beyond them.


Of course, this does not happen constantly or all the time. But that is why many of us have a movie, sometimes a piece of music, a painting, a sculpture or a play that stays in our minds. It can suddenly, perhaps even for a moment, break down all the prejudices you have held until that day, and this can become an important turning point in your life. I have been doing theatre and working in the arts for nearly 45 years, and I see that art has such a power. This is also true for me personally; I do not think of it only from the audience’s perspective. It is a space that constantly changes and transforms me, allowing me to reconsider what I have always believed to be true, to look at it from another perspective and to feel differently. The development of the inner world also carries the possibility of bringing thoughts about the real world we share to another dimension and a deeper level.”


Ignoring the world around us also negatively affects artistic production


Kural said art could also play an effective role in the Peace and Democratic Society Process and continued: “An artist does not necessarily have to understand the entire political sphere or be deeply involved in it. But ignoring the world they live in and the network of relationships around them is also a major obstacle to artistic production. For me, an artist is someone who questions the world, the country and the life they live in. Because when they do not engage in this questioning, when they do not see those contradictions, I believe they cannot truly build those cries within themselves. Therefore, of course, what we aim for in this process is peace.”


The law is inadequate but could mark the beginning of rebuilding


Jülide Kural said that an important turning point had emerged in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, particularly with Abdullah Öcalan’s call: “I think a very important turning point has emerged both for the state of the Republic of Turkey and for the Kurdish movement, the Kurdish Freedom Movement, which has been struggling for so many years, particularly with Abdullah Öcalan’s call. The fact that an organization that has waged such a strong and prolonged struggle is dissolving itself and laying down its arms means that, for someone like me who advocates peace, we are in a process that arouses curiosity but also requires great caution.


I certainly find this process very valuable because it opens up the possibility of peace and, in the long term, the possibility of peace between peoples, and offers a glimmer of hope. But, of course, I have questions, and I think we need to be very careful. The Framework Law that has emerged, in particular... There is again something dialectical here; we need to develop a way of thinking that takes this into account.


It is undoubtedly very important that, for the first time, the state is addressing in Parliament, through legislation, the Kurdish people’s struggle for equal citizenship and freedom, which has remained unseen and unheard for so long. But when I look at the law itself, I see many problems. If we are talking about this issue, why does the word ‘Kurdish’ not appear even once? The use of a security-oriented language is another issue that raises questions for me.


Peace is so difficult to build, and freedom is …

title: Memorial gathering for martyrs continues into its third day
content:
Organized by the Association for Solidarity, Cooperation and Culture of Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER), the condolence gathering for the martyrs of the Kurdistan Freedom Struggle at Koşuyolu Park in the Rezan (Bağlar) district is continuing into its third day.


Alongside a large poster of Abdullah Öcalan, banners reading “Martyrs never die,” “Martyrs are the light of our path,” and “Martyrs are our honor” were hung at the condolence site. Families who arrived at the site in the morning began receiving condolences after placing photographs of the fallen guerrillas and carnations on the tables.


Many people visited the condolence gathering in the morning. Those attending chanted “Martyrs never die.”


A commemoration event will be held at 6:00 p.m. following the condolence gathering.

title: Two prisoners held in “Pit-Type” jail go on indefinite hunger strike
content:
Hüseyin Özarslan and Mehmet Akdemir, two of four political prisoners at Antalya High-Security Pit-Type Prison whose promised transfers were not carried out, began an indefinite hunger strike on 18 August.


Ferdi Sarıkaya, a member of TAYAD, told ANF that Mehmet Akdemir, who is over 60 and has various health problems, and Hüseyin Özarslan would not be able to withstand a prolonged hunger strike, and added that “the promises must be kept so that another coffin does not emerge from the pit-type prisons.”


Four months passed, but no transfer carried out


Hüseyin Özen, Tahsin Sağaltıcı and Gürkan Türkoğlu were forcibly taken to Antalya City Hospital on the 264th day of an indefinite hunger strike they had launched demanding transfer in protest against the inhumane isolation conditions imposed at Antalya High-Security Pit-Type Prison. After being forcibly subjected to medical intervention at the hospital, Gürkan Türkoğlu fell into a coma and later died while fighting for his life in the intensive care unit. After the Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor of Antalya promised that the four prisoners in the pit-type prison would be transferred to the L-Type Prison located 100 meters away, Hüseyin Özen and Tahsin Sağaltıcı ended their indefinite hunger strikes on their 266th day. Özen and Sağaltıcı were hastily transferred from the hospital to Antalya L-Type Prison, but it has emerged that the transfer of the four political prisoners at Antalya Pit-Type Prison, which was a condition for ending their hunger strike, has still not been carried out despite four months having passed.


TAYAD member Ferdi Sarıkaya announced that Hüseyin Özarslan and Mehmet Akdemir, two of the four political prisoners awaiting transfer, began an indefinite hunger strike on August 18 after the Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor of Antalya failed to keep his promise.


Promotion for those promising a transfer that never happened


Sarıkaya emphasized that the Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor of Antalya also failed to keep his promise that Hüseyin Özarslan, Mehmet Akdemir, Mustafa Gök and Osman Beyazkaya, who are held at Antalya Pit-Type Prison, would be transferred to an L-Type Prison or another suitable prison.


Pointing out that the Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor in question and the prison prosecutor responsible for sentence enforcement were promoted while Gürkan Türkoğlu was in intensive care, Sarıkaya said: “The Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor of Antalya promised that after Tahsin Sağaltıcı and Hüseyin Özen completed their hospital treatment, Hüseyin Özarslan, Mehmet Akdemir, Osman Beyazkaya and Mustafa Gök, who remained at Antalya Pit-Type Prison, would also be transferred with them to the L-Type Prison. However, even though four months have passed, this promise has not been fulfilled.


In Osman Beyazkaya’s case, his status as a prisoner serving an aggravated life sentence was cited as the reason, while it was claimed that instructions were awaited from the Ministry of Justice for the other three prisoners. Not only did the Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor fail to keep his promise, he was promoted while Gürkan Türkoğlu was in a coma. Likewise, the prison prosecutor was promoted on the same day. I do not know what kind of promotion this was. But I believe they were promoted because they were responsible for Gürkan Türkoğlu’s death. Because there was nothing here that warranted a promotion; on the contrary, they abused their positions. If both the deputy chief prosecutor and the prison prosecutor had accepted the transfer requests on time, Gürkan Türkoğlu would be alive today. Now the promises they made have also been left hanging. When lawyers asked the newly appointed Deputy Chief Public Prosecutor of Antalya why the transfers had not been carried out, he cited Osman Beyazkaya’s aggravated life sentence as the reason, while saying that transfer requests for the other three prisoners, Hüseyin Özarslan, Mehmet Akdemir and Mustafa Gök, had been submitted and were currently awaiting a signature from the Ministry of Justice.”


Concern for condition of prisoners


Pointing out that the four political prisoners who should have been transferred are being arbitrarily held at Antalya Pit-Type Prison, Sarıkaya emphasized: “To protest this unlawfulness, Hüseyin Özarslan and Mehmet Akdemir began an indefinite hunger strike on August 18. Hüseyin Özarslan is 66 years old, while Mehmet Akdemir is 64. Both have various health problems. Özarslan and Akdemir cannot withstand …

title: Trump'tan Kanada'ya tarife çıkışı: 'Artık buna son'
content:
ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Kanada ile yaşanan tarife gerilimine ilişkin sosyal medya hesabından açıklama yaptı. Trump açıklamasında Kanada'nın "ABD'nin bir eyaleti olmadan eyalet olmanın getirilerinden yararlanmak istediğini" savundu.

Kanada'nın ABD'li çiftçilerden uzun yıllardır para aldığını ve onları tarifelere tabi tuttuğunu, artık buna izin vermeyeceklerini belirten Trump, "Kanada, eyalet olmadan eyalet olmanın faydalarından yararlanmak istiyor. Ayrıca yıllardır harika çiftçilerimize çok yüksek gümrük vergileri uyguluyorlar. Artık buna son." ifadelerini kullandı.

İki ülke arasında üç günlük ek sürede yürütülen görüşmelerden anlaşma çıkmayınca ABD'nin yaklaşık 20 milyar dolarlık Kanada ürününe getirdiği yüzde 50 ek gümrük tarifesi yürürlüğe girdi.

Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney, görüşmelerde ilerleme sağlandığını ancak ortaya çıkan şartların Kanada'nın hedeflerini karşılamadığını belirterek müzakere heyetini Ottawa'ya geri çağırdı.

title: Alevis in metropolitan cities face discrimination and exclusion
content:
Alevis have reached the present day through resistance as a people subjected to oppression, exploitation and massacres in Turkey. Cemevis and Alevi cultural centres across Turkey continue to exist as the result of a long struggle and resistance.


Crosses were marked on the doors of Alevi homes, Alevis were denied employment because of their identity, and they were subjected to the imposition of Sunni Islam in schools. For a long time, they were unable to bury their dead according to their own faith. In response, the Alevi community secured many of the rights it has today and advanced its demands through its own struggle and resistance.


Ali Kenanoğlu from the Hubyar Sultan Ocak, Mercan Gül from the Atmi Ocak, and Sevim Yalıncakoğlu, an Alevi spiritual leader (ana) from the Alevi Yalıncak Sultan Ocak, spoke to ANF about the struggle for life waged by Alevis in metropolitan cities, where they have sought to rebuild their lives following displacement.


Those who could not go to Germany migrated to Turkey’s cities


 


Sevim Yalıncakoğlu said that Alevi migration to metropolitan cities began in the 1960s and noted that those who were unable to go abroad as workers moved particularly to major cities: “If we look at Turkey as a whole, the wave of migration from villages to cities began in the 1960s, and the main migration started when Germany began recruiting workers. It was during that period that people first began thinking about migrating from villages to cities. Those who could not go to Germany, those who could not go abroad as workers, then said, ‘There is Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir and Adana in Turkey.’ During that period, the Alevi population became widely dispersed across these cities.


People who had lived within their own communities in villages moved together to wherever others from their community were going. There was a logic to this, of course. Whenever someone moved to the city and found a job, they would call one of their relatives to join them, and that circle would expand.”


No one could perform the Passing to the Truth rite in Istanbul


Sevim Yalıncakoğlu said that Alevi houses of worship (cemevis) began to become widespread in cities particularly after the Sivas Massacre and noted that Alevis faced serious difficulties, especially in conducting funeral rites: “The rapid establishment of cemevis in cities, the creation of Alevi institutions and the beginning of organizational efforts among Alevis, particularly in Istanbul and other cities, largely began after the Sivas Massacre. Of course, these people did not suddenly appear here; they had already been living in these places. In the 1970s, 1980s and before the 1990s, Alevis faced a particular problem: There was nowhere for them to perform the Passing to the Truth (Hakk’a yürüme) rite. There were only a few places in Istanbul, the tekkes and dervish lodges of the time. Karacaahmet and Şahkulu were the two best-known dervish lodges. Apart from these, there was a cemevi in Haramidere, established in 1988. Just imagine, a cemevi was established in Kartal around 1986, but Istanbul was enormous. In the 1970s, there was virtually nowhere apart from Şahkulu and Karacaahmet. I asked them, ‘What did you do then?’ They said, ‘No one performed the Passing to the Truth rite in Istanbul.’


In other words, out of necessity, one or two people who passed away during the winter were simply washed outside their homes before being sent away. Unfortunately, they also had to take some of them to mosques because the state did not allow the Passing to the Truth rite to be performed outside their homes.”


There was serious exclusion by people in everyday life


Yalıncakoğlu also spoke about the everyday lives of Alevis and described their experiences. She said: “I think we experienced something that every Alevi has experienced. We went to Zara, a district of Sivas, and no one around us was Alevi. I did not even know that there were beliefs other than Alevism in the world because I had only lived in my village. There was serious exclusion by people; they looked at your faith as if you were doing something terribly wrong, as if you did not actually have a faith. They would say things that made you imagine someone throwing you into a cauldron and burning you alive simply because you were Alevi.


Just imagine, someone who came from an Alevi village to study in the city was being raised to become hostile towards their entire family. Because your worship was not really …

title: Political prisoner Mahbube Shabani goes on hunger strike in Iran
content:
Mahbube Shabani, a political prisoner who was detained and arrested during the January protests in Iran, began a hunger strike to protest the poor conditions in the quarantine section of Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad and the continued uncertainty surrounding her case.


Shabani was transferred to the quarantine section on 5 July as part of a disciplinary punishment. It was reported that Shabani was subjected to severe physical intervention during the transfer and developed a skin condition due to the unhealthy conditions in the quarantine section.


Shabani was detained in Mashhad on 2 February. After her detention, she was held in solitary confinement for an extended period before being transferred to the women’s ward of Vakilabad Prison.


According to the indictment prepared against her, Shabani is accused of taking people who were injured during the protests on 8, 9, and 10 January 2026, to medical centers on her motorcycle.


The initial indictment also charged Mahbube Shabani with “moharebeh” (enmity against God). However, this charge was removed from the text several weeks before the final indictment was prepared.

title: Rize sokakları ezber yıktı: Dert dinleyen Özel, yeni dertlerin sahibi oldu
content:
Rize Çayeli’ne bağlı Balıkçılar Köyü’nde yükselen ilk ses, bölgenin hiciv kültürünün canlı bir özeti gibi. 


Bir yurttaşın "Şair Eşref’in hemşerisisiniz, Rize’de musluklar hariç her yer akıyor" serzenişine, YENİ Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel’in yine Şair Eşref’in telgrafhanedeki meşhur nüktesiyle yanıt vermesi hepimizin yüzünü gülümsetti. 


Çünkü, binanın muhtelif yerlerinin aktığı, muslukların ise kurak kaldığı o eski bürokratik mizah, bugün Karadenizli köylünün altyapı ve geçim dertleriyle birebir örtüşüyordu.


"Bülbül gibi konuş başkanım"


21 Ağustos Trabzon ve 22 Ağustos Rize durakları, YENİ Parti’nin il dışındaki ilk büyük sınavı niteliğindeydi. Karşılama, bölgenin simgesel kodlarıyla başladı. Erdoğan’ın "bizim simit" dediği Rize simidi ve "Aman sesin gitmesin, bülbül gibi konuş başkanım" dilekleriyle ikram edilen Anzer balı…


Rize merkezde, Çarşıbaşı’nda halkın arasına karışıldığı an, analiz edilmesi gereken en kritik sahalardan sanırım. 


Doğu Karadeniz genelinde YENİ Parti’nin Çerçeve Yasa tutumuna yönelik soru işaretleri ve bu konuda takınılan "Evet-Hayır" tavrının bölgedeki yansıması merak konusuydu.


Özgür Özel’in saha yürüyüşünde gördüğü yoğun ilgi, bu konudaki tereddütleri büyük oranda dağıttı. Karadeniz etabında sınavın en kritik virajı aşıldı diyebiliriz, Özel’in halktaki karşılığı görünür hale geldi. Kuşkusuz Diyarbakır, Hakkâri, Mardin ve Şırnak gibi kentlerindeki yurttaşların bu yaklaşıma nasıl yanıt vereceği ve sürecin oradaki karşılığının ne olacağı sorusu hâlâ yanıt bekleyen bir denklem olarak duruyor.


Yürüyüşe dönecek olursak… Yürüyüş boyunca “hak hukuk adalet” sloganı hep yükseldi. Yine Rize sokaklarında alışılageldik ritmin dışında "Özgür gelecek, karanlık bitecek”, “Özgür Türkiye özgür gelecek”, “özgür gelecek müjde gelecek” sloganı yankılandı. 


Taksim Meydanı’ndan İstiklal Caddesi boyunca Tünel’e uzanan o hıncahınç yürüyüş hatlarını andıran kalabalıkta, pencere ve balkonlardan çaya davet edenler, evine çağırıyorlardı. Sokaktaki temaslar siyasettin insan ölçeğini gösteriyordu. 


"Aman dur kötü bir şey söyleme"


Özgür Özel Rize merkezde halka birlikte yürüdü.

pic.twitter.com/Lycepim8CO


— Evrim Kepenek (@kepenekevrimm)

August 23, 2026


Özel’in daha önceki ziyaretinden tanıdığı yaşlı bir kadına annesinin sağlık durumunu sorup detayları hatırlaması dikkat çekiciydi. "Emekli maaşımı sana vereceğim" diyen kadına "Yok,biz iyi kötü kotardık sen aylığının hepsini verme" yanıtını verdi. 


Gümüşhane’den kendisini görmek için koşan çocuklar ve döner ustasının "Ankara’ya gelecek, sırf senden sebep geldi" diyerek çocuğunu tanıtması alandaki ilgiyi özetliyordu. "Seni çok seveyrum, lanet başına o tarla faresine oy verdim" diyen kadını ise Özgür Özel "Aman dur, kötü bir şey söyleme" diye karşıladı. 


Sanırım bu tablo, YENİ Partililerin kafasındaki "Acaba tepki ne olur?" sorusunu yanıtlamış oldu. Rize’nin siyasi geçmişine  atıfta bulunan Özel de Rizelilerin gösterdiği ilgisinden memnundu 


Kıyı Köyleri: Taş dökülen sahiller ve Zelek Direnişi


Rizespor formasının hediye edildiği durağın ardından rota sahil köylerine kırıldı. Balıkçılar Köyü’nde mikrofon halka uzatıldığında, bölgenin ekolojik ve ekonomik yaraları dökülmeye başladı. Yurttaşlar, sahilin taşlarla doldurulmasından, avlanacak balık kalmamasından ve İkizdere-İyidere hattında iktidara verilen oylara rağmen karşılık alınamamasından dert yandı. 


Özel’in bu taleplere yanıtı, kurumsal bir çözüm olarak Denizcilik Bakanlığı’nın kurulması önerisi oldu.


Gezinin belki de en yüksek gerilimli ve insani durağı Zelek Köyü idi. Yıllardır kadınlı erkekli geçimini denizden sağlayan köy, havuz/kafes balıkçılığı yapmak isteyen bir şirketin (ve arkasındaki siyasi iddiaların) tehdidi altındaydı. Daha geçen hafta jandarmanın müdahalesiyle yerlerde sürüklenen köylüler "Deniz olmazsa biz de olmayız" diyerek direniyordu.


Zelek Su Ürünleri Derneği Başkanı projenin zararlarını anlattı. Özel "Kadın balıkçılar konuşacak dediniz, hep erkekler konuştu" uyarısı üzerine mikrofonu alan Kaptan Hacer, "Önce gemi adamı değil, gemi insanı desinler" diyerek gülümsetti ve kafeslerin köyü yok edeceğini vurguladı.

title: Deniz ticaretine El Nino etkisi: Panama Kanalı'nda günlük gemi geçişleri azaltılacak
content:
Panama Kanalı'nda günlük gemi geçişleri, El Nino hava olayının neden olabileceği olumsuz etkileri hafifletmek ve kanal havzasına düşen yağış miktarının beklenenin altında kalması nedeniyle gemi geçiş sayısını azaltma kararı alındı.

Duyuruda, ülkede yağış mevsiminin başlamasına ve kanal yönetiminin uyguladığı su tasarrufu tedbirlerine rağmen havzadaki mevcut koşulların ek önlem alınmasını gerektirdiği kaydedildi.

Kararın, hizmetin güvenilirliğinin korunması ve insani tüketim için su kaynaklarının güvence altına alınması amacıyla alındığı belirtildi.

Pasifik okyanusundaki yüzey sıcaklıklarının yükselerek şiddetli kuraklığa ve daha sıcak kışlara yol açabileceği dile getirilirken, bu yılki El Nino etkisinin de kayıtlardaki en şiddetli iklim olaylarından biri olacağı tahmin ediliyor.

Kanalın bu yıl normalin altında yağış alması nedeniyle kanal yönetimi geçen ay su seviyesindeki düşüşü yönetebilmek için gemilerin daha az yük taşımalarını zorunlu kılan kısıtlamalar getirmişti.

Panama Kanal İdaresinin açıklamasına göre, kanal havzasındaki yağışların azalması nedeniyle günlük geçişlerin kapasitesine ilişkin geçici değişikliklere gidilecek.

Kanalda ilk kısıtlar 3 Eylül'de başlarken, 15 Eylül'den itibaren günlük 32 geminin geçişine izin verilecek. Böylece, kanaldaki günlük gemi geçişleri söz konusu tarihten itibaren mevcut seviyesine göre yüzde 11 azaltılacak.

author: anonym
title: 10 Jahre nach dem Mord an Eugeniu Botnari – Erinnern heißt Kämpfen!
content:
Eugeniu Botnari: ein Todesopfer rechter Gewalt


Vor zehn Jahren starb Eugeniu Botnari. Er wurde aus sozialdarwinistischen und rassistischen Motiven getötet.


Eugeniu Botnari war 2015 aus Moldawien nach Deutschland gekommen. In Berlin verfügte er über keinen festen Wohnsitz und kam des Öfteren bei Freundinnen und Verwandten unter. Seine Ehefrau blieb in Moldawien. Am 17. September 2016 bezichtigte der Leiter der Edeka-Filiale im Bahnhof Lichtenberg ihn zunächst des Diebstahls und fügte ihm schließlich im Getränkelager des Supermarktes mit Quarzhandschuhen so schwere Verletzungen zu, dass Eugeniu Botnari eine Hirnblutung erlitt. Während sich der Täter mit Videoaufnahmen der Misshandlung vor seinen Mitarbeiterinnen brüstete, ging Eugeniu Botnari zunächst aus Angst vor den Behandlungskosten nicht zum Arzt. Drei Tage später, am 20. September 2016, verstarb er an den Folgen eines Schädel-Hirn-Traumas.


Der Täter wurde im März 2017 zu einer Haftstrafe von drei Jahren und drei Monaten verurteilt. Während der Verhandlungen vor dem Berliner Landgericht stellte sich heraus, dass die Misshandlungen System hatten: André S. hatte bereits zuvor mehrfach Personen in dem Getränkelager des Edeka mit Quarzhandschuhen zusammengeschlagen. Die meisten seiner Opfer waren migrantische wohnungslose Menschen. Trotz all dieser Eindeutigkeiten erkennt der deutsche Staat die Tat bis heute nicht als politisch motiviert an.


Erinnern und Gedenken


Mittlerweile erinnert am Bahnhof Lichtenberg einiges an Eugeniu Botnari: Nachdem 2023 ein buntes Graffiti-Mural an einer Wand des Bahnhofs enthüllt wurde und der Bezirk die Umbenennung des Bahnhofsvorplatzes beschloss, dauerte es weitere zwei Jahre bis zur tatsächlichen Umbenennung und Einweihung der Gedenktafel.


Grund dafür war eine Schmähkampagne aus den Reihen der AfD und FDP sowie durch die Boulevardpresse, die Eugeniu Botnari nicht als Todesopfer rechter Gewalt anerkennen wollten, sondern als „Ladendieb“ diffamierten. Zeitgleich wehrte sich der Bezirk gegen die Benennung der Tat als „rassistisch“ und nannte sie stattdessen „fremdenfeindlich“. Als Kompromiss erinnert die Gedenktafel nun an „alle Opfer extrem rechter und menschenverachtender Gewalt“.


Dass der Platz dennoch umbenannt wurde und nun an Eugeniu Botnari erinnert, ist das Ergebnis jahrelanger und beharrlicher antifaschistischer Kämpfe gegen die Verharmlosung der Tat. Doch auch jetzt ist für uns klar: Erinnern ist nicht mit der einmaligen Einweihung einer Gedenktafel abgehakt, Gedenken nicht durch Platzumbenennungen abgeschlossen – schon gar nicht, solange die Verhältnisse fortbestehen, die Sozialdarwinismus und Rassismus den Weg ebnen.


Den Verhältnissen den Kampf ansagen


Die erkämpften Gedenkorte sind nur ein Tropfen auf dem heißen Stein im Kampf gegen die Abwertung armer, wohnungsloser und suchtkranker Menschen. Denn unter dem Vorwand eines vermeintlichen Sparzwangs und sich verschärfender materieller Ungleichheit geht der „Klassenkampf von oben“ unvermindert weiter. Seien es die Maßnahmen der Bundesregierung, die den Kahlschlag sozialer Sicherungssysteme vorantreiben, sei es die Hetze der bürgerlichen Medien gegen vermeintlich „Faule“ oder seien es die neu eingeführten Patrouillen in den Berliner S-Bahnen, die obdachlose Menschen rauswerfen sollen – die Botschaft ist klar: Die Folgen neoliberaler Politik sollen gefälligst diejenigen ausbaden, die angeblich faul sind, die nicht genug arbeiten oder sich vermeintlich nicht anstrengen. Gesellschaftliche und strukturelle Probleme werden zu den Folgen persönlichen Versagens erklärt.


Der Hass auf arme Menschen ist real – und er ist tödlich. Im Lichte der Parolen des Neoliberalismus und der medialen Hetze gegen arme, wohnungslose und suchterkrankte Menschen hat die Gewalt gegen obdachlose Menschen jüngst erneut Höchsstände erreicht. Das gesellschaftliche und politische Interesse daran, dieser Gewalt entschieden entgegenzutreten und langfristige Lösungen zu suchen, geht wiederum gegen Null. Mit diesen Verhältnissen kann es für uns keine Versöhnung geben.


Unsere Solidarität gilt all jenen, die im Visier sozialdarwinistischer Hetze und Gewalt geraten!


Zehn Jahre nach dem Tod von Eugeniu Botnari gehen wir am 17. September 2026 auf die Straße: In Erinnerung an Eugeniu Botnari und gegen die sozialdarwinistischen Zustände in diesem Land! Kämpfen wir für das gute Leben für alle und gegen Marginalisierung, Verdrängung, Sozialdarwinismus und Rassismus!

title: Ukrayna Rusya'ya İHA saldırısı düzenledi, Putin "Pandora'nın kutusunu açtılar" dedi
content:
Ukrayna’ya ait insansız hava araçlarının (İHA) Rusya’nın farklı noktalarına düzenlediği hava saldırılarında 10 kişi hayatını kaybetti, onlarca kişi yaralandı. Yaşananların ardından Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin, “Şişeden cini kendileri çıkardılar” ifadeleriyle Kiev yönetimine uyarıda bulundu.

Rusya’nın Ukrayna’da 16 kişinin ölümüne ve 135 kişinin yaralanmasına yol açan saldırılarının ardından Ukrayna, Rusya’daki çok sayıda bölgeye İHA saldırısı başlattı. Moskova yönetimi, doğrudan ekonomik altyapı ve sanayi tesislerinin vurulduğunu, can kayıpları ile yaralanmaların yaşandığını bildirdi.

Rusya Savunma Bakanlığı, gün içindeki ilk açıklamasında 250 İHA’nın etkisiz hale getirildiğini duyururken, gece boyunca toplam 457 insansız hava aracının düşürüldüğünü kaydetti.

Belgorod Valiliği, saldırılar sonucu bölgde 2 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiğini, 13 kişinin yaralandığını bildirdi.

Samara Valisi Vyaçeslav Fedorişçev, yaşlı bir kadının öldüğünü, sanayi tesislerinin zarar gördüğünü ve yerel bir rafineride yangın çıktığını aktardı. Bölgedeki e-ticaret şirketi Ozone ise lojistik tesisinin hasar alması ve personelin yaralanması nedeniyle çalışmalarını durdurduğunu açıkladı.

Krasnodar Valisi Venyamin Kondratyev, Azak Denizi kıyısındaki Yeysk kasabasında 2’si çocuk olmak üzere 3 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiğini açıkladı.

Sivastopol’da ise bir İHA’nın şehir içi otobüse isabet etmesiyle en az 2 kişi hayatını kaybetti, 10 kişi yaralandı.

Luhansk’a düzenlenen saldırıda 16 yaşında bir çocuk da dahil olmak üzere 2 kiş hayatını kaybetti, 9 kişi yaralandı.

Saldırıların ardından Vladimir Putin, Ukrayna’nın temel hedefinin Rus ekonomisini sarsmak olduğunu vurgulayarak, “Kiev bunu yaparak, şişeden cini kendisi çıkardı” dedi. Putin ayrıca, “Pandora'nın kutusunu kendileri açtılar. Zaten zor durumda olan hassas ekonomik sektörlerine yönelik yanıtımızı almış oldular” açıklamasında bulundu.

title: Çayırhan madeninde 1 işçinin öldüğü göçük: Gözaltına alınan 9 kişiden 4'ü tutuklandı
content:
Ankara – Beypazarı ilçesi Çayırhan Kömür İşletmeleri’nde 1 işçinin hayatını kaybettiği, 12 işçinin yaralandığı maden ocağındaki göçüğe ilişkin gözaltına alınan 9 kişiden 4’ü tutuklandı. Diğer şüphelilerin işlemlerinin devam ettiği bildirildi.

Hırkatepe Mahallesi’nde bulunan Çayırhan Kömür İşletmeleri’ne ait maden ocağında dün saat 18.00 sıralarında tavan çökmesi meydana geldi. İhbar üzerine bölgeye jandarma, emniyet, itfaiye, AFAD, UMKE ve sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi.

Göçükte Erdi Kahveci isimli işçi hayatını kaybetti. Yaralanan 24 işçi ise Beypazarı ve Ankara’daki hastanelere kaldırıldı. Yaralılardan bazılarının tedavilerinin sürdüğü, 2 işçinin durumunun ağır olduğu belirtildi.

DHA’nın aktardığına göre, Beypazarı Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından başlatılan soruşturma kapsamında maden sahasında sorumlu olduğu belirtilen 9 kişi gözaltına alındı. Gözaltına alınan 9 kişiden 4’ü tutuklandı. Diğer şüphelilerin işlemlerinin devam ettiği bildirildi.

title: Zonguldak'ta 70 Kürt işçiye saldırı: Can güvenliği çağrısı
content:
Şırnak’ın Cizre Silopi ilçelerinden Zonguldak’ın Alaplı ilçesine bağlı Bektaşlı köyüne mevsimlik fındık işçisi olarak giden 70’ten fazla işçi ve ailelerinin iki gündür saldırıya uğradığı belirtildi.

Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) Şırnak milletvekilleri, sosyal medyaya yansıyan görüntüler ve kamuoyunda oluşan kaygılar üzerine açıklama yaptı. Milletvekilleri, işçilerin dün saldırıya uğradığı bilgisinin kendilerine ulaştığını belirtti. İşçilerin bu sabah partiyle iletişime geçmesinin ardından Zonguldak Valiliği ve Alaplı Kaymakamlığı ile görüşmeler gerçekleştirildiği kaydedildi.

Görüşmelerde, saldırıya jandarmanın müdahale ettiği ve işçilerin güvenliğinin sağlandığı bilgisinin paylaşıldığı aktarıldı. Ancak işçilerin akşam saatlerinde tarladan dönüşte yeniden saldırıya uğradığı belirtildi. Açıklamada, kamuoyuna yansıyan görüntülerde jandarmanın olay yerinde bulunmasına rağmen saldırının gerçekleşmesini engelleyemediği ifade edildi. Bunun üzerine Alaplı Kaymakamı ile yeniden görüşüldüğü belirtilen açıklamada, 70’ten fazla işçi ve ailelerinin can güvenliğinin derhal ve etkin biçimde sağlanması gerektiği vurgulandı. Kaymakamlığın ise ailelerin yakın mesafede güvenli bir yere taşınması ya da bulundukları yerde gerekli güvenlik önlemlerinin alınması yönünde çalışma yürüttüğü bilgisi paylaşıldı.

Açıklamada ayrıca saldırıya ilişkin Alaplı Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından adli sürecin başlatıldığı bilgisine yer verildi.

Mevsimlik tarım işçilerinin geçimlerini sağlamak amacıyla yüzlerce kilometre uzaktan Zonguldak’a geldiği belirtilen açıklamada, “Halkımızın can güvenliğinin sağlanması kamu makamlarının sorumluluğundadır” denildi. Milletvekilleri, işçilerin ve ailelerinin can güvenliğinin sağlanması, saldırının tüm yönleriyle soruşturulması ve benzer saldırıların yeniden yaşanmaması için sürecin takipçisi olacaklarını belirtti.

title: Bıçaklı saldırıda yaralanan Yeni Parti Milletvekili Melih Meriç, entübe edildi
content:

content:
Fotoğraf: Habib M'henni/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 4.0

Filistin Devlet Başkan Yardımcısı Hüseyin eş-Şeyh, Ramallah'taki ofisinde gazetecilere yaptığı açıklamada, seçimlerin, özellikle Filistin'in coğrafi ve demografik bütünlüğünü korumak ve Gazze Şeridi'nin Batı Şeria'dan ayrılmasını önlemek gibi ulusal, siyasi ve stratejik nedenlerle "stratejik bir karar" olduğunu ifade etti.

Genel seçimlerin kararlaştırıldığı gibi kasım ayında yapılacağını kaydeden Şeyh, seçimlerin Gazze'de ya da Filistin topraklarının başka herhangi bir noktasında yapılamaması ya da engellenmesi durumunda da B planının hazır olduğunu dile getirdi.

Şeyh, B planının, ulusal uzlaşı yoluyla Filistin Ulusal Konseyinin kurulması olduğunu anlattı.

Hamas'ın seçimlere kendi adıyla katılmayacağına dikkati çeken Şeyh, "siyasi sisteme katılımın, Filistin Kurtuluş Örgütü'nü Filistin halkının tek meşru temsilcisi olarak tanıma ve uluslararası kararlara uymaktan geçtiğini" belirtti.

Öte yandan, Hamas sözcüsü Hazım Kasım yaptığı yazılı açıklamada, seçimlerin zamanında yapılmasının "olumlu bir tutum olduğunu ve Filistin Başkanı Mahmud Abbas'tan da daha önce olduğu gibi seçimlerden geri adım atmamasını beklediklerini" vurguladı.

Kasım, Hamas'ın Filistin ulusal hareketinin merkezinde yer aldığını ve siyaset sahnesinin temel bileşeni olduğunu kaydetmişti.

Hamas, genel seçimlere katılacağını açıklamış ancak bunun mümkün olan en geniş ulusal uzlaşı içinde olacağını ifade etmişti. Hamas'ın diğer Filistinli gruplardan çıkaracağı adaylarla seçime katılması öngörülüyor.

Filistin'de 2021'de yapılması planlanan yasama ve başkanlık seçimleri, İsrail'in Doğu Kudüs'teki Filistinlilerin seçimlere katılımını garantileyen onayı vermemesi gerekçesiyle Abbas tarafından ertelenmiş sonrasında da iptal edilmişti.

Filistin Devlet Başkanı Abbas, 9 Temmuz'da imzaladığı başkanlık kararnamesiyle, 2006'dan bu yana yapılamayan genel seçimler için 28 Kasım 2026 tarihini belirlemişti.

title: Esenler'de freni boşalan hafriyat kamyonu 7 araca çarptı
content:
İstanbul - Esenler'de rampadan ilerlediği sırada freni boşalan hafriyat kamyonu, seyir halindeki araçlara çarptıktan sonra park halindeki araçlara çarparak durabildi. Kazada 7 araçta büyük çapta hasar meydana gelirken, kazada ölen ya da yaralanan olmadı.

Kaza, saat 19.00 sıralarında Tuna Mahallesi Mahmutbey Caddesi'nde meydana geldi. Edinilen bilgilere göre, rampada seyir halinde olan 35 HC 0089 plakalı hafriyat kamyonunun henüz belirlenemeyen bir nedenle freni boşaldı. Sürücüsünün direksiyon hakimiyetini kaybettiği tonlarca ağırlıktaki kamyon, sokakta önüne çıkan ve park halindeki 7 araca çarptı.

Çevredekilerin ihbarı üzerine olay yerine çok sayıda polis ekibi sevk edildi. Kazada yaralanan olmazken, polis ekipleri çevrede geniş güvenlik önlemi aldı. Kaza nedeniyle Mahmutbey Caddesi, geçici bir süre araç trafiğine kapatıldı.

Kazaya karışan ve kullanılamaz hale gelen araçlar, çekicilerle olay yerinden kaldırılmasının ardından, caddedeki trafik akışı yeniden normale döndü.

author: Sara Awad
title: As a Palestinian From Gaza, I Can Study Abroad in Safety, But Never Visit Home
content:
Our ability to study in safety is tied to a feeling of being emotionally trapped, for we are unable to return home.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Since Israel’s war began in Gaza, Palestinian university students have seen their education and futures upended. All universities have been damaged or destroyed, campuses have closed, and around 88,000 students have been deprived of access to higher education, according to Palestinian officials. Friends of Palestinian Universities has reported that nearly 1,400 university students have also been killed.

For some students, obtaining a scholarship abroad is no longer a privilege to have; it is a necessity to reclaim a future interrupted by war. Many European countries and universities have opened their doors for those students, with scholarships and programs offering a chance for survival. Many Palestinians have managed to leave Gaza, but this comes with another kind of suffering: They can study in safety abroad, yet cannot return home to their families.

I paid that price when I left home.

I was evacuated from Gaza to Italy in December 2025 after the war destroyed my university and all of my city. I was fortunate to receive a scholarship that allowed me to continue my bachelor’s degree in Italy. I am safe here, and I have a place to rebuild my future. However, my family is still in Gaza.

This is my first summer away from my homeland. I live in an apartment with international students. In the past weeks, I watched them pack their stuff and book tickets to go home. I watched them leaving in excitement to see their families and friends after an exhausting academic year. But I had to stay behind.

I was afraid to experience that moment, and I wasn’t ready to see my own pain reflected so visibly in front of me.

Leaving Gaza never looked like taking a plane from one country to another. It was more complex, more complicated. Palestinian students do not simply buy a ticket and travel to their destination. They walk into authority proceedings that feel impossible to schedule in a short while. Gaza’s borders are totally controlled by Israel and there is no way to leave Gaza as before through the Rafah border, as Israel has imposed a total blockade on the borders.

Special humanitarian corridors have to be created by the host country, students face visa issues and travel restrictions, and agreements between the governments and Israeli authorities determine whether they can leave from Gaza. Every step has to align before the scholars can leave. And they leave with nothing but phones and identification documents.

These elaborate processes offered a way out but with no promise for a way back in. Freedom was given to us to leave, but something seems hollow about an idea of freedom that means one cannot return home.

Many Palestinian students have been given a chance to continue their path elsewhere in Europe and beyond. Some made it to Ireland, others to France, as well as Spain and other countries. Those students each experience new lifestyles, new language, faces, and unfamiliar surroundings. But we all have the same painful reality of separation from our own family.

I spoke with three students who are living through the same contradictions as I am, but in a very different place and environment. I wanted to understand how this pain weighs on each of us.

Their pain is different but we all share the same trauma of war.

In Ireland, Abubaker Abed, 24, is a journalist and football reporter and commentator from Dair Al Balah, Gaza Strip. He left behind the life he had built in Gaza, along with the places, people and memories he was deeply attached to, in order to save whatever remained of his future.

“It hurts me that I haven’t seen my family for a year and a half. I feel so much pain,” Abed told me.

He does not dream of returning to Gaza for only a holiday or a brief visit. He dreams of going home for good — to sit with his family in their own home, to live beside them without a screen or a border between them, and to feel safe together.

Abed’s suffering is not limited to the summer holiday. He is constantly reminded of his painful circumstances when he sees the freedom of movement enjoyed by other students. “I feel jealous when a colleague mentions a gathering of his family while I cannot even see mine,” he mentioned.

Abed wishes that all Palestinian …

content:
Organized by the Association for Solidarity, Cooperation and Culture of Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER), the condolence gathering for the Kurdistan Freedom Martyrs at Koşuyolu Park in the Rezan (Bağlar) district continued on its second day with a large turnout.


At the condolence site, where photographs of the martyrs were placed on tables alongside carnations, it drew attention that

şemamok

Thousands of people, including visitors from surrounding cities, visited the condolence gathering throughout the day. Young people, mothers, and women entered the site chanting “Şehîd namirin” (“Martyrs never die”) and remained at the condolence site throughout the day.


During the condolence gathering, the slogans “Bijî Serok Apo” (“Long live Leader Apo”) and “Bê Serok jiyan nabe” (“There can be no life without a leader”) were frequently chanted. The second day of the condolence gathering concluded after prayers were recited.

author: Unknown
title: Saturday Mothers demand answers about the fate of Mustafa Mehmet Günkan
content:
The Saturday Mothers gathered in Galatasaray Square for the 1,117th week of their protest, which they have been holding to demand answers about the fate of their loved ones who were forcibly disappeared in state custody and to call for those responsible to be brought to justice.


This week’s protest focused on the fate of Mustafa Mehmet Günkan, who was forcibly disappeared in custody on August 18, 1994. The press statement was read by Yasemin Bektaş.


Stating that Mustafa Mehmet Günkan’s fate has remained unknown for 32 years, Yasemin Bektaş said: “Mehmet Günkan was the headman of Akçayurt village in the Hani district of Diyarbakır. On June 13, 1994, a clash took place near the village. Afterwards, in the early hours of the morning, the gendarmerie (military police) raided Akçayurt and forcibly evacuated the village. Hundreds of people from Akçayurt and surrounding villages were taken to a holding area set up next to the Topçular Gendarmerie Station. Mustafa Mehmet Günkan was among the villagers held there for a week. When Günkan was released a week later, he had been severely tortured. He then traveled to Ankara and appealed to government officials. He also applied to the Human Rights Association (IHD) and spoke about what he had experienced on a television channel.”


‘They tortured me’


Yasemin Bektaş recalled an interview Günkan gave to the

Turkish Daily News

 on August 3, 1994, quoting him as saying:


“The security forces burned down my village. They took me to the Topçular Gendarmerie Station and tortured me. My ribs were broken. They gathered people outside the village and gave them nothing for four days. A total of 430 people from my village have now moved to Adana, Diyarbakır and surrounding villages. We have nothing to eat. They also burned all our crops. I came to Ankara to ask the government for help.”


Bektaş stated that after returning from Ankara, Günkan took steps to enable the villagers to return to their homes and, for this purpose, approached the Hani Topçular Gendarmerie Station.


On August 18, 1994, soldiers told Günkan that a non-commissioned officer named Hakan had summoned him to the Topçular Gendarmerie Station. Günkan subsequently went to the station and, after a while, was taken out of the station building and put aboard a military helicopter.


‘No effective judicial process was carried out’


Yasemin Bektaş stated that Mustafa Mehmet Günkan was never heard from again after that day and his family made numerous appeals for him to be found and for his fate to be disclosed.


Bektaş also recalled that Amnesty International expressed concern for Mustafa Mehmet Günkan’s safety in an Urgent Action issued on September 21, 1994. She continued:


“Amnesty International called on Gendarmerie General Commander Aydın İlter, Interior Minister Nahit Menteşe and State Minister Responsible for Human Rights Azimet Köylüoğlu to take urgent measures to establish Günkan’s whereabouts and to provide information on the results of the investigation. Despite all these appeals, testimonies and calls, no effective judicial process was carried out to uncover the fate of Mustafa Mehmet Günkan or to identify and prosecute those responsible. Günkan’s fate was left in the dark. Those responsible for his disappearance, as well as those who failed to fulfill their obligation to prevent it, were protected by impunity.”


‘We will not stop demanding justice’


Bektaş emphasized that they have continued to ask the same question for 32 years, saying: “No matter how many years pass, we will not stop demanding justice for Mustafa Mehmet Günkan and for all those who have disappeared, nor will we stop reminding the state that it is obliged to act within the rule of law.”


Letter from Günkan’s son read out


Following the press statement, Human Rights Association (IHD) member Nazım Dikbaş read a letter from Mustafa Mehmet Günkan’s son, Heybet Günkan.


In his letter, Heybet Günkan said: “My father, Mehmet Günkan, was the headman of our village in the summer of 1994. He was a public official who was loyal to his state. After our village and surrounding villages were burned, he contacted human rights organizations to draw attention to what had happened, traveled to Ankara and spoke on television about the events. All he did was speak out about the injustice he had suffered and give a voice to his fellow villagers.”


Günkan stated that while his father was returning to his village, he was summoned to the station by the …

author: Ivis García
title: Summer Drought Compounds Longstanding Water Challenges in Puerto Rico
content:
Dry weather has depleted reservoirs, but Puerto Ricans have been dealing with a failing water system for years.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Imagine turning on your kitchen faucet and nothing comes out. Not for an hour, but for two full days. Then the water returns, only to stop again two days later.

That is what more than 180,000 customers in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and six nearby municipalities have been dealing with since Aug. 7, 2026, and officials expect 48-hour rotating outages to continue at least through August.

The official explanation is drought that has depleted the island’s reservoirs. July was the driest month San Juan has recorded in more than 120 years. The Superaqueduct, a large, aging pipe system that carries water to the metro area, also ruptured in June, severely reducing water supplies.

“This situation is out of our hands,” Gov. Jenniffer González said in early August as water rationing began.

But as a professor of urban planning who has spent years studying water in Puerto Rico, I know that a great deal of the problem Puerto Rico is facing has been in someone’s hands. And for many households I’ve spoken with, the announcement changed less for their daily lives than you might expect.

Puerto Ricans have dealt with water-rationing before, including during a drought in 2015 that left 400,000 customers receiving water service every third day, and again in 2020. After Hurricane Maria in 2017, parts of the island went nearly five months without dependable service. The water interruptions never really stopped for many Puerto Ricans after that.

Residents of one San Juan neighborhood counted 123 days of water outages over the 13 months before the latest rolling outages began. Some brought their unwashed laundry to a protest in the capital in August 2026. A community leader in another town told The Associated Press the rolling outages schedule did not mean much, because her neighborhood had been experiencing water outages for several months.

Filling buckets, keeping jugs by the door, checking the faucet each morning — for many Puerto Ricans, that routine was in place long before now.

The government-owned water company, Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority, or PRASA, is responsible for the water system. But no agency publishes how often households lose service, and Puerto Rico has no independent water regulator. Past engineers’ reports for PRASA have counted reported leaks and overflows, but not how many homes were affected. Much of the information about the latest outages has come instead from residents and investigations by the Puerto Rico House and Senate into repeated water interruptions.

Part of Puerto Rico’s water problem is the large amount of water lost between water treatment facilities and customers.

Two aging systems are failing at once: large transmission mains like the Superaqueduct, where a break can cut off an entire city, and roughly 15,000 miles of distribution lines that leak continuously.

This is not a new problem. PRASA lost 267 million of the 513 million gallons it produced each day, close to half, to leaks from pipes before it reached anyone in fiscal year 2024, according to Puerto Rico’s federally appointed Financial Oversight and Management Board, which certifies the utility’s budget. The utility’s fiscal plan includes investing in leak detection, but shows only a 6% reduction in water losses since 2019.

Overall, the costs have been estimated at nearly US$100 million annually in wasted water production and over $200 million in lost revenue.

The island, which has been battered by severe storms and earthquakes in recent years, relies heavily on disaster recovery funds from the Federal Emergency Management Agency and funding from other federal and state agencies for its water system repair work. To secure those funds, it prioritizes projects that FEMA will reimburse — treatment plants, meters and hurricane reconstruction — rather than the thousands of miles of small pipes where most of the water is lost.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has put Puerto Rico’s need for distribution and transmission pipe work at $2.2 billion, far more than the funding it receives for water systems or the amount it gets from customers.

In addition to the outages, water quality problems over the years have created widespread mistrust of Puerto Rico’s water …

author: Qassam Muaddi
title: Israel Targets Water Wells and Farmland, Attacking West Bank’s “Breadbasket”
content:
“The destruction of the agricultural economy in the West Bank is itself the Israeli purpose,” said one expert.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Agriculture in the northern West Bank could be on the verge of disappearing under the weight of Israeli land confiscation and the destruction of water wells. The Atouf area, in the Tubas governorate in the northeastern West Bank, and long known as the region’s “breadbasket,” has been targeted by settler attacks on its water lines. The settler raids complement the Israeli army’s ongoing infrastructure projects in the area, which have plowed through Palestinian farmlands and demolished wells.

For four months, thousands of Palestinian farmers in the Atouf plain have been unable to access water for their crops after settlers began attacking and damaging water lines, according to local residents. In recent weeks, the Israeli army has bulldozed farmland in Atouf as part of a military road project, further damaging water lines in the process. The army has also issued demolition orders for wells on the plain and has already demolished several.

The northern West Bank has been at the center of Israeli military orders and settler activity in recent months after the Israeli government allowed settlers to return to sites where four Israeli settlements had been evacuated in 2005. In a first since the Second Intifada, the Israeli army took over a neighborhood in the city of Jenin for military purposes inside Area A, which is the part of the West Bank that is supposedly under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Palestinian Authority (PA).

Tubas has also seen its share of Israeli raids and settlement expansion, particularly given its strategic location overlooking the northern Jordan Valley. But the destruction of water sources on Tubas’s farmland carries deeper implications for Palestinian life in the area and across the West Bank, reaching beyond the issue of Palestinian geographic continuity and land ownership.

The plain of Atouf is shared between the villages of Atouf and Ras al-Ahmar, both extensions of Tammoun, the administrative center of eastern Tubas. Together, Tammoun, Atouf, and Ras al-Ahmar hold more than 85,000 dunams (8,500 hectares) of farmland, parts of which the Israeli government has confiscated over the years of occupation. As of early this year, some 30,000 dunams of land in Tammoun and its eastern villages were still being farmed by Palestinians, with hundreds of families depending on agriculture in the region.

Sameer Bisharat, former mayor of Tubas, told Mondoweiss that “70 to 80 percent of people in Tammoun and its surroundings depend partially or entirely on farming for their living, especially after Israel revoked working permits.”

“Israeli settlers from the surrounding outposts have been coming and damaging the water lines, emboldened by the fact that the Israeli army had begun building a military road across the plain last year,” Bisharat explained.

Palestinians in Tammoun tried several times to fix the damaged lines, but the Israeli army kept ordering workers to leave the area, Bisharat said. Then, over the past two weeks, the Israeli army began distributing demolition orders for water wells that farmers depend on for irrigation. Last week, it began demolishing several wells in the Atouf plain.

Durgham Muhammad, a full-time farmer in Atouf, owns 400 dunams (40 hectares) of farmland in the Atouf plain, including greenhouses, fields growing several crops, and a water well.

“I produce seasonal crops like wheat, tomatoes, onions, cucumbers, potatoes, lettuce, spinach, and various fruits,” he told Mondoweiss. “Like most farmers here, I sell them to vendors in the vegetable markets of Nablus, Beita, and Qabatia. I hire 30 farmers to help me, and their families depend on this land for their income.”

Muhammad used to irrigate his farm from his own well, with enough left over to sell to other farmers in the plain. But last week, he received a demolition order for the well.

“For the past four months, our work has practically stopped, and we are barely figuring out how to survive financially,” Muhammad noted. Although it has yet to be demolished, he cannot make use of the water well.

“What we are trying to do currently is get as much water as we can from the pipes to irrigate some of the crops and save as much of our produce as possible,” he said …

author: Jon Queally
title: Trump’s 50 Percent Tariffs Take Effect After US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse
content:
Experts warn the two countries may be poised to slip into an escalating trade war.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

That’s how one Canadian journalist described overnight developments between the governments of the US and Canada after trade talks between the two were suspended on Friday night without a deal in place to avoid the imposition of 50% tariffs threatened by President Donald Trump on a wide swath of Canadian goods.

Both nations accused the other of scuttling the deal, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney citing “last-minute changes” by the Trump administration and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer pointing to “new demands and walk backs” by the Canadians.

Asked earlier on Friday if a deal was within reach, Trump responded, “I think so, yeah, we’ll see.” But by late Friday night, it was clear the talks had collapsed entirely as Carney summoned Canada’s representatives back to Ottawa.

In his statement on Friday night, Carney said, “We have recognized from the beginning that America has changed, and that we will not return to our old relationship. Our government understood, before many, that America is altering all its trade relationships. Putting tariffs on its closest allies and charging for access to its vast market.”

The fresh American tariffs and the promise of Canadian counter-tariffs are a significant escalation in the dispute between Canada and the US, two countries once seen as being as close as can be on trade.

Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc met with Greer, his American counterpart, throughout the week in Washington, DC, to try to secure a deal before the administration’s Friday night deadline.

The terms of the tentative deal were not made public, but separate sources have said the agreement would have lowered sectoral tariffs that have been crushing the Canadian aluminum, steel and automobile sectors for months. In return, Carney asked Canadian premiers to consider ending provincial bans on American alcohol.

While Carney said the Canadian government operated to strike “a fair deal that would provide the best access to the US market and greater certainty to Canadian businesses and workers,” ultimately the “progress has not been enough,” leading to the suspension of talks.

Carney noted that the US government under Trump would impose, starting at midnight on Friday, a 50% tariff on roughly $28 billion worth of goods and he vowed that Canada would “match those tariffs dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses.”

With such pain being inflicted on both sides of the border, economist Dean Baker, co-founder of the Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR) in Washington, DC, said Americans will not avoid the sting of higher prices on a variety of consumer goods, which he argues should be recognized as a tax imposed by President Trump’s chaotic trade policy.

“Trump is going to be hitting American consumers with a new round of tax hikes just over two months before the election,” warned Baker.

Peter Armstrong, senior economics reporter for CBC News, said not only would the new tariffs hit “very hard” in the sectors targeted and “be catastrophic for some businesses,” the additional concern that people must understand is that “the collapse in talks” between the US and Canada “might be even worse” due to the breakdown in trust and the new “injection of uncertainty” between two nations that once stood as solid and reliable trading partners.

With no clear sign about when, how, or if talks would resume, Armstrong warned the risk of tit-for-tat retaliation — a spiraling trade war, in other words — remains high. Armstrong said he texted one business leader in Canada to ask “just how bad” things are and the one-word reply was: “Very.”

Peter Armstrong on the collapse of Canada-US trade talks: "There will be books written about what happened tonight." pic.twitter.com/Hcw9nJK4Yl

“The US-Canada trade war is threatening to spiral,” commented Bloomberg’s Josh Wingrove. “Carney is threatening to match tonight’s tariffs dollar-for-dollar; if he does that, a US official is saying Trump will be given options to retaliate again.”

Labor union leaders in Canada expressed support for Carney’s position, but also lamented the looming negative impact the tariffs would have on Canadian industry and workers. As the Toronto Star reports:

Scientists are preserving vital climate-related information amid the Trump administration’s attacks on climate science.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Since June 23, a group of former employees of the communications branch of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) have been busily resurrecting one of the government’s premier educational websites on climate change.

Climate.gov was started in the early 2010s by communicators with NOAA, and for more than a decade it consistently produced high-quality graphics and other charts documenting rising global temperatures, changing rain patterns, drought conditions, El Niño impacts, and other climate-related data. If you were a layperson and wanted to understand the parameters of human-induced global warming, the website rapidly became a go-to spot. By the 2020s, it was logging more than 1 million visitors per month, according to Rebecca Lindsey, a West Virginia-based communications specialist with an undergraduate degree in biochemistry and a master’s degree in journalism who used to work as the site’s lead writer and editor.

In February 2025, as the so-called “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE) purges accelerated, most of the staff and contractors attached to the website, Lindsey included, were fired — part of a NOAA culling that saw the agency’s workforce cut by roughly 600 in the first couple months of the new administration. By May of last year, the website had been officially taken down. Try to access it today and you get redirected to a NOAA site with this Orwellian message:

In compliance with Executive Order 14303 (‘Restoring Gold Standard Science’), the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s June 23, 2025 Memorandum (‘Agency Guidance for Implementing Gold Standard Science in the Conduct & Management of Scientific Activities’), 15 USC § 2904 (“National Climate Program’), 15 USC § 2934 (‘National Global Change Research Plan’), and 33 USC § 893a (‘NOAA Ocean and Atmospheric Science Education Programs’), you have been redirected to NOAA.gov. Future research products previously housed under Climate.gov will be available at NOAA.gov/climate and its affiliate websites.

Calling it “gold standard science” is, of course, something of a stretch; peruse this site and you’ll find no mention of human-induced global warming, no mention of CO2 emissions exacerbating climate change, no mention even that global warming is accelerating.

Lindsey and her colleagues have, however, refused to go quietly into the night. They believe their educational mission was too important for them to simply fold in the face of Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s hostility. “We worked very hard for 15 years to build Climate.gov, and had a relationship with our readers,” Lindsey explained to Truthout. “And we wanted that to continue. We decided too much had been invested and too much was at stake to let it go without a fight.”

A year after Climate.gov’s demise, Lindsey and several of her erstwhile colleagues resurrected the vast majority of its materials. Left out of the mix were only a few data sets, the information from which they are still trying to access, that were removed early in the DOGE purges because they ostensibly violated anti-DEI mandates or because they referred to the Gulf of Mexico despite Trump’s executive order renaming it the Gulf of America. The new, privately run site is Climate.us and it contains a wealth of sophisticated data sets and graphics on the world’s climate. Each week, new parts of the site come online— including, most recently, a blog titled the El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO), recreated just in time to help website visitors grapple with the likely consequences of what is shaping up to be the most powerful El Niño in decades.

Their work has proven to be an inspiration for ex-government employees in a number of other different agencies and branches of government. Former Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) communicators are, Lindsey says, now looking to resurrect climate-related EPA pages that have been taken down; a group called the Public Environmental Data Partners is attempting to rescue specialist environmental monitoring tools — it has some information online, but not yet a fully interactive website. Another group, the Environmental Data and Governance Initiative is working to save specialized …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Se presentó el informe sobre sistema penal y seguridad de la Comisión por la Memoria
content:
La Comisión Provincial por la Memoria (CPM) presentó su 20° Informe Anual, El sistema de la crueldad XX, que realiza en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura de la provincia de Buenos Aires. El diagnóstico denuncia las graves violaciones a los derechos humanos en un sistema penal que crece y se endurece año tras año, la grave crisis de las políticas de niñez y los déficits de las políticas de salud mental.


“Presentamos este informe con la convicción que sostenemos desde el primero: una política de memoria no puede disociarse de las violaciones de derechos humanos del presente”, dijo la directora ejecutiva del organismo, Sandra Raggio, al abrir la mesa de presentación que integró junto a Roberto Cipriano García, Adolfo Pérez Esquivel y Dora Barrancos, presidentes de la institución, y Diana Márquez de Víctimas por la paz y Juan Manuel Irrazabal del Comité Nacional de Prevención de la Tortura como invitados.


“Este informe no tiene buenas noticias -anunció Dora Barrancos-, en el sistema de seguridad persisten deficiencias estructurales que parecen no tener solución de continuidad”. En las cárceles de la Provincia, que hoy tienen casi el doble de personas detenidas en el sistema penal de adultos que hace 10 años, la CPM registró 91.833 hechos de torturas y otras violaciones de derechos, el 16% de ese total fueron hechos de negación o restricción de acceso a la justicia.


“No exageramos: la realidad desborda de violencias estatales que no negamos ni ignoramos, eso es lo que está haciendo el Ministerio Público Fiscal”, denunció Roberto Cipriano al presentar los datos. La provincia de Buenos Aires tiene el sistema de encierro más grande del país: a diciembre de 2025, había 63.934 personas detenidas en cárceles, alcaidías, comisarías y con monitoreo electrónico contra 61.810 del año anterior. La tasa de encarcelamiento en la Provincia duplica la tasa mundial, el número de detenidos crece interanualmente cerca del 5% y hoy es casi el doble que hace 10 años. Esa cantidad de detenciones colapsan el sistema de encierro: A diciembre de 2025, la sobrepoblación en cárceles y alcaidías era del 116%.


Tanto Cipriano como Barrancos explicaron que la prisión preventiva, el juicio abreviado y la escasa aplicación de medidas morigeratorias de la prisión son las herramientas principales en el sostenimiento de la política de encierro de la Provincia. Esto tiene consecuencias claras: a diciembre de 2025, el 47% de las personas alojadas en cárceles y alcaidías estaban detenidas sin condena firme, es decir, siendo inocentes para la justicia. En el caso de las mujeres (56 %) y personas trans (53 %) es peor aun. El juicio abreviado acelera los tiempos de la condena en detrimento de las garantías y derechos procesales: hoy 9 de cada 10 causas se resuelven por este medio. En el otro extremo, desmintiendo el mediático relato de la “puerta giratoria”, la justicia niega 8 de cada 10 pedidos de morigeración de la pena.


“Son momentos muy difíciles para el país, tenemos que tratar de hacer el esfuerzo de reconstruir, seguir andando. Este informe se presenta a 50 años del Golpe, en medio de una devaluación de la democracia”, sumó Pérez Esquivel. “Lo único que crece aquí son las fuerzas policiales para reprimir al pueblo, no para ayudarlo. Mientras los legisladores bajan la edad de imputabilidad. Qué quieren conseguir?”, se preguntó el Nobel de la Paz. Ese crecimiento se hace evidente en la aparición de las nuevas patrullas municipales se conjugan con la policía consolidando la guetización o segregación territorial de las personas pobres que viven o trabajan en la calle.


Durante el último año, también aumentaron los casos de uso letal de la fuerza, fueron 141, una muerte cada 60 horas. La mayoría, 87 casos, fueron cometidos por agentes en actividad pero fuera de servicio defendiendo bienes propios; en 17 de esos casos se trató de policías que mataron mientras trabajaban como choferes de aplicaciones de viaje. Además se registraron 18 muertes durante el momento de la aprehensión.


“Con este diagnóstico no se puede mirar para el otro lado, es abrumador, no deberíamos poder tolerar esto en democracia. La puerta giratoria abre hacia adentro y la pregunta es qué tipo de sociedad estamos formando, porque en los discursos que fomentan la venganza no hay una técnica de seguridad. El punitivismo es una antropología del miedo”, evaluó la abogada y presidenta de Víctimas por la paz Diana Márquez.

author: Unknown
title: Iranian Supreme Court upholds death sentence against Arghavan Fallahi
content:
The Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) reported that the Iranian Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence issued against Arghavan Fallahi.


According to HRANA, Fallahi was sentenced to death in July of this year on the charge of baghi (armed rebellion) by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.


Following Israel’s attack on Evin Prison in June 2025, Fallahi was initially transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison and subsequently to Qarchak Prison in Varamin. She was later transferred back to Evin Prison.


Previously, an informed source told HRANA regarding the political prisoner’s situation: “Following her arrest, Ms. Fallahi spent some time in Wards 209 and 241 of Evin Prison, under the supervision of the Judiciary’s Intelligence Protection Organization. During this period, she was subjected to severe psychological torture, and attempts were made to extract forced confessions from her in connection with the assassinations of two judges, Mohammad Moghiseh and Ali Razini.”


Arghavan Fallahi was arrested by security forces in late January 2025 and transferred to the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, known as Ward 209 of Evin Prison.


Fallahi had previously been arrested alongside her father by security forces in November 2022 and was later transferred to Evin Prison. She was subsequently sentenced by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, to two years in prison on charges of “assembly and collusion” and “propaganda against the regime.”


She was released from Evin Prison after completing her sentence.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish activist Manijeh Khoshnoud sentenced to three months in prison in Iran
content:
58-year-old Kurdish activist Manijeh Khoshnoud from Bukan has been sentenced by Branch 101 of Bukan Criminal Court Two, on the charge of “propaganda against the system,” to three months’ imprisonment. The verdict was communicated to her on August 11, 2026.


Khoshnoud had been detained on May 26, 2026, after security forces entered her family home, without presentation of a judicial warrant, and was transferred for interrogation to a security detention facility in Orumiyeh. In the course of the arrest, security forces also confiscated her laptop, mobile phone, and a number of her books. After 15 days in detention, she was temporarily released on bail of two billion tomans.


Manijeh Khoshnoud had previously been detained in July/August 2024, and had been released on bail following interrogation. In that case, too, she had been sentenced by Branch 101 of Bukan Criminal Court Two, on the charge of “propaganda against the system,” to 10 months of Ta’zir Imprisonment.

title: Bu hafta ne oldu? (22 Ağustos 2026)
content:
Telaşa mahal yok, her şey kontrol altında.

Bu hafta İBB davasının ikinci celsesi başladı.

Duruşmada çapraz sorgusu yapılan itirafçı Muzaffer Beyaz'ın beyanı sırasında savcı ifadeleri ‘beğenmedi’, beyanı bölüp Beyaz’ın tutuklanmasını talep etti.

Hemen o anda. Talep reddedildi, sonra ikinci defa tutuklanması talep edildi.

Bir önceki duruşmada savunması yaptırılmamasına rağmen ‘susma hakkının kullandığı’ varsayılmıştı. Bu defa da mahkeme başkanı ‘Uygun bir arada yaparsın’ dedi.

Yaklaşık 4 buçuk milyon oy alan, memleketin en büyük şehrinin seçilmiş belediye başkanı; kendisinin görevden alınmasına neden olan dosyada ‘uygun bir ara’ savunma yapacak.

Bu hafta o ‘uygun ara’ Süleymancıların kapısını çalmış gibi duruyor.

Şimdi hummalı bir temizliğe girişen iktidar dün böyle değildi elbette.

Süleymancıların kurucusunun torunu AKP’den milletvekiliydi örneğin.

Mersin’de Cumhuriyet Başsavcısı Seman Eskiler' Süleymancıların lideriyle el pençe divan poz veriyordu.

2019’a kadar -bir önceki tarikat lideri döneminde- devam eden ittifak bozulunca...

“Dini hassasiyetlerin istismarına göz yummayacağız!”

Bir yandan da Cumhurbaşkanının başdanışmanı Oktay Saral’ın Furkan Vakfına ilişkin ‘suyunuz ısınıyor’ demesinin hemen ertesi günü, Kuytulculara da operasyon çekildi.

Bir yanda memleketi sarmalayan tarikatlar, öbür yanda çıkar ilişkileri bozulunca operasyona girişen iktidar...

Ne istediniz de vermedik ki gerçekten?

Bir yandan da istediğini bir türlü alamayanlar var.

Bu hafta YKS yerleştirmeleri açıklandı.

Tercih yapanların oranı 2019’dan bu yana en düşük seviyeyi gördü. Son sınıf öğrencilerinin yarısı bile tercih yapmadı.

Özel liseler yerleşme oranında 15 puan fark atarken meslek liselilerin ancak yüzde 15’i lisansa yerleşebildi.

Ancak sanırım eğitim sistemimize ilişkin sorunlar bunlar değil.

Örneğin öğretmenlerin önlük giymesi, velilerin okula randevuyla gelmesi, çerçeve yasanın öğrencilere anlatılması...

Bunlar MEB’in bu hafta okullara gönderdiği genelgeden.

MEB okulların ‘güvenlik sorununu’ öğretmenlere önlük giydirerek çözüyor.

Dedik ya, her şey kontrol altında.

Mesela Aile Bakanlığı ve yargı da el ele ‘müstehcenlik’ avında.

Sıra, Mabel Matiz’e geldi, yeniden.

O sırada bir haftada olanlara bir bakalım:

Antalya’da havaalanı çalışanı bir kadın, Yalova’da Sultan D, Elazığ’da Hasret K, Mardin’de Bedriye Naz erkekler tarafından katledildi.

Enflasyon da kontrol altında örneğin.

Biliyoruz kontrol altında değil gibi duruyor ama aslında öyle.

TÜİK’in bu hafta enflasyon ve batık borç rakamlarını açıkladı.

Halkın enflasyonu yıllık yüzde 31.75 oldu. Ancak örneğin MESS grubunda yer alan motorlu taşıtlar üretiminde enflasyon yüzde 16.36, askeri sanayi üretiminde yüzde 20.67 oldu. Yani size bize 31.75, kalanınki kontrol altında.

author: Unknown
title: Uyku sağlığı için önemli uyarı: Sadece kaç saat uyuduğunuz değil, saati de önemli
content:
Fotoğraf: Andrea Piacquadio/Pexels

Araştırmalar, uyku süresinin yanı sıra yatış ve kalkış saatlerindeki düzenin de sağlık üzerinde etkili olduğunu gösteriyor. Uzmanlar, biyolojik ritmi korumak için düzenli uyku rutinine dikkat edilmesini öneriyor.

Yetişkinler için her gece yaklaşık 7-9 saat uyumanın önemli olduğu genel olarak bilinir. Ancak yayımlanan güncel araştırmalara göre, kaç saat uyuduğunuz kadar ne zaman uyuduğunuz ve ne zaman uyandığınız da genel sağlığınız ve uyku kaliteniz için bir o kadar kritik. Bilim insanları, düzensiz bir uyku programına sahip olmanın, yeterli süre uyusanız bile vücudun biyolojik ritmini bozduğunu ve uzun vadeli sağlık risklerine yol açtığını vurguluyor.

Sadece uyku süresi yeterli değil: Araştırmalar, haftalık ortalama uyku süresini tuttursanız dahi (örneğin bir gün gece 23.00'te, ertesi gün 02.00'de uyumak) uyku düzenindeki tutarsızlığın vücut üzerinde olumsuz etkiler yarattığını gösteriyor.

Uyku düzenliliği: Yakın dönemde yapılan geniş kapsamlı araştırmalar, yatış ve kalkış saatlerindeki istikrarın (uyku düzenliliğinin) genel sağlık ve hatta yaşam süresi üzerinde uyku süresinden daha güçlü bir belirleyici olabileceğini ortaya koyuyor.

Biyolojik saat (sirkadiyen ritim): Yataktan çıkış ve yatağa giriş saatleri sürekli değiştiğinde, vücudun iç saati karmaşık sinyaller alıyor. Bu durum bağışıklık sisteminden metabolizmaya, odaklanma yeteneğinden kalp sağlığına kadar pek çok işlevi olumsuz etkiliyor.

Uzmanlar, uykudan maksimum verim almak ve vücudun doğal ritmini desteklemek için şu adımları öneriyor:

Aynı saatlerde yatıp uyanın: Hafta sonları da dahil olmak üzere her gün benzer saatlerde yatıp uyanmaya özen gösterin.

Yatmadan önce ekranlardan uzak durun: Mavi ışık, vücudun melatonin (uyku hormonu) salgılamasını engelleyerek biyolojik saatin gecikmesine neden olur.

Sabah gün ışığı alın: Sabah uyandıktan kısa bir süre sonra doğal gün ışığına maruz kalmak, vücudun sirkadiyen ritmini sıfırlayarak geceleri daha kolay uykuya dalmanızı sağlar.

author: Unknown
title: Yaz aylarında cilt sağlığı: Güneşten korunurken yapılan 3 hata
content:
Hasan Can Bilici [email protected]

Yaz aylarında cilt sağlığı alışkanlıklarını gözden geçirmek büyük önem taşıyor. Güneşte tamamen güvende olunduğu düşünülse de cilt kanseri riskini artırabilecek bazı yaygın hatalar gözden kaçabiliyor. İşte farkında olmadan yapılan o 3 hata:

Sadece hafifçe sürmek cildi tam olarak korumuyor. Uzmanlar, tüm vücudu kaplayacak şekilde yaklaşık 30 ml (bir shot bardağını dolduracak miktarda) güneş kremi kullanılmasını tavsiye ediyor. Ayrıca koruyuculuğun devam etmesi için kremin her iki saatte bir (yüzme veya terleme durumunda ise daha sık) yenilenmesi gerekiyor.

Güneşten korunmak için sadece açık havada olmak gerekmiyor. Yapılan araştırmalar, insanların cilt kanserine vücutlarının sol tarafında daha sık yakalandığını gösteriyor; bunun en büyük nedeni ise araba kullanırken UV ışınlarına maruz kalınması. Standart pencereler ve araba camları ultraviyole ışınlarının yalnızca bir kısmını engellediği için, araç içindeyken veya pencere kenarında çalışırken de cilt hasara açık hale geliyor.

Bronzlaşmak sanıldığı gibi sağlıklı bir görünüm değil, aksine cildin UV ışınlarına karşı verdiği bir savunma reaksiyonu ve hasar belirtisidir. Dermatologlar bu nedenle "güvenli bronzlaşma" diye bir kavramın bulunmadığını vurguluyor. Yapılan güncel araştırmalar, solaryum kullanımının en tehlikeli cilt kanseri türü olan melanom riskini neredeyse üç kat artırdığını ortaya koyuyor.
