author: anred
title: Alexandra Sabio lleva un año sin ver a su hijo: se lo arrebató el funcionario de Neuquén y militante contra las «falsas denuncias» Claude Staicos
content:
El 20 de agosto de 2025, un grupo de policías y funcionarios judiciales y estatales se metió al jardín de infantes donde asistía M., de 5 años, para arrebatarlo de los brazos de su madre y llevarlo con el progenitor, Claude Staicos. Al calor del fortalecimiento de los discursos sobre las «falsas denuncias» de las mujeres y valiéndose de su cargo como secretario de Prensa de Neuquén, Staicos lleva un año impidiendo que Alexandra Sabio vea a su hijo y que éste vea a su madre, su abuela, sus amigos y todas las personas que componían su entorno hasta entonces. Este jueves se cumple un año y se vence el plazo legal de «cuidado unilateral», con lo cual M. debería volver con su madre.


La razón que esgrimió Staicos para llevarse a M. fue un «impedimento de contacto»: como la madre, supuestamente, no permitía que él viera a su hijo, tanto el funcionario como la Justicia de Neuquén decidieron impedirle el contacto a ella. Sin embargo, meses atrás Sabio fue sobreseida en la causa por impedimento, comprobándose que no obstaculizó las visitas. Saliendo de la versión de Staicos, amplificada en redes sociales por un montón de grupos de «padres contra las falsas denuncias» que militan el silenciamiento de las mujeres, están la verdad de Alexandra y de tantas otras mujeres cuyas hijas e hijos son arrancados por padres violentos. Por @nativa.difusion


Cuando M. estaba por nacer, Sabio tomó la decisión de separarse: Staicos la agredía verbal y físicamente, la controlaba y la degradaba constantemente en uno de los tantos casos de violencia explícita perpetrada por un varón hacia su pareja. Frente a ello, el secretario de Prensa de Rolando Figueroa la secuestró en su casa por varios días junto al bebé, hasta que intervino la policía local.


Desde entonces, se impuso un régimen de cuidado compartido que Staicos incumplió recurrentemente. Sabio documentó periódicamente cómo su expareja se ausentaba de las visitas pautadas con su niño, mientras temía que la amenaza que le había lanzado al separarse se hiciera realidad: que un día le quitaría a M., en venganza «por todo lo que me hiciste». Instrumentar y dañar a un niño para herir a la madre, la definición básica de la violencia vicaria.


Desde ese 20 de agosto, cuando la policía armada se metió en el jardín despertando el repudio de toda la comunidad educativa y la sociedad en general, Alexandra sabe poco y nada de M. y se moviliza para volver a verlo. A partir de hoy, tiene a su favor, además, el argumento del plazo: la orden emitida a la medida de Staicos le otorgaba el cuidado unilateral por un año, período que acaba de vencer. Hoy hay menos motivos aún para mantener al niño separado de su madre.


Durante todo este año, Staicos demostró la eficacia de sus contactos en el Poder Judicial y el Ejecutivo de la provincia que él mismo integra, pero también su peso mediático. Fueron varios los medios que bajaron notas sobre el tema o que directamente se negaron a comunicar el testimonio de Alexandra, lo que se explica teniendo en cuenta que, además de secretario de Prensa, su expareja es dueño de una parte importante de los medios hegemónicos neuquinos.


Asimismo, el miembro del gabinete de Figueroa integra e impulsa grupos activos en las redes y en las calles contra las supuestas falsas denuncias que, contrario a las cifras existentes, buscan instalar que las mujeres denuncian violencia falsamente. Es la misma clase de grupos que integraba el doble femicida Pablo Laurta, con los que simpatizan Agustín Laje y otros tantos del entorno de Javier Milei, y que hacen de empuje a proyectos infundados como el de Carolina Losada.


Las denuncias falsas constituyen menos del 3% de las que ingresan a los sistemas de Justicia, y, dentro de ese universo, la violencia de género ocupa un lugar minoritario: la mayoría tiene que ver con supuestos delitos económicos. En cambio, la subdenuncia sí parece ser un problema real: la Encuesta Nacional de Victimización del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC) de 2017 indica que apenas 12,5% de las violencias sexuales se denuncian.


Mientras tanto, Alexandra Sabio no sólo no recibió justicia por las agresiones ejercidas por Staicos en su contra, sino que sigue impedida de vincularse con su propio hijo en una situación apañada y sostenida por el Gobierno de Neuquén y un sistema judicial misógino, favorable a los hombres que violentan y abusan. author: CMI Argentina
title: Desalojos exprés y represión a comunidades indígenas en todo el país anticipan el modelo de la “Ley de Inviolabilidad”
content:
En las últimas semanas, distintos territorios indígenas del país volvieron a quedar bajo amenaza o directamente fueron escenario de desalojos ejecutados por fuerzas represivas. En los casos de las comunidades mapuche Kinxikew y Melo de Villa La Angostura (Neuquén), la Comunidad Santa Rosa de Humahuaca (Jujuy) y la comunidad Mbya Guaraní de Puente Quemado II de Garuhapé (Misiones), se repite un patrón de intervención estatal y judicial que avanza sobre comunidades. Aunque la llamada “Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada” aún no fue sancionada en Diputados, su media sanción en el Senado ya aparece como telón de fondo de estos procesos. Las comunidades advierten que el endurecimiento del marco legal y la aceleración de los desalojos configuran un escenario donde, en los hechos, se anticipa la aplicación de un modelo que busca facilitar la expulsión de quienes habitan y resguardan los territorios, amparados por la Constitución Nacional, que reconoce la preexistencia étnica y cultural de los pueblos indígenas y la posesión y propiedad comunitaria de las tierras que tradicionalmente ocupan. ¿La nueva legislación que impulsa el gobierno de Javier Milei viene a crear un escenario o, más bien, a darle forma legal a una ofensiva que ya comenzó?


La llamada “Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada” obtuvo media sanción en el Senado el 7 de agosto, con 37 votos a favor y 33 en contra, y ahora debe ser tratada por la Cámara de Diputados. Entre otras modificaciones, el proyecto establece que las acciones de desalojo se tramiten mediante un juicio sumarísimo y contempla la posibilidad de una restitución anticipada del inmueble, cuando “exista verosimilitud del derecho del propietario”.


Aunque la norma todavía no está vigente y espera a su tratamiento final en Diputados, en las últimas semanas distintos desalojos y órdenes de desalojo contra comunidades indígenas permiten advertir un mecanismo que se parece al que el proyecto busca acelerar. Así, en Neuquén, Jujuy y Misiones la propiedad privada aparece como argumento central de procedimientos que avanzan sobre territorios ancestrales reivindicados por las comunidades, amparadas por el artículo 75 inciso 17 de la Constitución Nacional, que reconoce la preexistencia étnica y cultural de los pueblos indígenas y la posesión y propiedad comunitaria de las tierras que tradicionalmente ocupan.


Repasando los últimos casos, el más reciente ocurrió en Neuquén, cuando las comunidades mapuche Kinxikew y Melo sufrieron este miércoles 19 de agosto un desalojo sobre el territorio que resguardan colectivamente desde 2011, ubicado entre los kilómetros 2082 y 2083 de la Ruta Nacional 40, en cercanías de Villa La Angostura. Las comunidades habían alertado inicialmente por un operativo previsto para el 20 de agosto y, posteriormente, denunciaron que podía adelantarse, tras advertir la llegada de efectivos del y de Gendarmería. Finalmente, el desalojo se concretó, en un conflicto que arrastra varios intentos de desalojo y una disputa judicial de larga duración.

Antes, en Humahuaca, Jujuy, el pasado lunes 10 de agosto, un operativo de la Policía provincial desalojó con represión a familias de la Comunidad Santa Rosa. Según las denuncias difundidas tras el procedimiento, hubo más de cien efectivos, balas de goma, mujeres con niños retiradas por la fuerza y ocho personas detenidas. También fueron denunciadas viviendas destruidas durante el operativo.

Las familias desalojadas permanecen actualmente a la intemperie y sin un lugar donde vivir, luego de que las topadoras destruyeran sus viviendas. Ante la falta de respuestas, levantaron precarias carpas y ranchos y buscan refugio entre familiares y vecinos, mientras intentan resolver especialmente la situación de niños, niñas y adultos mayores. La comunidad continúa en permanencia para recuperar el territorio y en estado de alerta frente a nuevos episodios de hostigamiento.

author: Unknown
title: İşçiler Melek Otel önünden seslendi: “Mehmet Ulusoy hakkımızı ver!”
content:
13 aylık ücret, tazminat ve sosyal hakları ödenmeyen Melek Hotels Moda işçileri, otel önünde eylem yaptı. DİSK’e bağlı Dev Turizm-İş’in çağrısıyla düzenlenen eylemde, “Turizm işçisi köle değildir” ve “Melek Otel işçisi yalnız değildir” sloganları atıldı. İşçiler, tüm hakları ödenene kadar mücadeleyi sürdüreceklerini söyledi.

İstanbul Kadıköy’de bulunan Melek Hotels Moda işçileri, ödenmeyen ücretleri, tazminatları ve diğer sosyal hakları için otel önünde bir araya geldi. DİSK’e bağlı Devrimci Turizm İşçileri Sendikası’nın (Dev Turizm-İş) çağrısıyla saat 18.00’de gerçekleştirilen eylemde işçiler, “Mehmet Ulusoy hakkımızı ver!” yazılı dövizler taşıdı.

Eylem boyunca “İşçiler açken patronlara huzur yok!”, “Turizm işçisi köle değildir!” ve “Melek Otel işçisi yalnız değildir!” sloganları atıldı. İşçiler adına yapılan açıklamada, 13 aylık ücret alacakları başta olmak üzere tazminat ve diğer hakların ödenmesi talep edildi.

Melek Hotels Moda işçileri adına açıklamayı Şükran Bozkurt yaptı. Bozkurt, konuşmasına ülkenin farklı yerlerinde süren işçi direnişlerini selamlayarak başladı. BTO-Sen, Bağımsız Maden-İş, Enerji-Sen, Nakliyat-İş ve Birleşik Metal-İş öncülüğünde sürdürülen grev ve direnişlere dayanışma mesajı gönderdi.

Bozkurt, işçilerin yaşadığı ekonomik sıkıntılara dikkat çekerek uzun süredir patron Mehmet Ulusoy tarafından oyalandıklarını ve haklarının ödenmesi için bekletildiklerini söyledi.

“Bu zor yaşam koşullarında, neler yaşadığımızı, nasıl ayakta kalmaya çalıştığımızı anlatmamıza gerek yok. Bütün bu uzun süre içerisinde patron Mehmet Ulusoy tarafından hep oyalandık, bekletildik, atlatıldık” diyen Bozkurt, kendilerine yaşatılan mağduriyete rağmen Ulusoy’un lüks tatil beldeleri ve eğlence mekanlarından paylaşımlar yaptığını belirtti.

“Artık yeter” diyerek Dev Turizm-İş’le birlikte hakları için mücadele etme kararı aldıklarını ifade eden Bozkurt, “Bu mücadelemiz de tüm haklarımızı alıncaya kadar sürecektir!” dedi.

Bozkurt, konuşmasının devamında Mehmet Ulusoy’a doğrudan seslenerek işçilerin haklarını alana kadar mücadele edeceklerini söyledi.

“Artık susmayacağız, beklemeyeceğiz, sesimizi yükselteceğiz” diyen Bozkurt, şöyle konuştu:

“Biz geçim derdiyle boğuşurken sana huzur vermeyeceğiz. Tüm haklarımızı alana kadar iki elimiz senin yakanda olacak Mehmet Ulusoy. Yaptıklarını bütün dünyaya anlatacağız. Nereye gidersen git karşına çıkacağız. Bizden çaldıklarını geri alacağız!”

Eylemde konuşan Dev Turizm-İş Genel Sekreteri Gökhan Aslan ise Melek Otel’de yaşananların turizm sektöründeki genel çalışma koşullarından bağımsız olmadığını söyledi. Aslan, turizm işçilerinin düşük ücretlere, ağır çalışma koşullarına, tacize, mobbinge ve şiddete karşı mücadele etmek zorunda kaldığını belirterek işçileri örgütlenmeye çağırdı.

Turizm sektöründe kuralsızlığın ve hak gasplarının giderek yaygınlaştığını ifade eden Aslan, işçilerin günün sonunda yalnızca daha iyi çalışma koşulları için değil, yaptıkları işin karşılığı olan ücretlerini alabilmek için de mücadele etmek zorunda bırakıldığını söyledi.

Aslan, konuşmasında Melek Otel işçilerinin yaşadığı sorunun sektör açısından daha geniş bir tabloya işaret ettiğini belirterek şöyle konuştu:

“Turizm işkolunda ne yazık ki bu örneklerle çok fazla karşılaşıyoruz. Düşük ücretlerle, ağır çalışma koşullarıyla, mobbing ve tacizle, şiddetle karşı karşıya kalan turizm işçileri, günün sonunda ücretlerini alabilmek için bile mücadele etmek zorunda kalıyor. Melek Otel işçilerinin yaşadığı da bunun bir örneğidir. Burada işçilerin alın teri, emeği ve ödenmeyen ücretleri var.”

Mehmet Ulusoy’a seslenen Aslan, işçilerin emeği üzerinden elde edilen servete dikkat çekerek sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:

“Bugün lüks içinde yaşayabilirsin. Ama o servetin içinde bu işçilerin alın teri var. O zenginliğin içinde bu işçilerin ödenmeyen ücretleri var. Bugün üzerinde oturduğun servet, yıllarca çalışan işçilerin emeği üzerine kuruludur.”

İşçilerin bütün hakları ödenene kadar mücadele edeceklerini vurgulayan Aslan, “İşçi arkadaşlarımızın bütün hakları ödenene kadar bu mücadele sürecek. İşçiler açken size huzur olmayacak!” dedi.

Aslan ayrıca turizm işçilerine çağrıda bulunarak düşük ücretlere, ağır çalışma koşullarına, tacize, mobbinge ve şiddete karşı örgütlü mücadelenin önemini vurguladı.

İstanbul Kadıköy Moda’da faaliyet gösteren Melek Hotels’te çalışan işçiler, uzun süredir ödenmeyen ücret ve diğer işçilik alacakları için mücadele ediyor. Dev Turizm-İş, otelin eski sahibi Mehmet Ulusoy’un işçilere 13 aylık …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: House Democrat Suggests DSA Members in Congress Shouldn’t Get Security Clearances
content:
Nearly all of Rep. Jared Moskowitz’s remarks since his primary win have focused on his disgust for DSA.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Conservative Democrat Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Florida) has been on a rampage against the progressives and the left after winning his primary against a Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member this week — at one point suggesting that democratic socialists elected to Congress shouldn’t be able to get security clearances.

Moskowitz’s first priority after winning his primary on Tuesday night was not to speak about his priorities for his constituents or the importance of beating Donald Trump-allied Republican opponent Scott Singer in the general election, despite the fact that the race is widely expected to be highly competitive. Rather, his first comments were boasts about his win against DSA member Oliver Larkin and taunts against the left more broadly.

“Florida is known for hurricanes, and so the DSA is a disaster area in Florida — and there’s no federal reimbursement coming to help these people,” Moskowitz said in an interview with Politico held moments after he won his primary on Tuesday.

The AIPAC-backed Democrat — one of the most vehemently pro-Israel politicians in the House — said that DSA members who are winning their primaries and will potentially be his colleagues in Congress are “anti-American at their core.”

“People who have said anti-American things and have said things that are pro-Russian and pro-China, should they really get a security clearance?” he said, adding: “Florida is where DSA goes to die.”

There already are current and former DSA members in Congress who have access to sensitive and classified “national security” information by virtue of their office, like Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-New York) and Rashida Tlaib (D-Michigan), as well as politicians who identify as democratic socialist like Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont). Members of their staff would need to obtain such clearances in order to access classified information.

Moskowitz’s rhetoric is profoundly anti-democratic and echoes sentiments from the Trump administration’s fascist campaign of crackdowns on those with left-wing beliefs in the U.S. It came even as a DSA member, state Rep. Angie Nixon, won the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Florida the same day that Moskowitz won his primary — a candidate that, as a Democrat, Moskowitz would typically be expected to support.

In his comments, he also criticized progressive politicians for campaigning with popular streamer Hasan Piker. In criticizing Piker, Moskowitz said, “I’m standing up for the Democratic Party…I’m standing up for all Americans that love this country.” He also suggested, without evidence, that progressives are now trying to hide Piker’s support. “For all those people who thought it was a great idea to campaign with him, as Jay-Z once said, ‘Bring ’em out, bring ’em out.’ They shouldn’t be hiding him now,” he said.

“I’m genuinely concerned for his mental well-being,” Piker told Politico in response. “I think he should stop posting on the internet and focus on defeating the Republican in his newly redistricted congressional seat.”

Moskowitz was so focused on his triumph over DSA and his dislike of Piker that the two topics have dominated almost all of his remarks since his win — including a statement about his victory and interviews with numerous news outlets afterward. His only post on X on election night was a sarcastic post that read, “My condolences to @hasanthehun,” tagging Piker.

During the primary race, local media reported on Moskowitz’s refusal to engage with Larkin in several instances throughout the campaign. He derogatorily called Larkin a “communist” — a line of attack that has been encouraged by Republican strategists in their campaigns against Democrats — and refused to participate in a primary debate against the democratic socialist — a move that invited Republicans to label him as “cowardly.” Moskowitz has also baselessly accused Larkin and Piker of opposing him because he is Jewish.

author: Frida Garza
title: Frontline Farmerworkers Are Most at Risk From the Cyclospora Outbreak
content:
A farm laborer advocate discusses why public responses must avoid further stigmatizing this vulnerable workforce.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Earlier this summer, when the news broke about an outbreak of cyclosporiasis — a parasitic infection that results in abdominal distress and is passed on via food or water that has been contaminated by human fecal matter — spreading across the country, one question came up again and again: How did human poop end up in our food system?

On the internet, speculation abounded. Could farmworkers be sick themselves? Were they relieving themselves in the field because their working conditions didn’t ensure proper access to bathrooms? Or did this have something to do with farmworkers, often migrant men and women, being deported? Perhaps, all along, they were the ones protecting consumers from foodborne illnesses. Posts about the outbreak, centering farm labor as either the potential source of disease or as stewards of the food supply, began to crop up.

But these theories are all either incomplete or misguided, say food safety experts. The scale of this summer’s outbreak — the biggest known in U.S. history — suggests widespread contamination of the food supply. For that, they say, we should look closely at irrigation water and other water that’s used in our highly industrialized, global food supply chain.

For example, in some agricultural regions, sewage water is treated and then reused to irrigate crops. This practice is common in areas experiencing drought or water stress, and it is legal in nearly half of U.S. states. When water in such a system is not treated to the highest standards, complications can occur. Whether contaminated water contributed to the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak this year is unknown. Public health authorities are still investigating to understand the source of the current outbreak; so far, one company, Taylor Farms, has been associated with the outbreak in multiple states. Last week, the FDA announced it had begun an on-site inspection at a Taylor Farms facility in central Mexico.

Meanwhile, the increase in scrutiny on farmworkers only compounds the other stresses that the population is facing, said Amy Liebman, chief program officer at the Migrant Clinicians Network, an organization connecting farm laborers to health care. In the following conversation, which has been edited for length and clarity, Liebman discusses the risks of further stigmatizing this vulnerable workforce at a time of mass deportation, public health breakdowns, and climate change.

It feels like there are potential risks of further stigmatizing immigrant farmworkers based on how we talk about this infectious disease. What are the things the public should know about this issue, and what are the most accurate, responsible ways to talk about it?

Amy Liebman: Basically, I think we have a disconnect between what we expect and demand in terms of a safe food supply and how we actually do that. I am concerned that farmworkers are actually more vulnerable to getting the disease than they are likely to be the source of the outbreak.

Whenever there’s any infectious disease outbreak, we’re concerned about people living in close quarters. So recognizing that the living and working conditions are often one and the same for farmworkers, that’s really important. There’s other issues that might come up with farmworkers, such as the number of bathrooms or where their well water comes from.

There’s a lot of unknowns — it’s very hard to understand the source because of the amount of time that it takes to trace infections. But it does seem more likely that this involved some kind of contamination from water. So it’s important to understand the overall environment in which our food is grown and processed — from the harvesting to the processing and the selling and finally to being put on our tables. And understand that there’s all kinds of room for contamination in that process.

What are things your organization has been hearing from clinicians in the field? When migrant farmworkers get sick with cyclosporiasis, are they seeking care?

So there’s multiple things going on. We have the dismantling of our public health system. We really depended on our frontline folks at health departments trying to figure this out without huge direction or support, at least initially, from the CDC. That piece impacts everybody. Everyone is impacted by …

title: Jubilados marcharon al Ministerio de Salud: “Nos están matando”
content:

title: Five children injured in landmine explosion in Til Temir
content:
The five children, who were herding sheep in the area around the village of Til Hemam, west of Til Temir, were injured in the landmine explosion.


The injured children were taken to Habur Hospital in Til Temir, where they received emergency treatment. The two seriously injured children, Îbrahîm Ebducasim (17) and Muhamed Xelef (12), were transferred to hospitals in Hesekê.


Ebdurehman Mehmûd (14) sustained an injury to his right foot; Ûsama Hesen Seqir (13) was injured in his right knee and abdomen; and Leys Eseed Şihaze (10) sustained an injury to his right foot.

author: Jake Johnson
title: Israeli Settlers Have Displaced 107 Palestinian West Bank Communities Since 2023
content:
A new report by Human Rights Watch details how the Israeli government has directly facilitated displacement.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Intensifying violence by government-backed Israeli settlers in the illegally occupied West Bank is fueling the mass displacement and erasure of entire Palestinian communities, according to a report published Thursday by Human Rights Watch.

HRW pointed with alarm to United Nations data showing that the average number of settler attacks per day in the West Bank has risen to the highest level on record as the far-right Israeli government, led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, continues to expand settlements in open defiance of international law.

The leading human rights group’s new report estimates that Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank has “fully or partially displaced 107 communities,” comprised of nearly 6,000 Palestinians, since January 2023. The escalating displacement in the West Bank comes amid Israel’s ongoing genocidal assault on the Gaza Strip.

“The Israeli government and the settlers share the same goal of maximum land and minimum Palestinians, with the authorities not only failing to stop settler violence, but actively enabling it,” Sarah Sanbar, acting Israel and Palestine researcher at HRW, said in a statement. “Settlers shoot, attack, and expel Palestinians from their land, and the state provides the weapons, the legal cover, and the budget to do it.”

HRW’s report was released days after the Israeli government published a new tender for the construction of more than 1,200 housing units in the West Bank. The anti-occupation group Peace Now noted that the bidding period for companies to build the units closes a week before Israel’s elections.

“Building in E1 will ruin the possibility of reaching an end to the conflict and a peace arrangement based on two states,” said Peace Now. “The government is trying to sign contracts with contractors before the elections so that it will be much harder for the next government to cancel the construction.”

HRW warned that companies seeking a role in constructing the new housing units are “bidding on complicity in a war crime.”

For its report on settler violence, HRW interviewed 20 witnesses and reviewed video footage of attacks, which have included physical assaults, sexual violence, property destruction, theft, and killings — often carried out alongside Israeli soldiers. HRW noted that Israel’s National Security Ministry has “formed civilian ‘rapid response squads’ in settlements” and given them “special policing powers, uniforms, and weapons.”

“I have known war in this region for all my life, but never like this,” said Um Muhammad Muammar, a 72-year-old resident of Qaryut whose two sons were killed by Israeli settlers. “My sons’ children are now fatherless; their wives are now widows. What more can we say?”

With the support of Israel’s government, settlers have established 65 new outposts in the West Bank this year alone. “Israeli organizations Kerem Navot and PeaceNow reported in July that these outposts currently effectively control more than 1 million dunams (100,000 hectares) of land — approximately 18% of the West Bank — four times what they controlled before the current government took office,” HRW observed.

“The impunity Israeli authorities accord settlers stems directly from the free pass Israel’s allies and donors have granted it,” said Sanbar. “Accountability starts with the settlers committing crimes but doesn’t end there. Israel and the governments that give it a blank check share responsibility and should be held to account.”

author: Andrea
title: ᐃᓚᒌᑦ ᕿᓂᖅᐳᑦ ᑭᐅᔾᔪᑎᓂᑦ ᑐᖁᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐃᕗᔾᔨᕕᖕᒥ ᓄᑲᑉᐱᐊᒥᒃ
content:
For the English version of this story, please see

Community mourns 4-year-old Ivujivik boy as family seeks answers

.


ᐃᕗᔾᔨᕕᖕᒥᐅᑦ ᑲᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 13−ᒥ ᐃᓗᐃᓪᓚᕿᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᑎᓴᒪᓂᒃ-ᐅᑭᐅᓕᒃ ᔫᓯ ᐳᓪᓚᔮᑦᒥᑦ ᐃᓚᖏᑦ ᕿᓂᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᑭᐅᔾᔪᑎᓂᑦ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐸᖅᑭᔭᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐱᓚᐅᖅᑕᖓᓂ ᑐᖁᓚᐅᙱᓐᓂᖓᓂ.


ᐳᓪᓚᔮᑦ ᐃᓗᕕᖅᓯᐅᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓯᒪᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ 1 ᐅᓐᓄᓴᒃᑯᑦ, ᐊᓈᓇᑦᑎᐊᖓ, ᐋᓂ ᒪᖏᐅᖅ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓄᓇᓖᑦ ᕙᐃᔅᐳᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᙵᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


ᒪᖏᐅᖅ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᐃᕐᙳᑕᖓᑕ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᖓᓂ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᓄᓇᓖᑦ ᕙᐃᔅᐳᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᙵᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑐᑯᕝᖁᓚᐅᙱᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


ᔪᓚᐃ 31−ᒥ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓄᑲᑉᐱᐊᖅ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖏᓐᓇᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᓈᖓᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᓂᕆᓚᐅᑦᑎᐊᕐᓇᓂ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᕈᓯᐅᑉ ᐅᖓᑖᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓚᒌᑦ ᕿᓃᓐᓇᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᔪᒪᓂᕐᒧᑦ.


ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐃᓗᐊᖅᓴᐃᔨᖏᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᔾᔨᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᐃᓚᒌᖑᔪᓂ ᑐᓂᔭᐅᖁᔭᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᓂᐊᖁᖅᓯᐅᑎᓂ ᐋᑦᕕᐅᓪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑕᐃᓕᓈᓪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓈᒻᒪᒃᑐᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᑦᑎᐊᓚᐅᙱᓚᖅ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᓇᒍ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑎᒋᔭᐅᔪᓂ.


ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᖅ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᔅᓯᒐᓚᒃᑎᒍᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᒋᐊᕋᓱᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᔪᓂ ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᐱᓚᐅᙱᓚᑦ ᑭᐅᔭᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


ᓄᓇᕕᖕᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᖅᑏᑦ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᖃᕋᓴᐅᔭᑎᒍᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒃᑯᑦ ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᖅ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᕆᔨᕐᖁᓐᓄᑦ ᐸᓖᓰᑦ ᑭᐅᓚᐅᕐᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 1−ᒥ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑕᐅᔪᒪᓂᐅᔪᒧᑦ ᐅᖃᓗᖕᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᔾᔪᑎᓕᖕᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᒪᙱᑦᑐᒥ ᑎᓴᒪᓂ-ᐅᑭᐅᓕᖕᒧᑦ ᐊᖏᕐᕋᕆᔭᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᕗᔾᔨᕕᖕᒥ.


ᑐᐊᕕᕐᓇᖅᑐᒥ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᐃᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᖅᑎᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᓂ ᐅᓯᑲᑦᑕᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᓱᕈᓯᕐᒥ ᐃᓅᓕᑦᓯᕕᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᒃ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᑭᐅᖕᒪᑕ, ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᑉ ᑐᖓᓕᐊ ᓵᓐ ᓛᖕᓯᑐᕇᑦ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


ᐅᖃᐅᓯᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐃᓅᓕᑦᓯᕕᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᒃ ᐃᑭᐊᖅᑭᕕᖓᓂ, ᐃᕗᔾᔨᕕᒃ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖑᔪᒥ ᐃᓗᐊᖅᓴᐃᔨᖃᖅᐳᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᖕᒥ ᐃᓗᐊᖅᓴᐃᔨᖃᖅᐳᑦ ᑕᐃᑲᓂ.


ᑭᖑᓂᐊᒍᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 9−ᒥ, ᒪᖏᐅᖅ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᔫᓯ ᑐᖁᓚᐅᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐸᓯᒃᖠᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᓗᐊᖅᓴᐃᔩᑦ ᐃᕗᔾᔨᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐳᕕᖕᓂᖅᑑᒥ ᐅᒃᐱᕈᓱᓚᐅᙱᓐᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐱᕐᔪᐊᖑᓂᖓᓂ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ.


ᑕᐃᒃᑯᐊ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑕᐅᔪᑦ ᑎᑭᐅᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᓄᕐᓂᖅᓴᓄᑦ ᐅᖃᓕᒫᖅᑎᓄᑦ ᑲᑕᔾᔭᖅᑎ ᓰᓇ ᓄᕗᓕᙵ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᕐᒪᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᖓᓂ ᐳᓪᓚᔮᑦ ᑐᖁᓂᖓᓂ, ᐃᓚᖃᖅᑐᒥ GoFundMe ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᐱᕈᖅᓴᐃᓇᓱᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐃᓚᖏᓐᓄᑦ.


ᐃᓅᖃᑎᒌᖕᓄᑦ ᓯᐊᒻᒪᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᖓ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐅᖓᓯᒃᑐᒥᙶᖅᑐᓂ ᐃᒃᐱᒍᓱᖕᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᕿᒃᓵᖕᓇᖅᑐᒃᑰᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᑖᙳᕆᐊᖅᑐᒥ ᐅᖃᓪᓚᖕᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐸᖅᑭᔭᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᓄᓇᓕᐅᔪᓄᑦ.


ᒐᕙᒪᑐᖃᒃᑯᑦ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᒥᓂᔅᑕᖓ ᒫᓐᑎ ᒑᓪ− ᒫᔅᑎ, ᓕᐳᕈᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᓇᑕᐅᑉ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᖅᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐊᐱᑎᐱ—ᓯᕿᓂᕐᒥᐅᑦ—ᓄᓇᕕᒃ—ᐄᔭᐅ, ᑐᓂᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᐃᒃᐱᒍᓱᖕᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᕿᒃᓵᖕᓇᖅᑐᒃᑰᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 12−ᒥ ᐳᓪᓚᔮᑦ ᐃᓚᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐅᕐᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᕙᐃᔅᐳᒃᑯᑦ.


“ᐆᒻᒪᑎᒃᑯᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᕐᓇᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑐᓴᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᑎᓴᒪᓂ−ᐅᑭᐅᓕᖕᒥ ᓄᑲᑉᐱᐊᕐᒥ ᐃᕗᔾᔨᕕᖕᒥ, ᓂᕈᐊᖅᑕᐅᕝᕕᒋᔭᓐᓂ,” ᒑᓪ-ᒫᔅᑎ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ.


“ᓂᕆᐅᒃᐳᒍᑦ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑯᐸᐃᖕᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᐃᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᓂ ᐃᓚᐅᔪᓂ ᑭᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐆᒥᖓ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᓪᓚᕆᐅᓂᖅᐹᖑᔪᒥ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᓯᓂᕐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᐅᔪᖅ ᑐᓂᓯᔪᓐᓇᕐᓂᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᑭᐅᔾᔪᑎᓂ ᐃᓚᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓄᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᓗᑎᒡᓗ ᐱᑎᑦᑎᑦᑕᐃᓕᒪᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᓯᕗᓂᒃᓴᒥ ᐱᓂᕐᓗᒡᔪᐊᕐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂᖓᓂ.”


ᐃᓅᓕᑦᓯᕕᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓄᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓄᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᑐᓂᓯᓚᐅᖅᐳᑦ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐊᖑᔪᒥ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 12−ᒥ, ᐅᖃᐅᓯᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᖃᔅᓯᒐᓚᖕᓂ ᕿᒥᕐᕈᔭᐅᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑕᐅᓯᒪᕗᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᓱᕈᓯᐅᑉ ᑐᖁᓂᖓᓄᑦ.


ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᐅᑉ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᑐᑭᒧᐊᒃᑎᑦᑎᔨᖏᑦ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᓯᒪᕗᑦ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᙱᑦᑐᓂᒃ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᕿᒥᕐᕈᔭᐅᓂᖓᓂ. ᑐᖁᖓᔪᓕᕆᔨ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑎᑦᑎᓯᒪᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐊᖅ ᐅᖃᖅᓯᒪᕗᖅ.


ᑐᖁᖓᔪᓕᕆᔨᐅᑉ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᖓ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓲᖑᔪᒥ ᑐᖁᔪᖃᕌᖓᑦ ᐅᕘᓇ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᓯᕆᕐᔪᐊᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ, ᑐᑭᓯᓇᙱᑦᑐᒥ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᑲᒪᑦᑎᐊᙱᑦᑐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᓂ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓲᖑᕗᖅ ᑕᖅᑭᓂᑦ 6−ᓂ 12−ᓄᑦ, ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᑯᐸᐃᖕᒥ ᑐᖁᖓᔪᓕᕆᔨᒧᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᕕᖓᓂ ᐅᖃᖅᑎᐅᔪᒥ ᔭᐃᒃ ᓚᒧᑕ ᒍᕋᓈᑐ ᖃᕋᓴᐅᔭᑎᒍᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓄᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᖏᑕ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᖃᐱᓘᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᑲᒥᓴᓇᖓ ᐃᓚᐅᖃᑕᐅᒋᕗᖅ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᒻᒥᒃᑰᖅᑐᒥ ᐃᓅᓕᓴᐃᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑎᐅᔪᒥ ᓯᓚᑖᓂ ᐃᓅᓕᑦᓯᕕᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕕᖓᓂ ᕿᒥᕐᕈᓂᐊᖅᐳᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓐᓂᐅᔪᒥ.


Québec solidaire, ᑲᓇᑕᐅᑉ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᖓᓂ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕐᔪᐊᓄᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕐᔪᐊᖑᔪᓂ, ᖃᐃᖁᔨᓂᖃᖅᐳᖅ ᑯᐸᐃᖕᒥ ᓱᕈᓯᓄᑦ ᐱᔪᓐᓇᕐᓂᕆᔭᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᖃᓄᐃᙱᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᑲᒥᓴᓇᖓᓂ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᒨᓯᐅᑉ ᑐᖁᓂᖓᓂ.


“ᐅᓇ, ᓱᓕᒃᑲᓐᓂᖅ, ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᒍᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᒥᒃ ᖃᓄᐃᑦᑑᓂᖏᑦ ᐱᔾᔪᑎᒋᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᐊᑭᕋᖅᑐᐃᓂᐅᒍᓂ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᕐᓇᙱᑦᑐᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥ−ᐸᖅᑭᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᐅᔪᒥ, ᑐᑭᓯᓇᑦᑎᐊᖅᑐᒥ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᖅᐳᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᒪᓕᒃᑐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕐᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᔪᒥ,” ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕐᔪᐊᑦ ᐅᖃᖅᑎᖓ ᓲᓪ ᓴᓇᑎ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᖅᐳᖅ ᐋᒍᔅᑎ 13−ᒥ ᐅᐃᕖᑎᑐᑦ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᓕᐊᖑᔪᒥ.

author: Wolfgang
title: Solidaritätskreis fordert Rücknahme der Abmahnung gegen IGM-Vertrauensmann Jörn Kleffel durch VW Nutzfahrzeuge in Hannover
content:
Dossier


„Ihr habt sicher aus dem Frühjahr unsere Aktivitäten zur Unterstützung des Kollegen und IGM-Vertrauensmanns Jörn Kleffel im Kampf um die Rücknahme seiner Abmahnung durch VW Nutzfahrzeuge in Erinnerung. Es gab eine ganze Reihe von Solidaritätsbekundungen aus gewerkschaftlichen Kreisen sowie ca. 450 Unterschriften für diese Forderung. Nun ist der Zeitpunkt der Hauptverhandlung seiner Klage gegen VWN vor dem Arbeitsgericht herangerückt und wir möchten Euch alle um eine möglichst breite Beteiligung/Besuch bei diesem Prozess bitten. Dieses Verfahren wird ein wichtiges Signal setzen, wie kritische, fortschrittliche und linke KollegInnen sich im Kampf um die berechtigen Interessen der Arbeiter in einem Betrieb artikulieren können und dass auch Konzerne wie Volkswagen nicht glauben brauchen, mit dreister Einschüchterung jeden Kritiker mundtot machen zu können. Wir würden uns deshalb sehr über Deinen/Euren Besuch bei diesem Prozesstermin freuen. Er findet statt am Dienstag, 21. August 2012 um 11.15 Uhr am Arbeitsgericht Hannover, Ellernstrasse 42. Wir treffen uns bereits ab 10.45 Uhr vor dem Gericht, um Jörn den Rücken zu stärken

“ Email an die Redaktion des LabourNet Germany vom 10.08.2012, mit der „alles“ begann:


Jörn Kleffel verliert die Klage gegen die Abmahnung durch VW vor dem Landesarbeitsgericht in Hannover, eine Revision vor dem Bundesarbeitsgericht wird nicht zugelassen


„

Am 19. August fand in zweiter Instanz vor dem Landesarbeitsgericht der Prozess des IG-Metall-Vertrauensmanns Jörn Kleffel gegen VW statt. Um das Ergebnis gleich vorwegzunehmen – so, wie es Richter Dr. Rinck quasi schon mit der Begrüßung tat: Die Klage gegen die Abmahnung wurde abgewiesen. Eine Revision vor dem Bundesarbeitsgericht wird nicht zugelassen. (…)


Zur Kundgebung vor dem Prozess kamen etwa 25 Unterstützer: Familienangehörige, Freunde, VW-Kollegen und Vertreter der Widerstandskomitees gegen die Werksschließungen aus Hannover und Braunschweig, Frauen vom Frauenverband Courage sowie Vertreter von Yuna – Demokratische Jugend und der MLPD. RTL Nord und die Hannoversche Allgemeine Zeitung berichteten. (…) Der Richter legte die Situation von 2024 ausführlich dar und konnte sich sogar ein Stück weit in die damalige Stimmung der Kollegen hineinversetzen: „Es steht außer Frage, dass Sie und Ihre Kollegen in so einer Situation emotional aufgewühlt waren.“ Er stimmte auch der Argumentation von Jörn Kleffel und seinem Anwalt Frank Stierlin zu, dass gewerkschaftliche Vertrauensleute „das Recht und sogar die Pflicht haben, ihre Kollegen über wichtige Entwicklungen zu informieren“.


Der Streitpunkt sei jedoch klar: Das Koalitionsrecht der Arbeiter, also ihr Recht auf gewerkschaftliche Betätigung im Betrieb, müsse gegen das Eigentumsrecht von VW und dessen Recht auf die vereinbarte Arbeitsleistung abgewogen werden – sprich gegen das Recht auf Ausbeutung der Arbeitskraft der VW-Arbeiter. Mit dem Bandstopp habe Jörn Kleffel „in einem Akt der Eigenmacht“ und „ohne Not“ entschieden, die Interessen der Arbeiter über die von VW zu stellen. Das sei nicht zu akzeptieren. Das Recht stehe hier eindeutig auf Seiten von VW. Jörn Kleffel hätte seine Kollegen schließlich auch in der Pause informieren können

…“

Korrespondenz aus Hannover vom 20.08.2026 bei den Rote-Fahne-News


 („Politisches Urteil zur Unterdrückung von Streiks“)


Er hielt das Band für drei Minuten an: Klage des IGM-Vertrauensmannes Jörn Kleffel gegen VW gegen seine Abmahnung vom Arbeitsgericht Hannover abgelehnt


„Es geht ums Prinzip“ – VW zeigt sein wahres Gesicht bei der gerichtlichen Bestätigung der Abmahnung


„

Auch wenn die Arbeiter bei VW in einer Situation sind, in der akut ihre Arbeitsplätze

gefährdet sind, dürfen sie nicht zur Beratung ihrer Situation das Band anhalten, auch

nicht kurz. Die Sorgen und Ängste der Arbeiter um ihre Zukunft und die Zukunft ih

rer Familien dürfen den reibungslosen Produktionsprozess nicht stören. So urteilte

das Arbeitsgericht Hannover am 25.11. zu der Klage des IGM-Vertrauensmannes Jörn

Kleffel gegen VW gegen seine Abmahnung. (…) Das Gericht entschied am Dienstag, die Abmahnung bleibt bestehen. Davor hatten

VW und das Gericht einen „Kompromiß“ vorgeschlagen: „Rücknahme der berechtig

ten Abmahnung“ zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt. Damit hätte Jörn zugestimmt, dass sein Ver

halten eine „eine vertragliche Pflichtverletzung“ gewesen sei. Darauf ließ Jörn sich

nicht ein.

title: I see you replacing remembrance of ancestors for reverence, inserting a hierarchy that wasn’t there
content:
I’m starting to think all humans are fundamentally spiritual, and just like every other human need, if you repress it, it’ll just express itself covertly in fucked up ways

You have a human need to process the world through narrative, to share meaning with community, to have a path to redemption, to ritualize your uncertainties, to connect with inanimate objects

If you cross your arms and deny yourself this expression, all of those psychological needs will get funneled into a spirituality most unpleasant, like conspiracy rabbit holes and unhealthy obsessions with fandom

If you care about your morality, then you should care how your spiritual needs manifest and ensure they’re being met and fulfilled, lest you become one of those people willing to crusade for your discord mod

Being a leftist queer doesn’t isolate you from this, you’re not immune from latent cultural Christianity (I say as a leftist queer)

Intentionally design your spirituality!

Or just use skepticism and critical thinking skills? I guess it depends how you define spirituality but if that involves “believing in things they aren’t real” then Jo, that’s not a necessary human experience. The fuck makes you think we need a path to redemption? Redemption from what? And toughest purpose?

Sure but by that same token human beings can’t live life in an entirely scientifically functional way. I do still get flutters in my chest when I look up at the sunlight through the bottom of a treetop, and I think letting yourself get swept up in that with a little bit of philosophical wish-washing is good for you

Again how do we define spirituality here? Is it just having rituals or does it require belief in unreal things? We need to be clear on terms here to begin with. Does having a fandom count? Just having moral principals we stick to? Is it compatible with a rationalist and materialist worldview?

I mean “unreal” perhaps in the sense that our emotions and reactions cannot be perfectly scientifically explained.

You can’t be unflinchingly rational about all things at all times, sounds like an awful boring way to love. Gotta have some whimsy and wonder someplace

Why do you assume whimsey and wonder are mutually exclusive to rationality? Wonder is what leads to research and further understanding.

You still seem to be affected by the cultural stereotype of a joyless atheist.

I *am* an atheist, I just choose not to be entirely, perfectly rational all the time

Atheists can still be affected by cultural Christianity, including internal used atheist stereotypes.

I fully admit to taking irrational actions such as my fear of wasps but I still recognize these as irrational.

I try to view the world as rationally as I’m able, knowing that my phobia is an irrational fear response caused by chemical reactions in the brain doesn’t “ruin the whimsey” or whatever.

Sure but you still have to let yourself FEEL things without explaining them away right? I know that my wonder is a chemical reaction but that’s not what I’m thinking about as it’s happening

Why do you believe explaining something somehow ruins it? Also to get back to the original discussion, are we considering “having emotions” as the same as spirituality?

Your internal experience is rational. There is no such thing as an “irrational emotion.”

Emotions are our baseline way of processing the world around us, and they happen regardless of whether or not that emotion is proportional or makes sense to an outside viewer. Therapists say “your feelings are valid” because they literally are, and that includes even the more pernicious emotions. Saying an emotion is irrational is like saying the way your eyes filter through light is irrational. Emotions aren’t bound to rationality.

That doesn’t mean every single emotion will be pleasant or healthy, but they do have to be acknowledged and honored. Your fear of bugs should be honored. Your awe at sunlight through treetops should be honored. Those things don’t require a relationship to reason and logic because they’re not involved in the brain’s higher reasoning. Emotions and fears are not actions.

Further, we can act rationally on an unverified worldview. We can be acting rationally and choosing to engage with spirituality for our personal well-being. Just as an example, it’s rational to ward and protect your house if you believe it can be negatively influenced by spirits. You can say believing in spirits is irrational, but belief actually makes up a surprisingly …

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicados del Centro de  Estudiantes y la Dirección del Liceo Rayen Mapu, frente a procedimiento policial al interior del establecimiento que obligó a estudiantes a desnudarse frente a sus compañeros
content:
«COMUNICADO DEL CENTRO DE ESTUDIANTES


Sobre situación ocurrida con estudiantes de 2° medio.


Como Centro de Estudiantes del Liceo Rayen Mapu, queremos informar a nuestra comunidad educativa sobre una situación que nos fue comunicada por estudiantes de 2′ medio y que consideramos de especial gravedad.


De acuerdo con el relato entregado por nuestros compañeros y compañeras, durante una jornada de clases se produjo la pérdida de un teléfono celular perteneciente a una estudiante del curso. A partir de esta situación, dos estudiantes fueron señalados como principales sospechosos, sin que, según lo informado por ellos, se les hubiera comunicado la existencia de antecedentes concretos que justificaran dicha acusación.


La situación adquiere especial preocupación porque, según el relato recibido, fue la docente a cargo de la clase quien identificó a estos estudiantes como sospechosos y posteriormente solicitó la presencia de Carabineros en el establecimiento.


Antes de realizar una investigación que permitiera establecer qué había ocurrido realmente,cuatro estudiantes habrían sido retenidos y se les habría impedido salir al recreo.


Como Centro de Estudiantes, consideramos necesario cuestionar esta actuación, ya que una sospecha no puede transformarse automáticamente en una acusación ni justificar que determinados estudiantes sean tratadoscomo responsables de un hecho que aún no ha sido esclarecido.


Posteriormente, una vez que los estudiantes se encontraban nuevamente en la sala, funcionarios de Carabineros habrían realizado un procedimiento dirigido solamente a dos de ellos, frente al resto de sus compañeros y compañieras.


La situación que más nos preocupa corresponde al procedimiento realizado sobre los estudiantes. Según lo informado, a uno de ellos se le habría solicitado quitarse el polerón y las zapatillas y, además, se le habría levantado la polera frente a sus compañeros. Al segundo estudiante se le habría solicitado quitarse pantalones, polerón, polera y zapatillas, para posteriormente realizar sentadillas frente a sus compañeros, funcionarios policiales y funcionarias del establecimiento presentes en ese momento.


Como Centro de Estudiantes, condenamos tanto la exposición de los estudiantes como cualquier actuación previa que haya contribuido a que fueran individualizados y sometidos a este procedimiento sin que existiera una investigación que determinara su responsabilidad.


Queremos ser claros: la pérdida o eventual hurto de un objeto debe ser investigado y, si corresponde, denunciado ante las autoridades competentes. Sin embargo, la responsabilidad de un estudiante no puede darse por establecida simplemente por una sospecha. Todo estudiante tiene derecho a ser tratado con respeto y a que se respete su dignidad mientras los hechos son investigados.


La legislación chilena protege la integridad fisica y psíquica, la vida privada y la honra de las personas. Estos derechos tienen especial relevancia cuando se trata de niños, niñas y adolescentes.La Ley N° 21.430, sobre Garantías y Protección Integral de los Derechos de la Niñez y Adolescencia, establece la protección frente a injerencias arbitrarias en la vida privada y reconoce el derecho de niños, niñas yadolescentes a ser escuchados en los asuntos que les afectan. Estos principios también están reconocidos por la Convención sobre los Derechos del Niño.


Por lo tanto, consideramos necesario que se investigue no solamente el procedimiento realizado posteriormente, sino también la forma en que se originó esta situación, incluyendo la decisión de individualizar a determinados estudiantes como sospechosos y solicitar la intervención policial.


Como representantes estudiantiles, solicitamos:


Que se investigue formalmente todo lo ocurrido, desde el momento en que se informó la pérdida del celular hasta el procedimiento realizado posteriormente.


Que se determine qué antecedentes existían para señalar especificamente a determinados estudiantes como sospechosos.


Que se revise si la actuación de la docente y de los demás adultos presentes se ajustó a sus deberes y a los protocolos del establecimiento.


Que se determine si el procedimiento policial se realizó conforme a la legislación vigente.Que se resguarde la dignidad, integridad fisica y psíquica, honra y privacidad de los estudiantesinvolucrados.


Que los estudiantes afectados sean escuchados y puedan entregar su versión de los hechos.


Que se adopten medidas para evitar que una situación …

author: David Bacon
title: Union-Busters Are Using ICE to Intimidate California Wine Industry Workers
content:
California’s wine industry runs on immigrant exploitation. Now migrant workers are unionizing.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

In late July, Raul Calvo, a well-known California union-buster, called workers at the Rodney Strong Vineyards into a meeting. Salvador Ramirez, who’d labored among big wine tanks for 12 years, says he was shocked by what he heard. “He said he was just going to give us the information that he got in an email three days ago, that ICE [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] was here outside,” Ramirez remembers, noting that Calvo told workers the vineyard was technically in a border zone due to its proximity to the ocean.

Ramirez says workers were very upset — not just by Calvo’s implied threat, but because the company’s attitude had changed drastically. Last October, when there were rumors that ICE agents planned a wave of raids in the San Francisco Bay Area like those underway in Los Angeles, the company had called everyone into a meeting. Ramirez recalled, “‘You’re our workers,’ they told us. ‘We have to support you and we’re not going to allow them to come in [without a judge’s warrant]. We’re going to take care of each other.’“

Calvo did not respond to Truthout’s request for comment.

In the months afterwards, however, workers began talking with each other. They then reached out to North Bay Jobs with Justice (JwJ), a coalition of community organizations and unions in Sonoma and Napa Counties with a long history of fighting for workers’ rights. North Bay JwJ helped them organize a workplace committee, and put them in touch with Teamsters Local 665, a union with representatives on the organization’s board.

Ramirez and 31 of the winery’s 50 workers signed a petition asking that the company agree to a card check process for recognizing the union they’d formed, and for a “fair process to exercise our right to organize and form a union without threats and intimidation.” At the beginning of June, they took it to management. Rafael Malfavon, whom the workers call “Junior,” presented it and asked the company to accept their decision. Community leaders — including Chris Herrod, the mayor of Healdsburg — went along to support them.

The company’s response was to hire a local union-buster, Jesse Rojas, who held two meetings with workers. Then Calvo, Rojas’s boss, showed up. When he challenged Calvo in a meeting over misstatements about unions, Malfavon says he was ridiculed. “That just proved to us that the company won’t listen to what workers are saying and what we’re asking for, and hired this dude who calls me a liar,” he said.

Workers formed a delegation and went to Becky Oseguera, the company’s human relations director. According to Ramirez, “One of us said the company had brought in these people and they were trying to intimidate us with the migra, and that wasn’t right. I said, ‘We believe this is a very serious line that’s been crossed.’ She told us, ‘Don’t you see that I’m very busy, with all this stuff that you’re doing?’”

Ramirez and his co-workers started organizing in part because the company was terminating longtime workers. “They started having meetings with us,” Malfavon recalled, “saying they had to cut their budget. No one would get bonuses like before. We noticed that we weren’t getting raises while we had to do extra work, and they wouldn’t hire people to help. But the executives were getting promotions.”

One fired worker was Belen Flores, who had banged her knee at work and was then let go by the company, citing a genetic vision problem as a pretext. “I could always do my job to the last day,” Flores said. “I never got even a warning.”

Ramirez was incensed. “She’d been working here for nine years, and they fired her just like that,” he said. “There were rumors that there are five more people on the list after Belen. I could see the future that awaits us.”

Malfavon said that when his brother was terminated, he asked the company for some explanation. “They didn’t want to answer any of my questions. I had no words. I literally sat in the corner and started crying. I felt so powerless.”

The terminations came on top of increasing economic pressure. Despite working at Rodney Strong while also holding another full-time job, Malfavon is still living at home with his parents. Two-thirds of the people working in the winery have second jobs, he says. Malfavon is …

author: Acratosaurio rex
title: Durruti como símbolo, y el mito de Durruti
content:
Aquí Durruti, antes de comerse crudo a un bebé


Hablábamos en el artículo anterior de mitos y de símbolos

. ¿Cuál es el símbolo por excelencia de nuestra época, dentro del ámbito anarquista del Reino? Pues Durruti.


Durruti es nuestro símbolo más potente. Los anarquistas sabemos que nos han dicho muchas veces que Durruti era

uno de tantos

, por la cosa de que no queremos tener líderes y todo eso del culto al líder. Además, era un tío yo diría más bien feo, no lo pondría en un póster en mi dormitorio, por los sustos que me daría cuando despertase de la borrachera del sábado. No es como que te diría yo, el Che Guevara con esa barbita y esa mirada soñadora de gilipollas…


Pero por lo que sea, por no tener los anarquistas un buen servicio de propaganda, nos detenemos en Durruti, y en lo  que dijo Durruti en el momento culminante de nuestro querido mito revolucionario: que

 llevamos un mundo nuevo en nuestros corazones

.


Esa frase dicha por Durruti, unida al

no nos asustan las ruinas, vamos a heredar la Tierra

 y que los trabajadores somos capaces de construir ese nuevo mundo, ha sido traducida a cientos de idiomas del planeta. Condensa, resume, emociona, fundamenta. Es poética. Es inspiradora. Es nuestra. Esa es la fuerza del símbolo. No solo es una frase que conmociona al anarquista, si no que fue dicha por uno de los protagonistas de nuestra epopeya, en el momento tremendo en que miles de trabajadores libertarios se batían a muerte contra fuerzas superiores. Renunciaban a todo (o sea: incluso a sus vidas), menos a la victoria (o sea: el mundo nuevo). Con esa frase,

ellos son nosotros, y nosotros somos ellos.


Pero, ay, vienen los destructores de nuestros símbolos. Los historiadores que dicn que hacen ciencia y

muestran hechos

. Es mentira. En serio. La historia no es lo que pasó, si no el relato de lo que pasó, y que conviene al momento presente y al propio historiador (1). Hay historiadores (2) que afirman que esa frase no es más que una construcción literaria periodística, y que nunca fue dicha por Durruti, si no por el periodista Van Paassen, un tipo que era un cristiano metodista partidario del sionismo, que era un trolero según la prensa de derechas, ya que había denunciado a los nazis, augurando el genocidio en los años treinta.


Ese era el periodista que entrevistó a Durruti y que publicó esas frases en el Star de Toronto. Si eso queda establecido de esa manera, el símbolo

pierde parte de su fuerza

. No se invalida el símbolo, pero se debilita. De hecho hay otras entrevistas hechas a Durruti, la de Kolstov por ejemplo nos lo muestra como un personaje histriónico, algo histérico y autoritario. Iliá Ehrenburg lo presenta como un bolchevique dispuesto a renunciar al anarquismo. Otros lo presentan como un asesino subnormal que iba pegando tiros. ¿Con qué nos quedamos?


Porque vamos a ver, en una época en que no se grababan las entrevistas, si no que se tomaban notas por taquigrafía, y luego el periodista en su habitación redactaba la noticia, y la enviaba a su periódico… Evidentemente todos hacían algo de literatura.

Hay humo, veo fuego, ¡hostias putas, me ha rozado la bala!

Por ahí van los tiros. De las entrevistas de Kolstov y Ehrenburg, se poseen fotografías. De la de nuestro cristiano metodista/sionista Van Paassen no hay registro gráfico. No hay foto, ni pasaporte con visa, por ejemplo. Así que el historiador concluye, que nunca hubo entrevista, y que Van Paasen nunca habló con Durruti.


Vale. Pues eso es un indicio de que el historiador, serio, científico, de la academia, debería investigar más. Las contradicciones del periodista, las acusaciones de otros periodistas católicos, o incluso las dudas sobre el itinerario de Van Paassen,

no demuestran por sí mismas que nunca hablara con Durruti

. Demuestran que existen razones para estudiar cómo obtuvo la información, o dónde estaba en esas fechas. Lo cual es muy aburrido, porque el historiador tiene que ir a los archivos, libros de registro de hoteles y pensiones, búsqueda de facturas, recibos de viaje… Todo muy laborioso y frustrante, pero es lo que hay cuando se quiere demostrar algo más allá de toda duda. Porque, en fin, pudo pasar sin pasaporte, en avión, que es lo que él dijo. Y además: uno de los nuestros, Abel Paz, asegura que sí que hubo encuentro, que habló con testigos, que sí hubo entrevista.


¿A quién creemos? (3) Otro día sigo con lo de los símbolos y mitos, si eso.


———————-


Y eso me lleva a hablar de la Historia, y a …

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israel Finally Admits Responsibility for Killing Five-Year-Old Hind Rajab
content:
The Israeli military has finally admitted to opening fire on the car carrying Hind Rajab.


Israel has long denied that any troops were present in the Tel-al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City where the five-year-old and her family were killed on 29 January 2024.


But on Wednesday, the Israeli military announced that it would open a criminal investigation into both Rajab’s death and a separate incident in March 2025, in which Israeli troops killed 15 Palestinian medics and buried them in a mass grave.


Investigations by the Washington Post, Sky News and Forensic Architecture had already concluded that Rajab and six family members were fleeing Gaza when Israeli forces opened fire on their car. Israeli soldiers then shelled the ambulance dispatched to rescue Rajab, killing two medics.


The bodies of Rajab, her family and two Palestinian Red Cross paramedics were not recovered until 10 February 2023, when Israeli forces left the area. 


Rajab’s killing became one of the most reported crimes in the early months of the genocide in Gaza, after a recording of Rajab’s three-hour phone call to Palestinian paramedics was broadcast on global news networks. 


The story of Rajab’s death was later made into an Oscar-nominated film, The Voice of Hind Rajab, and cited in a

UN commission of inquiry accusing Israel of war crimes. 


The Hind Rajab Foundation, founded in 2024 to hold Israel accountable for war crimes in Gaza, said the Israeli investigation “should not be mistaken for a genuine step toward justice”.


“We do not trust the Israeli justice system, not out of an ideological position, but because of the track record,” said its director, Dyab Abou Jahjah. 


Only a “tiny percentage” of Israeli criminal investigations into the killing of Palestinians have produced convictions in the last decades, according to Dan Owen, a researcher at Israeli rights organisation Yesh Din.

author: Unknown
title: Iranian forces arrest three Kurdish men amid new crackdown
content:
As a new wave of arrests of Kurdish citizens continues, security forces have arrested three Kurdish men – Zaher Ghorbani, Shakhawan Khavari, and Farzin Khediripour – in Miandoab, Marivan, and Mahabad.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Ministry of Intelligence forces raided Ghorbani’s family home in the village of Gavmish Goli in Miandoab County, West Azerbaijan Province, on 14 August, intending to arrest him.


As he was not there, the forces arrested his father, Loghman Ghorbani, and said he would not be released until his son reported to the Intelligence Ministry office in Miandoab.


Ghorbani reported to the office on 16 August and was arrested. His father was reportedly released afterwards.


On 17 August, security forces arrested Khavari at his family home in the village of Ney in Marivan County, Kurdistan Province.


The following day, Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested Khediripour at his workplace in Mahabad, West Azerbaijan Province.


The three men were arrested without warrants. At the time of writing, no information was available regarding the reasons for their arrests or the charges brought against them.


Despite repeated enquiries by their families about their status, the security and judicial authorities have continued to refuse to respond or provide any information.


According to figures compiled by KHRN, Ministry of Intelligence forces and the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) have arrested at least 29 Kurdish citizens in Bukan, Mahabad, Oshnavieh, Orumiyeh, Marivan, Sanandaj, Kamyaran and Piranshahr since 23 July.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Familias endeudadas, centrales sindicales y movimientos sociales marchan hoy al Ministerio de Economía
content:
Las centrales sindicales (CGT, ambas CTA), la UTEP y colectivos de familias damnificadas marchan hoy al Ministerio de Economía para protestar contra el fuerte crecimiento del sobreendeudamiento familiar y la morosidad récord en Argentina. La convocatoria es desde las 14hs en las esquinas de Paseo Colón e Independencia, y Paseo Colón y Estados Unidos (CABA). Las columnas avanzarán hacia el Palacio de Hacienda, ubicado en Hipólito Yrigoyen 250.


Según datos del Banco Central, la morosidad en hogares escaló al 12,7% en junio de 2026, afectando a cerca de 5,8 millones de personas con atrasos graves o créditos impagos. Las organizaciones denuncian que la licuación de ingresos obligó a las familias a financiarse mediante tarjetas, fintechs y prestamistas informales para cubrir costos básicos como alimentos, medicamentos, alquileres y servicios públicos.


Endeudados Organizados, demandan una “emergencia crediticia” y un programa público de desendeudamiento. Rechazan además la postura oficial del Gobierno de Javier Milei y el ministro Luis Caputo, quienes catalogaron la situación como “un tema entre privados”.


En conferencia de prensa, el Secretario General de la Cta Autónoma Hugo Godoy, describió la situación actual: “340.000 puestos de trabajo formales que se han destruido y cerca de 30.000 empresas que se siguen cerrando. Pero a esto se viene agregando ya no solamente el endeudamiento del país de futuras generaciones para pagar la deuda externa, sino también esta situación en que la caída del consumo y la caída de los ingresos de los trabajadores y trabajadoras obliga al endeudamiento”.


Además, responsabilizó al gobierno nacional por esto: “El gobierno se sigue haciendo el distraído, dice que es un problema de privados o el presidente encima dice que nadie les puso una pistola en la cabeza” y denunció que “la política de Milei es criminal, no solamente nos pone una pistola en la cabeza a los trabajadores y trabajadoras, sino que además nos mata, como mata a los jubilados y las jubiladas y como mata a los trabajadores y trabajadoras dejando a las familias sin sus puestos de trabajo”.


Por su parte, la Secretaria General Adjunta de la Unión de Trabajadoras y Trabajadores de la Economía Popular, aseveró: “Nosotras somos las compañeras, las cuidadoras comunitarias, las que venimos también compartiendo una pregunta a toda la sociedad y también a este gobierno” y se preguntó: “¿Quién cuida a las que nos endeudamos para sostener la vida de nuestras comunidades en los barrios populares? ¿Quién nos cuida a las que nos endeudamos para comprar comida? ¿Quién nos cuida cuando nos endeudamos para pedir un préstamo para comprar el medicamento para nuestros hijos?”.


Por último, el Co-Secretario General Confederación General del Trabajo y Secretario Regional de Camioneros Tres de Febrero y San Martín, aseguró que “cuando la deuda es para poder comer, es un problema social, y es un problema de la economía y un problema de gobierno” y enfatizó: “Quiere decir que acá hay dos culpables y dos responsables: el presidente y el ministro de Economía, quienes llevan una política totalmente de ajuste, regresiva, y totalmente pisando los salarios de los trabajadores, rompiendo totalmente el consumo, y lo peor de todo, rompiendo todo el sistema productivo”.

author: Tom Midlane
title: Jury Refuses to Convict Palestine Action Activists
content:
A jury has refused to convict seven Palestine Action activists in connection with a raid on an Israeli arms factory in South Gloucestershire.


The defendants were members of the Filton 25 who faced charges of criminal damage and violent disorder over the infiltration of Elbit Systems in Filton, near Bristol, in August 2024. 


Jurors deliberated for more than 37 hours but were unable to reach verdicts for seven of the eight defendants: Madeleine Norman, Hannah Davidson, Teuta Hoxha, Ola Aleksandra Herbich, Ian Sanders, William Plastow and Yulia Brigadirova. They may now face a retrial.


The eighth defendant, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was found guilty of criminal damage.


During the case, which opened at the Old Bailey on 22 June, Plastow was cleared of violent disorder after the judge concluded that the prosecution had not produced enough evidence. 


None of the eight defendants were on the premises of the Elbit factory at the time of the break-in. Police produced so little evidence against Brigadirova that her barrister told the court “she should be called the invisible coordinator,” reported

Declassified UK

.


Six of the Filton 25 activists were cleared of aggravated burglary charges in February following a trial at Woolwich Crown Court. Following that trial, aggravated burglary charges against 18 other defendants were dropped.


Elbit Systems is Israel’s largest weapons firm. It produces 85% of the military drone fleet used to massacre Palestinians in Gaza.


In response to the verdicts, the Filton 25 Defence Committee said the charges were an attempt by the state “to justify their disproportionate proscription of the group.”


The committee stated: “Today’s verdict comes after each of the defendants already spent up to 18 months in prison without convictions. They were all held on remand as ‘terrorist prisoners’ for well beyond the pre-trial custody time limit of six months.”


An additional trial would be “a huge waste of resources” and “a cynical attempt to manipulate the court process in order to convict the defendants”, it added.


“Each one of those drones could have massacred hundreds of Palestinians. Yet for destroying them and undoubtedly saving lives, four Palestine Action activists were sentenced as terrorists, despite only being convicted of criminal damage.”

author: Gustavo Faleiros
title: A comida está cara? Lamento informar, pode piorar
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Vou começar pedindo licença à minha colega colunista aqui da

Pública

, a

Clara Saliba

, pois vou me intrometer no campo dela, a economia. Não estudei economia, mas sempre me interessei por esta relação entre o desenvolvimento econômico e a natureza. Tive a sorte de começar minha carreira no jornalismo cobrindo macroeconomia. Foi a partir do olhar econômico que eu me liguei nas questões ambientais.


Nos dias de hoje, há um indicador que reflete como poucos essa relação entre a demanda por recursos naturais e o nosso cotidiano: a inflação.


Tivemos na semana passada uma notícia boa de que, no mês de julho,

o Índice de Preços ao Consumidor, o IPCA

, indicador oficial da taxa de inflação do Brasil, ficou abaixo do esperado – 4,4% no acumulado de 12 meses. Ou seja, um percentual menor do que o teto da meta anual de 4,5%. A notícia foi ainda melhor pois a queda no índice se deve principalmente à deflação de 0,67% nos alimentos. Uma redução no custo da alimentação não ocorria desde julho de 2022.


Entretanto, essa melhora não se reflete na percepção das pessoas. Quando falamos de inflação, um indicador exato, é notável como prevalecem os sentimentos. “O consumidor sentiu no bolso”, é um dos clichês favoritos. Ou ainda: “O supermercado está uma fortuna” e “não dá para comer fora toda hora.”


Essas percepções e sentimentos não são esotéricos ou descolados da realidade. Muito pelo contrário!

A nossa preocupação com o custo da comida está baseada em um problema estrutural: por conta das guerras e dos eventos climáticos extremos, o preço dos alimentos tem subido de forma constante.

 Isso sem falar nos choques repentinos. Em abril deste ano, por exemplo, o feijão deu um salto de 20%.


Um

estudo da Fundação Getúlio Vargas

 mostrou que o preço dos alimentos, nos últimos dez anos, aumentou mais do que a taxa média de inflação. Enquanto na última década a alta acumulada no IPCA foi de 44%, o indicador para Alimentos e Bebidas subiu 64%.


“Não é uma sensação, é uma constatação. Os preços realmente estão muito mais altos. Você tem 20 pontos percentuais de alta a mais para alimentos, e isso faz uma grande diferença, porque os salários são corrigidos pelo IPCA”, disse o economista André Braz, coordenador dos Índices de Preços do FGV IBRE, em

entrevista ao Jornal Nacional,


“Se o seu salário dos últimos seis anos foi corrigido em média em torno de 45%, mas a sua despesa de supermercado subiu 65%, então não são quedas pontuais [no valor do alimento] que vão fazer esse aumento todo dissipar.”


A inflação de alimentos passou a ser um problema na maioria dos países. Isso começou na pandemia devido às disrupções nas cadeias globais de fornecimento. Mas a alta se mostrou persistente e tomou um rumo ainda mais grave em 2022, quando começou o conflito entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia, que afetou tanto o mercado de fertilizantes como o de grãos. Foi exatamente em março daquele ano, um mês após o início da guerra, que o preço da soja bateu o recorde histórico – R$ 200 por saca.


Desde então, a soja permanece com valor acima de sua média histórica. A soja mais cara certamente alegra o setor agroexportador, mas também influencia no preço da proteína animal por aqui, em especial do frango. Para ligar os pontos com a questão ambiental, temos visto que a expansão da soja na Amazônia e no Matopiba (região agrícola no Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia) retomou o fôlego a ponto de termos grandes atores da cadeia atacando o acordo que garantia a produção apenas em áreas livres do desmatamento – a chamada moratória da soja.


A soja talvez possa parecer um mercado distante do nosso dia-a-dia, mas o preço do café certamente ficou na cabeça de todo mundo. No ano passado, em fevereiro, o café atingiu seu recorde histórico. Como podemos ver no gráfico abaixo, o preço do grão já vinha subindo desde 2020, ano da pandemia, e só no comecinho deste ano ele começou a dar uma aliviada. Mas aí, outro choque no preço dos alimentos chegou com a guerra dos Estados Unidos e Israel contra o Irã. O conflito no Estreito de Ormuz causou um salto nas cotações do petróleo e, por consequência, no custo dos combustíveis. Vejam, o café já começou a subir de novo!


Se por um lado muitas explicações para a alta nos alimentos se concentram nas guerras, por outro o fator climático …

author: Unknown
title: Women in Istanbul protest against sexual violence in Turkish deportation centers
content:
Following allegations of torture made by German activist Paula Maier, women in Istanbul protested against sexual violence in Turkish deportation centers, police custody and prisons. The Women Strong Together Alliance (Kadınlar Birlikte Güçlü) stated that the violence described by Maier was not an isolated incident, but part of a state practice used particularly against migrant women and politically active women.


During the protest at Tünel Square, participants carried a banner reading, “End sexual torture against women in deportation centers and police custody.” They chanted slogans including, “We will not remain silent, we are not afraid, we will not obey,” “End harassment and rape in police custody—the male-dominated state will be held accountable,” and “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom].


The protest was prompted by the testimony of Paula Maier. The German activist and member of the Caravan for the Defense of Humanity had traveled to Turkey in January this year to take part in international solidarity work with the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria, which at the time was under attack by the Syrian transitional government. Following her arrest, she was held in a deportation center. After returning to Germany, she publicly stated that she had been subjected to sexual violence and torture there by a male staff member.


“Deportation centers have become torture centers”


Simay Ada Kart, who read out the statement on behalf of the women’s alliance, placed the case in a broader context. She said that since their establishment, Turkey’s deportation centers had developed into places where policies targeting refugees and women intersect with racism and torture. Migrants are subjected to various forms of pressure intended to force them to leave the country or submit to deportation, she noted.


According to the alliance, sexual violence committed by state officials should not be regarded as a series of isolated abuses. The group also recalled accounts of sexual violence during detention made public by Anna, a participant in the Sumud Flotilla in solidarity with Palestine, and Alma of the Caravan for the Defense of Humanity.


“In prisons, police stations and deportation centers, strip searches, sexual harassment and sexual violence have virtually become routine practices aimed at breaking the will of women who resist and struggle, and at punishing them,” Kart said.


“Strip searches are not a procedure but torture”


Women Are Strong Together pointed to reports of abuse at various locations within Turkey’s detention and policing system—from the Istanbul Police Department on Vatan Street and Bakırköy Women’s Prison to police stations and deportation centers. Kart said that the control of and violence against women’s bodies were intended to intimidate women and deter them from political and social engagement.


Strip searches, she said, should therefore not be downplayed as an administrative “procedure”: “Strip searches are torture.”


The alliance also echoed Maier’s call not to allow the violence women have experienced to silence them. “It is the responsibility of all of us to turn these experiences into a story of resistance,” the activist had said. The organization announced that it would continue to strengthen international solidarity among women.


Who will hold those responsible accountable?


At the end of the protest, the alliance addressed a series of specific questions to the Turkish authorities and government: “Will the torture centers referred to as deportation centers be shut down? Will those responsible for harassing and raping women in prisons and police stations, as well as the state officials who turn a blind eye to such acts, be held accountable? Will acts of sexual violence in police custody and prisons be effectively investigated?”


The protest concluded with participants chanting slogans.

author: David Swanson
title: Commemorating Hiroshima and Nagasaki Bombings in Scotland
content:
By North East Scotland CND – Campaigning for Peace, an affiliate of WBW, August 20,2026


“Turning nuclear remembrance into positive change”


On 8 August we held our annual gathering to remember those who died in the Hiroshima and Nagasaki nuclear bombings. And as the event was held outside Marischal College, central Aberdeen, we engaged with local passersby and made some new recruits for our cause!


Guest speaker Yu Aoki, who was born in Hiroshima but lives in Aberdeen, talked about the horror of the atomic bombings and the urgency of the current world situation. We heard inspiring and rousing music from Melting Pot, Bryan Duncan, and JC Bigfoot as well as poems and song lyrics read by local CND Activists.


Looking forward, Jonathan Russell, our Chair, spoke about our ongoing Welfare not Warfare campaign.


Here are some key highlights from Jonathan’s speech:


These solemn anniversaries can never be passive history. They are an urgent, annual

alarm bell as governments across the world are being urged to turn themselves into the

largest, most dangerous warfare states in history.


(On 5 March the Financial Times featured an article declaring): “Europe must trim 

its welfare state to build a warfare state.” That is what Labour chancellor John Healey 

wants us to believe, too. It is a dangerous lie.


A lie leading to growing inequality, deepening poverty, and an arms race which—like all

arms races in history—can lead only to war involving levels of devastation which will 

make Hiroshima and Nagasaki look primitive in their death dealing consequences.


This is why we must turn sorrowful remembrance into active resistance and the 

building of positive alternatives. That is, ones which resist the predatory  arms lobby, and

recognise that true human and national security is built on foundations of social security,

solidarity and democratic accountability.

title: Guerrillas celebrate 42nd anniversary of the August 15 Offensive
content:
Kurdish guerrillas marked the 42nd anniversary of the August 15 Offensive in several regions of the Medya Defense Zones in southern Kurdistan (northern Iraq). Videos of the events show gatherings attended by hundreds of members of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) and the Free Women’s Troops (YJA-Star).


August 15 marks the beginning of the PKK’s armed struggle against the Turkish state in 1984 and is regarded as a historic turning point within the Kurdish freedom movement.


This year’s events focused in particular on the peace and  democratic society process initiated by PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan.


Commanders and members of the HPG and YJA-Star reaffirmed their determination to participate in the process initiated by Öcalan. At the same time, they described the physical freedom of the Kurdish leader as an indispensable prerequisite for the process to move forward.
